policy: Public-source analytical research. Reported facts, management statements, and analyst judgments retain their own definitions and limitations. Reading a source entry does not mean every page, minute, or statement was reviewed.

snapshots.splitBasis: Contemporaneous original filing basis; do not compare with adjusted prices without checking splits.
snapshots.shareBasis: Contemporaneous original filing basis
snapshots.cashDefinition: Cash and cash equivalents only. Marketable securities separately disclosed; add only after assessing operating needs/restrictions.
snapshots.debtDefinition: Term debt carrying value plus commercial paper; excludes leases.
snapshots.vintage: Exact original annual filing accession; current annual reference, not live or latest quarterly data.
interpretationNotes: Annual snapshot can be stale; quarterly changes and subsequent events not captured.
Review debt completeness and securities before computing equity bridge.

existing-company-base-cases.name: Apple Inc.
existing-company-base-cases.summary: A mature hardware franchise with recurring services: moderate expansion, durable margins and relatively light incremental capital needs.

rationale.growth: 8% starts above FY2025 growth of 6.4% but below the latest 16% quarter. Services and replacement demand support growth; the installed base and hardware maturity argue for an immediate fade rather than extrapolating one strong quarter.
rationale.targetMargin: 32% is close to FY2025 operating margin and below the current 33.2% TTM. Services mix offsets hardware competition; the latest tariff-refund benefit is not assumed permanent.
rationale.tax: 20% is a normalized blended cash-tax judgment above FY2025 accounting tax of 15.6%; one-off tax charges, geographic mix and minimum-tax changes make any single reported rate a weak long-run anchor.
rationale.salesCapital: 3.0x requires about $0.33 of net reinvestment for each extra $1 of revenue. Outsourced manufacturing and services justify lighter capital needs; this is not the inflated book return created by buybacks or a claim that working capital is free.
rationale.terminalROIC: 20% retains a brand/ecosystem advantage but materially reduces returns on new capital from the explicit-period margin/capital combination.
rationale.wacc: 9.0% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.0, modest 10% target debt and a 0.7-point debt spread reflect broad cash generation, balanced against product concentration and supply-chain exposure.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
rationale.otherClaims: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not evidence that no additional claims exist. Long-dated securities, leases and employee awards need a consistent enterprise-to-common-equity reconciliation; zero additional assets does not mean the securities are worthless.
rationale.otherAssets: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not a statement that all non-operating assets are absent or worthless. Review assets not already included in snapshot cash and avoid double counting.

reportedAnchors.classification: reported or directly derived from reported current financials
reported results and explicitly labeled management outlook; not the base-case forecast
reportedAnchors.text: Fiscal Q3 2026 revenue was $109.4bn, up 16%; reported gross margin included approximately two percentage points of favorable tariff refunds.

waccBuild.classification: analyst model estimate; only riskFreeUSD is an observed input
waccBuild.equityRiskPremiumClassification: chosen long-run assumption; January reference is 4.23%, not a current estimate
waccBuild.formula: Ke = Rf + assumed beta × chosen ERP + extra equity risk; WACC = Ke × (1 − debt weight) + assumed Kd × (1 − tax) × debt weight
waccBuild.limits: Not a live beta regression, bond yield, market-value capital structure or country-default estimate. Extra equity allowances can overlap with operating downside; stress both rather than treating precision as evidence.

bridgePolicy.note: Long-dated securities, leases and employee awards need a consistent enterprise-to-common-equity reconciliation; zero additional assets does not mean the securities are worthless.

modelLimits: Consolidated linear growth does not separately forecast hardware units, prices or services.
uncertainties: iPhone replacement cycles, China demand, tariffs and memory/input costs
Services regulation and the cost of supporting AI features

modelSuitability.note: An internally checked conditional model, not proof that business assumptions will be realized.

economicChecks.classification: computed consequences of assumptions; not reported outcomes or probabilities
economicChecks.note: Operating math only. No cash/debt/claims/share bridge is asserted; hard gates remain. Terminal share above 100% means negative explicit-period present value, not a probability.

companies.dossierMarkdown:
# Apple: forecast and valuation dossier
As of **17 October 2026**. Latest reported financial period: **27 June 2026**; September-quarter actuals are not yet available in the reviewed source set. Dollar amounts below are USD. This is conditional valuation research, not a recommendation to trade.

## Bottom line
The evidence supports a durable, modest-growth ecosystem, but does not support extending the latest 16–17% revenue growth or 50.1% gross margin indefinitely. Keep a three-year explicit growth phase before fading to maturity. A base 9%/8%/7% revenue path, first-year 31% operating margin and eventual 32% margin is more informative than immediately fading a single starting rate. Apple's June gross-margin refund benefit and September memory-cost pressure pull near-term margin in opposite directions.

The existing app's 8% growth, 32% target margin, 3x sales/capital, 20% tax and 9% WACC are broadly defensible mature/base judgments. The important changes are **timing, margin normalization and the equity bridge**. The existing zero additional assets/claims fields are unreviewed placeholders. June noncurrent securities alone are $84.118bn outside snapshot cash. No app changes were made.

## Reported operating evidence
Fiscal revenue was $383.285bn in 2023, $391.035bn in 2024 and $416.161bn in 2025. Operating income increased from $114.301bn to $123.216bn to $133.050bn. That is a strong margin record but a much slower revenue record than the latest product cycle. FY2025 operating margin was 31.97%. The last three fiscal quarters produced revenue of $143.756bn, $111.184bn and $109.417bn; trailing-year revenue is $466.823bn and EBIT $154.859bn, a 33.17% margin. Original filing contexts and quarterly calculations are retained in evidence-AAPL.html#facts and evidence-AAPL.html#quarterly-financials. [FY2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019325000079/aapl-20250927.htm), [June 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019326000020/aapl-20260627.htm).

June-quarter iPhone revenue was $54.252bn, Mac $10.352bn, iPad $6.191bn, wearablesevidence-AAPL.html#sources $7.883bn and Services $30.739bn. Services supplied 28.1% of revenue and 42.4% of gross profit, with a 75.6% gross margin. It is a material profit engine, but not the whole company. Greater China contributed $18.816bn of quarterly sales; geographic and product concentration remain meaningful. The installed base exceeded 2.5bn active devices in December2025; installed devices are neither unique paying customers nor a disclosed Services monetization denominator. [June financial statements](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/pdfs/fy2026q3/FY26_Q3_Consolidated_Financial_Statements.pdf), [January results](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/01/apple-reports-first-quarter-results/).

Reported June gross margin of 50.1% includes approximately two percentage points of tariff refunds. Subtracting that approximate amount gives 48.1% underlying quarterly GM and approximately 32.70% trailing operating margin, not an issuer-reported adjusted measure. The September guide is 47–48% GM including roughly one point of refunds, or 46–47% underlying. Higher memory costs and exhaustion of favorable inventory costs explain the prospective compression. A services-mix benefit cannot simply cancel an unmodeled hardware-cost shock. [July release](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/07/apple-reports-third-quarter-results/), [July management call transcript, secondary host](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/aapl/transcripts/658553-q3-2026/).

## Management outlook and its track record
July30 outlook for September: total revenue growth 9–11%, iPhone mid-teens, Services near the June growth pace allowing for FX, operating expense $19.1–19.4bn and tax about16.5%. FX was expected to worsen sequentially by about2.5 percentage points, and supply constraints to increase. This is one-quarter conditional outlook, not a formal annual or multiyear CAGR commitment. No December-quarter actual or management forecast is invented.

The 12-quarter history, FY2023Q4–FY2026Q3, preserves original dated outlooks and matching original financial periods. Numeric gross-margin outcomes: **seven within, five above, zero below**; mean reported midpoint error +0.56 percentage points. June2026's reported beat largely disappears after the approximate refund adjustment. Only the latest three completed quarters have explicit numeric revenue-growth ranges in this sample: actual growth 15.65% versus10–12%, 16.60% versus13–16%, and16.36% versus14–17%. Earlier descriptions such as low-to-mid-single digits are not assigned invented endpoints. The March2024 outlook also excluded roughly$5bn of prior-year catch-up sales from its comparison; it must not be scored against an unadjusted flat-revenue forecast.

Readable issuer-hosted historical transcripts were not verified. Quartr transcripts on Stock Analysis supply management wording; SEC filings and issuer releases supply actuals. This weakens confidence in nuances, and is explicitly recorded rather than presenting secondary material as issuer-hosted. Historical webcast replays were advertised for approximately two weeks. Detailed errors, definitions and gaps are in evidence-AAPL.html#guidance. No numerical management-credibility adjustment is applied.

Good reported outcomes do not mean accurate demand planning. In July, management acknowledged underestimating iPhone/Mac demand and resulting supply limits. April30 also retired the formal net-cash-neutral target; future buybacks should not be forced to follow an obsolete cash objective. [April call](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/aapl/transcripts/548666-q2-2026/).

## Reinvestment, cash conversion and dilution
Trailing CFO was $146.724bn and cash capex $10.041bn. Their difference, $136.683bn, is not unlevered owner cash flow: CFO includes SBC addbacks and volatile working capital. R&D reached $42.901bn TTM and SBC $13.706bn. If R&D is capitalized analytically, both NOPAT and invested capital must be restated; do not add an asset without changing earnings/reinvestment.

Nine-month cash capex $6.799bn was below D&A $9.973bn, but that does not imply zero economic reinvestment. Inventory rose from $5.718bn to $11.092bn; its cash-flow effect was -$5.461bn. Other assets used $16.266bn and payables $5.203bn, partly offset by receivable collections and other liabilities. The final $8.8bn deemed-repatriation tax payment is a separate nonrecurring cash-tax item. Outsourced manufacturing leaves Apple with $57bn of manufacturing purchase obligations, $56.2bn due within a year, plus other purchase obligations. Do not add overlapping obligation schedules or treat all supplier purchases as financing debt. [10-Q cash flow, notes and MD&A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019326000020/aapl-20260627.htm).

A 2.5–3x early incremental sales/capital ratio is a judgment that charges for inventory, ecosystem investment and supplier dependence despite low owned capex. Buybacks and expensed intangibles inflate book ROIC; they do not establish an infinite return on incremental economic capital. Base terminal ROIC is20%, falling to13% in the downside case.

Cash repurchases were $62.094bn over nine months, versus roughly$61.8bn program transaction cost; timing and definitions differ. Dividends used $11.778bn and equity-award tax withholding $6.462bn. Unrecognized compensation was $26.7bn over about2.7years. Retain SBC as an economic expense and reconcile future awards/shares or replacement repurchases; do not add back SBC and also assume dilution-free cash distributions.

## Leadership evidence
John Ternus became CEO on September1,2026, with Tim Cook becoming executive chairman. The completed financial/forecast sample is a Cook-era record, spanning CFO Maestri and Parekh. Ternus's prior hardware leadership is relevant but is not a multiyear CEO track record. [Issuer succession announcement](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/04/tim-cook-to-become-apple-executive-chairman-john-ternus-to-become-apple-ceo/).

Ternus's October TIME interview emphasizes integrated devices, software and personal context, while acknowledging memory constraints. The thesis is useful; it does not prove AI monetization. Apple confirmed Duo preorders beginning October16 and describes Siri AI as an English-language beta rollout. New-product revenue, contribution margin and retention have not been reported. evidence-AAPL.html#management distinguishes demonstrated demand, delivery, cost control and cash returns from these unproven outcomes. [Direct TIME interview](https://time.com/collection/best-inventions/2026/apple-iphone-duo/), [issuer product update](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/10/open-up-to-new-possibilities-with-iphone-duo/).

## Conditional forecast proposals
All rates below are analyst judgments. Annual periods run from the latest June trailing-year anchor; Apple's first modeled year is not identical to its September fiscal year. Growth fades linearly after the early phase. Capital efficiency fades over the last five years to match terminal ROIC, avoiding free terminal growth.

| Case | Early annual revenue growth | Early years / maturity | Mature EBIT margin | Tax | WACC | Terminal growth / ROIC | Maturity sales |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| base | 9%, 8%, 7% | 3 / 10 | 32% | 20% | 9% | 2.5% / 20% | $796.0bn |
| bull | 13%, 12%, 11%, 9%, 8% | 5 / 15 | 35% | 19% | 8.5% | 3% / 25% | $1,286.6bn |
| bear | 2%, 1%, 3% | 3 / 10 | 27.5% | 22% | 10.5% | 2% / 13% | $585.9bn |

Base early margins are31%/31.5%/32%; base early incremental sales/capital2.5x/2.5x/3x. The bull requires persistent premium upgrades and Services profit expansion, reaching$1.287tn sales at maturity. That is a conditional scale claim, not a market-size estimate. The bear allows low growth and27.5% mature EBIT margin. No scenario probabilities are assigned; all three are positive-FCFF in the simplified model, which does not exclude an actual cash shock.

WACC uses the coordinator-reverified October16 US10-year Treasury5.09%, chosen long-run ERP4.5%, assumed beta/capital weights/spreads and normalized tax. The January ERP reference4.23% is not a current October premium. Base beta1.0 and10% debt weight produce9.09% unrounded WACC, rounded to9%. These are not measured current betas or debt-market quotes.

## Enterprise-to-common-equity bridge and decision gates
June cash/equivalents $39.544bn plus current securities$22.855bn equals app snapshot cash$62.399bn. Noncurrent securities$84.118bn are not included there. Review availability and operating cash needs, then count them once. Exact debt components are current term$11.007bn plus noncurrent$71.340bn plus CP$1.997bn = **$84.344bn**. The note's rounded82.3bn term-debt figure is not the exact balance-sheet sum.

Cover shares are14.59418bn as of July17 versus14.608963bn at June27; weighted diluted historical shares are a different concept. Complete lease tables are last available in the reviewed FY2025 annual report: finance$1.230bn and operating$12.490bn. They must not be mislabeled June balances. A conditional Amazon/Globalstar transaction also contemplates redemption of Apple's interests in a special-purpose entity; no proceeds amount is assumed and no value is added before reconciliation. See evidence-AAPL.html#sources for the counterparty filing.

Do not publish a per-share value until leases, investments, taxes and outstanding awards are reconciled with forecast cash flows. Regulatory/distribution/search-economics changes, China competition, component supply, inventory mismatch and AI development/serving costs are core invalidators. Watch underlying GM after refunds, Services growth, inventory-to-sales, supply recovery and cash conversion. A credible review would revise the scenario inputs, not attach a generic management discount.

## Files and limitations
evidence-AAPL.html#facts retains original financial evidence; evidence-AAPL.html#sources dates and scopes sources; evidence-AAPL.html#guidance preserves the12-quarter comparisons; evidence-AAPL.html#judgment supplies annual schedules and mathematical scale checks; evidence-AAPL.html#management separates capabilities and tenure. Remaining gaps are current complete lease balances, a fully cleared common-equity bridge, product-level AI returns and readable primary Apple historical transcripts. No complete search of every interview or intraperiod revision is claimed.

implementationGates: No default otherClaims=0 or otherAssets=0 may be interpreted as verified absence.
Confirm current cash/debt/shares bridge and consistently classify leases before per-share publication.
Keep SBC as operating cost; reconcile issued shares/outstanding awards and any repurchase assumption without double counting.

analystJudgment.interpretation: WACC and terminal parameters are analyst estimates; strong guidance track records do not receive a mechanical credibility uplift.

rationale.growth: Three-year base 9/8/7% starts below recent16–17% growth and near September9–11% outlook. Services and >2.5bn active devices help; large hardware base, supply constraints and upgrade cyclicality argue against five years at16%. Bull requires durable premium upgrades, Services growth and new products; bear tests stalled hardware cycle.
rationale.margin: Current TTM33.17% contains an approximate47bp Q3 refund benefit. September underlying GM46–47% plus rising R&D supports a first-year31% EBIT margin rather than copying current quarterly highs. Recovery toward32% requires memory pressure easing and Services mix.
rationale.capital: Owned capex is light but inventory rose and R&D is expensed. Base2.5–3.0x incremental sales/capital charges meaningful investment instead of extrapolating negative net capex or permanent supplier financing.
rationale.tax: 20% normalized is above recent15–17% reported/quarter guidance, avoids one-time FY24 tax distortion and allows geographic/minimum-tax uncertainty.
rationale.terminal: 20% marginal ROIC preserves ecosystem advantage but fades far below near-term asset-light accounting returns. Ten-year base maturity,15-year bull and10-year bear are judgments, not product life forecasts.
rationale.bridge: Add84.118bn noncurrent securities only once if non-operating and available; exact June term debt+CP84.344bn. Annual lease figures stale; current awards/dilution still require policy. Net-cash-neutral target retired April30, so no forced buyback path.

invalidators: Two successive reported quarters materially below latest revenue outlook with weak Services or upgrade demand
Underlying gross margin below46% after refunds fade, without evidence of temporary component timing
Sustained Services growth below high-single digits or legal changes materially alter distribution/search economics
Inventory growth materially exceeds sales and later write-downs or channel discounting appear
R&D/AI serving costs rise without retention, revenue or pricing benefits
No supply recovery while premium-device demand or China competitiveness deteriorates

existing-company-base-cases.name: MICROSOFT CORPORATION
existing-company-base-cases.summary: Cloud and enterprise software sustain growth, while AI infrastructure reduces the capital efficiency of the historical software model.

rationale.growth: 18% begins near FY2026 reported growth. Azure and recurring enterprise subscriptions support the starting rate, which then fades to 2.5% as the revenue base expands.
rationale.targetMargin: 42% is below FY2026 operating margin of 46.8%. Recurring software remains profitable, but AI depreciation, inference costs and competition constrain permanent peak-margin extrapolation.
rationale.tax: 22% allows a higher normalized burden than FY2026 accounting tax of 19.4%; it does not extend discrete investment-related tax effects indefinitely.
rationale.salesCapital: 0.6x means $1.67 of incremental net capital per extra $1 of revenue. FY2026 cash capex was $115.9bn; AI capacity makes an old asset-light software ratio inappropriate. It remains a normalized net-reinvestment assumption, not gross capex guidance.
rationale.terminalROIC: 16% assumes a persistent distribution and switching-cost advantage while fading returns as cloud infrastructure becomes a larger part of the business.
rationale.wacc: 9.5% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.0, 5% target debt and a 0.5-point debt spread reflect diversified recurring revenue and modest financing risk, with AI-demand uncertainty still present.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
rationale.otherClaims: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not evidence that no additional claims exist. Finance-lease obligations and non-operating investments are material. Lease capitalization must be reconciled with operating profit and reinvestment, not deducted a second time mechanically.
rationale.otherAssets: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not a statement that all non-operating assets are absent or worthless. Review assets not already included in snapshot cash and avoid double counting.

reportedAnchors.classification: reported or directly derived from reported current financials
reported results and explicitly labeled management outlook; not the base-case forecast
reportedAnchors.text: FY2026 revenue was $331.8bn and operating income $155.2bn; Q4 revenue grew 18%.

waccBuild.classification: analyst model estimate; only riskFreeUSD is an observed input
waccBuild.equityRiskPremiumClassification: chosen long-run assumption; January reference is 4.23%, not a current estimate
waccBuild.formula: Ke = Rf + assumed beta × chosen ERP + extra equity risk; WACC = Ke × (1 − debt weight) + assumed Kd × (1 − tax) × debt weight
waccBuild.limits: Not a live beta regression, bond yield, market-value capital structure or country-default estimate. Extra equity allowances can overlap with operating downside; stress both rather than treating precision as evidence.

bridgePolicy.note: Finance-lease obligations and non-operating investments are material. Lease capitalization must be reconciled with operating profit and reinvestment, not deducted a second time mechanically.

modelLimits: One sales/capital ratio smooths the front-loaded infrastructure buildout and may overstate early cash flow.
uncertainties: AI monetization and customer returns on infrastructure spending
GPU useful lives, finance leases and capacity utilization

modelSuitability.note: An internally checked conditional model, not proof that business assumptions will be realized.

economicChecks.classification: computed consequences of assumptions; not reported outcomes or probabilities
economicChecks.note: Operating math only. No cash/debt/claims/share bridge is asserted; hard gates remain. Terminal share above 100% means negative explicit-period present value, not a probability.

# Microsoft: forecast and valuation dossier
As of **17 October 2026**. Latest reported financial period: **30 June 2026**. September2026/FY2027Q1 actuals are not assumed. All dollar amounts are USD. Conditional valuation research, not a trading recommendation.

## Bottom line
Microsoft's demand and distribution evidence supports a longer growth phase than a mature software-only model, but the capital burden has changed fundamentally. Use five explicit early years in the base and bull cases, then a fade to maturity. Base revenue growth18%/17%/15%/13%/11% reaches approximately$661bn in year5 and$1.217tn in year15. That requires successful monetization and utilization, not simply a large order book.

The largest modeling trap is treating the revised **$175bn CY2026 capex outlook as an economic cut from$190bn**. From FY2027 Microsoft extends datacenter/office building lives from15 to25years. More future datacenter leases then classify as operating rather than finance, removing them from reported capex. Management says underlying investment intentions are unchanged; the near-term depreciation benefit is expected to be small. A cash-flow model must follow economic investment and lease payments through the reclassification. [Official July call](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2026/earnings-fy-2026-q4).

Existing base assumptions of18% growth,42% mature margin,0.6x sales/capital,22% tax and9.5% WACC are not irrational, but a single constant capital ratio misses the investment surge. Proposed base uses front-loaded0.45x/0.50x/0.60x/0.70x/0.80x marginal sales/capital, eventually43% EBIT margin and15-year maturity. No app edits were made.

## Reported growth, mix and profit evidence
Revenue advanced from$245.122bn in FY2024 to$281.724bn in FY2025 and$331.839bn in FY2026. EBIT rose$109.433bn/$128.528bn/$155.237bn; operating margins44.64%/45.62%/46.78%. FY2026 revenue grew17.8%, EBIT20.8%. These figures support genuine operating leverage, but not a conclusion that AI infrastructure has software-like marginal capital needs. [FY2026 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm).

FY2026 Microsoft Cloud revenue was approximately$214.4bn,+27%; Azure exceeded$100bn,+41%. In Q4, consolidated revenue was$90.007bn. Approximate segment revenues were PBP$37.8bn, Intelligent Cloud$39.3bn and More Personal Computing$12.9bn, with respective margins58%,41% and21%. PBP's productivity economics help finance lower-margin infrastructure. Consumer/gaming weakness and impairments are counterexamples to a uniformly successful portfolio. More than30m paid M365Copilot seats and consumption pricing demonstrate adoption, but do not disclose product contribution profit or incremental price per retained seat. [Issuer call and Q&A](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2026/earnings-fy-2026-q4).

Commercial RPO reached$678bn,+84%, versus25% growth excluding OpenAI; average duration2.3years, about30% expected to convert over the next12months. Treat duration, conversion and credit exposure separately. Related-party OpenAI commercial revenue, including revenue-sharing payments, was$24.1bn, about7.3% of company sales; accounts receivable were$6.0bn. That is distinct from Microsoft's approximately25% equity stake, $13bn funding commitment ($11.9bn funded), and nonoperating investment gains. A large contract backed by a customer raising capital is not equivalent to cash already earned. [Annual report, investment and revenue notes](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm).

## Guidance quality, revisions and comparability
The primary issuer hosts readable full transcripts. The12-quarter sample FY2024Q1–FY2026Q4 matches original next-quarter guidance to the same nominal revenue periods. **All12 results exceeded the original upper bound**; mean midpoint error+2.44%, median+2.16%. Earlier consolidated ranges are explicitly derived sums of the three segment ranges. A one-quarter beat does not establish an unbiased forecast or justify increasing every modeled growth rate.

Azure's metric definition changed for FY2025. The original July2024 guide of28–29% CC growth is not comparable with34% reported under the revised definition. The August21 mechanical reissue guided approximately33% under the new definition, followed by34% actual. EMS/per-user PowerBI and other reporting changes shifted category boundaries; consolidated revenue outlook remained unchanged. FY2024 results used in the history retain the contemporaneous basis. [Original reporting-change exhibit](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312524204403/d846847dex991.htm).

Longer capacity forecasts have required revision. January2025 expected AI supply roughly balanced with near-term demand by FY2025 end; April pushed constraints beyond June; October2025 extended them at least through FY2026; April2026 at least through calendar2026. Demand growth and capacity delivery both matter, so these revisions are evidence of timing uncertainty, not proof of deployment failure alone.

FY2026 operating margin was initially expected slightly lower. January2026 revised to slightly higher, April to roughly one point higher including expected retirement-program expense; actual was+1.16points. This matched the last approximate view more closely than the initial view. The full history preserves original versus revised versions instead of silently replacing a forecast.

Current FY2027Q1 outlook: revenue$89.85–90.95bn, Azure approximately45% CC growth, COGS$29.6–29.8bn, opex$16.8–16.9bn, tax about20%, capex more than$50bn. FY2027 revenue and EBIT should grow double digits, operating margin decline less than1point, opex rise mid/high single digits, capex grow and cash FCF remain positive. These are pending conditional forecasts. There is no verified formal multiyear revenue CAGR commitment. [Official July outlook](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2026/earnings-fy-2026-q4), detailed dates/errors in evidence-MSFT.html#guidance.

## Capital intensity, accounting and cash conversion
Cash PP&E spend accelerated$44.477bn/$64.551bn/$115.948bn across FY2024–2026, while finance-lease right-of-use additions reached$24.608bn in FY2026. Cash capex plus those additions totals$140.556bn. A reported capex metric can differ because of delivery and recognition timing; it is not automatically identical to annual cash-flow capex plus every lease addition.

The annual report's **$34.3bn is depreciation alone**. Cash-flow “depreciation, amortization and other” is$38.534bn, and intangible amortization is separately about$4.7bn. Do not relabel the depreciation-only line full D&A, or assume the CFO reconciliation line is a clean D&A subtotal. Cash capex plus finance-lease additions minus that reconciliation addback is about$102.0bn against$50.1bn incremental revenue, a rough0.49x sales/investment proxy before working capital and other adjustments. This is a useful warning, not a fully normalized return calculation. [Annual financial statements and notes8/10/13](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm).

CFO was$182.935bn and cashcapex FCF$66.987bn. CFO includes$12.405bn SBC addback and timing effects: receivables used$12.737bn, while payables added$5.268bn and unearned revenue$9.361bn. Other investing outflows increased substantially from component facilitation. Cash FCF excludes newly incurred finance-lease investment and finance principal paid in financing; a valuation must reconcile that rather than assuming it is all distributable owner cash.

At June30, finance-lease liabilities were$66.594bn and operating$21.925bn. Additional uncommenced leases were$329.1bn, starting FY2027–2033 with1–20year terms. The contractual lease total$443.506bn includes undiscounted payments, interest and uncommenced arrangements; it is not an extra debt balance to subtract in full. Purchase commitments$194.060bn and construction$34.566bn further constrain flexibility. Count future investment/rent and financing consistently, avoiding both omission and double counting.

Longer building accounting lives do not change server/accelerator replacement cash needs. Q4 capex was predominantly shorter-lived CPU/GPU equipment. Stress faster obsolescence, component inflation, power delays and excess capacity after current shortages ease. Conversely, lower unit costs and better utilization can improve returns, but demand may also consume those savings through pricing and heavier usage.

## Management capability and interview evidence
Nadella has been CEO since February2014 and Hood CFO since May2013, spanning the measured period. The evidence shows sustained commercial growth and cost discipline, not proof of individual causality. Product adoption and reported datacenter deployment improvements support execution; shifting capacity dates, consumer weakness and huge uncommenced commitments are material counterexamples. evidence-MSFT.html#management evaluates five dimensions and identifies these limits.

In the March4 Morgan Stanley interview, Nadella described returns as a function of utilization across hardware generations, diverse customers and applications, plus subscription and metered consumption economics. This explains why Azure growth alone cannot capture all investment benefits, but is not a numerical project-ROI guarantee. [Primary conference transcript](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2026/morgan-stanley-tmt-conference).

## Conditional forecast proposals
Annual year1 is FY2027. After the stated early phase, growth fades linearly to terminal growth; capital efficiency converges to the value consistent with mature margin, tax and terminal ROIC during the final five years.

| Case | Early annual revenue growth | Early years / maturity | Mature EBIT margin | Tax | WACC | Terminal growth / ROIC | Maturity sales |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| base | 18%, 17%, 15%, 13%, 11% | 5 / 15 | 43% | 22% | 9.5% | 2.5% / 16% | $1,217.0bn |
| bull | 22%, 22%, 20%, 18%, 16% | 5 / 20 | 46% | 20% | 9% | 3% / 22% | $2,956.0bn |
| bear | 12%, 10%, 8% | 3 / 10 | 36% | 23% | 10.5% | 2% / 11% | $603.2bn |

The base begins at46% operating margin, consistent with management's less-than1point decline from46.78%, then gradually fades to43%. Front-loaded investment leaves little first-year simplified FCFF despite strong operating profit. All three scenarios remain positive-FCFF in this particular arithmetic; that is not a guarantee. More severe supply costs, lease commitments or an unfavorable working-capital swing can make cash flow negative.

The bull's **$2.956tn maturity revenue and$1.360tn operating profit** are especially demanding: almost9x current sales over20years. It requires major expansion of global enterprise spending and a durable Microsoft share of AI/application value. It is not validated by a20-year horizon alone. The bear still reaches$603bn sales; it is a slower-growth/margin-pressure case, not a catastrophic scenario. Independent recession, major security, customer-credit and regulatory shocks remain outside that range.

Base terminal marginalROIC16% exceeds9.5% WACC but is below the near-term software franchise's accounting returns. Bull22% and bear11% test persistence of excess returns. Base22% normalized operating tax is above recent quarterly20% outlook and excludes investment gains from operating logic. WACC uses Treasury5.09% observed October16, chosen ERP4.5%, assumed beta1.05 and5% debt weight; the build rounds9.55% to9.5%. No beta regression, market-value capital structure or current bond spread was independently estimated.

## Claims, investments, financing and dilution gates
Cash plus short-term investments$76.843bn is already in the snapshot. Long-term investments$36.348bn are separate carrying values, not guaranteed cash realizations. Remove investment gains from operating forecasts; if an investment is added separately, do not also capitalize the same underlying investment distributions in operating value. Operating customer revenue from OpenAI is a separate commercial stream with its own costs and credit risk.

Financial debt carrying amount$40.294bn excludes leases; contractual face principal$46.136bn is a different measurement. The IRS continues to propose$28.9bn additional tax plus penalties/interest on transfer-pricing issues. Microsoft disputes this and believes reserves adequate. Neither subtracting the entire demand as certain incremental debt nor assuming zero exposure is justified; reconcile reserves and stress incremental outcomes.

FY2026 program buybacks cost$16.719bn for about36m shares. The cash-flow repurchase line$22.271bn includes employee-tax withholding; dividend cash was$26.445bn versus$27.035bn declared. Share count stayed near7.43bn, so an automatic large future shrink is unsupported. SBC$12.405bn remains a cost; unrecognized stock-award compensation$24.8bn over about3years and292m shares authorized for future grants are not the same as currently outstanding dilution.

Cover shares7.425545bn, period-end7.427bn and historical weighted diluted7.453bn serve different purposes. A per-share value remains gated until lease-consistent cash flow, nonoperating investments, contingencies and awards are reconciled. evidence-MSFT.html#judgment includes operating-EV illustrations solely as mathematical consequences, with per-share values null.

## What would change the thesis
Track Azure growth against delivered capacity; RPO conversion and customer concentration; cloud gross margins; cash/lease/prepayment investment together; Copilot monetization versus usage cost; and impairment/replacement experience. Growth slowing as capacity becomes available would be more damaging than growth limited by documented shortages. A falling reported capex figure with rising lease cash payments is not an efficiency win. Higher economic depreciation, pricing competition, security/reliability failures and tax/regulatory exposure can invalidate the scenario even while headline bookings remain high.

implementationGates: No default otherClaims=0 or otherAssets=0 may be interpreted as verified absence.

analystJudgment.interpretation: WACC and terminal parameters are analyst estimates; strong guidance track records do not receive a mechanical credibility uplift.

rationale.growth: Base18/17/15/13/11% balances FY26+17.8%, next-quarter16–17% total guide, Azure45% CC guide and broad RPO growth excluding OpenAI25%. It does not extrapolate totalRPO84% or Azure43% to the consolidated company. Bull20-year scale is deliberately demanding and must be tested against customer IT spending.
rationale.margin: FY27 guide down<1pp anchors46% first-year versus46.78% FY26. Fade toward43% prices in lower-margin infrastructure/consumption mix and faster economic obsolescence; bull46% needs applications and efficiency offset; bear36% tests pricing/utilization failures.
rationale.capital: Base0.45x first-year incremental sales/capital charges approximately$133bn reinvestment, then improves. FY26 cash+finance-lease additions less cash-flow D&A/other already imply~0.49x before working capital. Long-run0.85x requires substantial utilization and efficiency gains. CY2026 capex175bn is classification-sensitive, not an investment cut.
rationale.tax: 22% normalized cash-tax estimate above FY27 quarterly20% guide, with investment gains/deferred taxes excluded from operating earnings logic.
rationale.terminal: Base16% marginal ROIC,15-year maturity;20-year bull22% ROIC requires durable software/application capture. Bear11% at10years leaves little spread over10.5% WACC. Final capital ratio is explicitly reconciled to terminal ROIC.
rationale.bridge: Lease liabilities66.594bn finance and21.925bn operating plus329.1bn uncommenced commitments require economic cash-flow treatment; do not capitalize all and also charge all lease rent. Review36.348bn investments separately; do not project fair-value gains into EBIT.

historical_OCF_to_FCFF_proxy.tax_caution: Cash taxes include group-wide taxes/refunds, not a disclosed unlevered operating allocation. This is an exact arithmetic normalization proxy, with interest timing, nonoperating-tax attribution and other-assets allocation requiring a sensitivity, not an audited FCFF.
historical_OCF_to_FCFF_proxy.warning: Subtracting all 41,441 deferred-tax add-back while leaving tax settlements in WC over-normalizes tax. Do not treat all 75,200 cash-flow D&A as physical PPE depreciation.

capital_and_supplier_financing.convention: Preferred cash-capex forecast excludes capital-creditors movement from operating WC. Track accrued asset additions and capital-creditor balances separately for capacity and paydown stress. If supplier credit is instead debtlike, include accrued capex, show equal financing inflow, and apply one consistent opening-liability claim. Never add 29,267 to cash capex as an unfinanced current cash requirement.

CY2026_to_rolling_year1.definition: Cash capex interpreted consistently with the company Q2 $53.1bn and H1 $96.3bn net-of-sales/incentives measures; guide is approximate, not a hard contractual floor.
CY2026_to_rolling_year1.gross_cash_capex_conversion: Add assumed ~$4bn annual asset sales/incentives: rolling year1 gross cash capex ~$238–278bn; do not compare gross and net unlabeled.

normalization_basis.reported_asset_lives: Buildings up to 40 years; servers/networking 5–6 years; heavy equipment 10–13; other equipment 3–10. Subset server life reduced 6 to5 effective2025; increased2025 D&A by~1,400.
normalization_basis.reported_PPE_cohorts: FY2025 gross server/networking172,492; construction-in-progress71,745; netPPE357,025. June2026 netPPE446,046. TTM PPE D&A49,741 and Q2 annualized55,476.
normalization_basis.reasoning: Existing assets plus recent buildout moving in service drive depreciation catch-up. Do not depreciate all new construction from day1 or keep D&A flat as capex surges. As a rough cohort check, 60% server additions over5.5years,30% facilities over25years,10% other over10years gives~13.1% annual depreciation on in-service additions; half-year convention and retirement/CIP schedules can support~65bn next-year D&A. Mix, lives and placement dates are analyst assumptions, not disclosed future mix.
normalization_basis.management_cycle_statement: Management described data-center spending about2years before monetization, servers purchased months before use, server breakeven under3years and longer-lived facilities. This supports an eventual normalization scenario, not certainty of utilization or returns.
normalization_basis.non_PPE_reinvestment_basis: Historical combined non-PPE amortization plus tax-adjusted operating-asset/liability cash movements was a 3.9bn source; forecast0–15bn year1 uses to allow Cloud receivables, inventory/content and lease-payment timing, excluding capital creditors and financing investments.
normalization_basis.years_after7: Fade temporary implied capital productivity toward existing terminal S:C0.98684, consistent with12%ROIC / (16%margin ×76%after-tax share). No lower terminal reinvestment/free-cash-flow windfall.

Capital-creditors timing, accelerated depreciation and customer investment funding are separate mechanisms. Do not call private equity marks deployable cash or treat backlog as funded orders.

An external-funding need is a conditional financing plan: test debt capacity, dilution, covenant/liquidity buffers and cash interest. It does not automatically invalidate operating EV, imply equity issuance, or create an extra debt deduction.

existing-company-base-cases.name: AMAZON COM INC
existing-company-base-cases.summary: AWS, advertising and fulfillment efficiency raise consolidated profitability, with a heavy infrastructure bill and lower-margin retail still central.

rationale.growth: 14% sits between FY2025 growth of 12.4% and Q2 2026 growth of 20%. AWS and advertising support expansion, but they cannot justify applying their segment growth to all retail revenue.
rationale.targetMargin: 15% improves on 12.1% TTM as AWS/advertising mix and retail efficiency rise. It remains far below AWS segment margins because consolidated sales include substantial low-margin commerce.
rationale.tax: 24% is a normalized operating-tax assumption. Recent investment gains distort pretax income and the accounting effective rate, so those gains do not set operating cash tax.
rationale.salesCapital: 0.8x requires $1.25 of net reinvestment per incremental $1 of sales. AI data centers, fulfillment and working capital keep reinvestment high even with supplier financing; early modeled FCFF can be negative.
rationale.terminalROIC: 10% assumes mature capital earns approximately the cost of capital. Scale advantages are largely competed away after the explicit growth period.
rationale.wacc: 10.0% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.2, 10% target debt and a 1-point debt spread balance resilient diversified businesses against discretionary spending and the infrastructure funding cycle.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
rationale.otherClaims: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not evidence that no additional claims exist. Review operating/finance leases, financing obligations and minority investments. Current cash is not a complete appraisal of all non-operating assets.
rationale.otherAssets: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not a statement that all non-operating assets are absent or worthless. Review assets not already included in snapshot cash and avoid double counting.

reportedAnchors.classification: reported or directly derived from reported current financials
reported results and explicitly labeled management outlook; not the base-case forecast
reportedAnchors.text: Q2 revenue grew 20%, AWS revenue grew 37%, and TTM free cash flow was an outflow of $7.6bn. The release separately identified non-operating investment gains.

waccBuild.classification: analyst model estimate; only riskFreeUSD is an observed input
waccBuild.equityRiskPremiumClassification: chosen long-run assumption; January reference is 4.23%, not a current estimate
waccBuild.formula: Ke = Rf + assumed beta × chosen ERP + extra equity risk; WACC = Ke × (1 − debt weight) + assumed Kd × (1 − tax) × debt weight
waccBuild.limits: Not a live beta regression, bond yield, market-value capital structure or country-default estimate. Extra equity allowances can overlap with operating downside; stress both rather than treating precision as evidence.

bridgePolicy.note: Review operating/finance leases, financing obligations and minority investments. Current cash is not a complete appraisal of all non-operating assets.

modelLimits: About 93% of modeled operating value comes after year 10. The result is highly dependent on mature margins, required reinvestment and discount rates.
A single margin hides very different AWS, advertising and retail economics; net reinvestment is not the company free-cash-flow reconciliation.
uncertainties: AWS capacity economics and depreciation versus AI demand
Retail wage, shipping and competitive pressures; investment gains are not operating earnings

companies.dossierMarkdown:
# Amazon forecast and valuation dossier

**Research cutoff: October 17, 2026. Latest reported quarter: June 30, 2026, released July 30; 10-Q filed July 31. USD billions unless stated.** This is an analytical scenario proposal, not investment advice, issuer guidance or analyst consensus. No Q3 actuals were available by the cutoff. Financial history contains 14 quarters and FY2023–FY2025. All videos are **not watched**; readable transcript coverage is specified below.

## Decision-useful conclusion

AWS acceleration warrants an explicit three-year high-growth phase rather than fading growth immediately. It does **not** warrant valuing AI capacity as capital-light software. A proposed base is **18%, 17%, 15% revenue growth for years 1–3**, then a fade to **2.5% by year 15**, a **16% mature operating margin**, **24% normalized tax**, **10.25% WACC**, and **12% terminal ROIC**. Early sales/incremental-capital ratios of **0.65, 0.75 and 0.85** keep substantial build-out costs in the forecast.

These are conditional research inputs. Do not install them as production defaults while the model omits the investment, customer-financing, lease and acquisition bridge. Existing zero nonoperating-asset/claim placeholders are materially incomplete. The proposed path reaches **$1.232tn revenue in year 3 and $3.160tn in year 15**, with $506bn mature EBIT. That is a demanding scale claim, not merely a small adjustment to near-term growth.

## 1. What actually changed

The latest quarter delivered revenue **$200.606bn, +19.6%**, and EBIT **$27.461bn**, a 13.69% margin. Q1 revenue was $181.519bn, versus $155.667bn a year earlier. AWS accelerated from 17.5% in Q2 2025 to about 20% in Q3, 24% in Q4, 28% in Q1 2026 and **36.7% in Q2 2026**. This supports a genuine operating inflection, although quarter-to-quarter growth contains capacity timing and Prime Day distortions. [Q2 2026 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000026/amzn-20260630.htm)

| Q2 2026 segment | Revenue | Share | EBIT | Segment margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| North America | 116.177 | 57.91% | 9.123 | 7.85% |
| International | 42.197 | 21.03% | 1.717 | 4.07% |
| AWS | 42.232 | 21.05% | 16.621 | 39.36% |

AWS generates approximately 60.5% of reported segment/consolidated EBIT from 21.1% of sales. Product mix is online stores $70.432bn, physical stores $5.794bn, third-party seller services $46.780bn, advertising $19.809bn, subscriptions $13.730bn, AWS $42.232bn and other $1.829bn. These product categories overlap the geographic segments; **do not add advertising on top of segment revenue**. AI and chip run-rates above $25bn each also overlap and are not separately additive segments. [Q2 release](https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Second-Quarter-Results/default.aspx)

Annual revenue rose from $574.785bn in 2023 to $637.959bn in 2024 and $716.924bn in 2025. FY2025 AWS sales were $128.725bn and EBIT $45.606bn. North America EBIT was $29.619bn; International $4.750bn. TTM June revenue is **$775.680bn**, EBIT **$93.712bn**, margin 12.08%. The machine-readable file preserves source observations and derived quarterly cash-flow figures. [FY2025 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000004/amzn-20251231.htm)

## 2. Management outlook, revisions and interviews

### Formal guidance

The July 30 outlook for Q3 was **$197–202bn revenue and $22.5–26.5bn operating income**. Moving Prime Day from Q3 into Q2 lowers the reported Q3 growth comparison by nearly four percentage points; FX was expected to subtract approximately 80bp. The guide excludes energy-derivative remeasurement and assumes no additional acquisitions, restructurings or legal settlements. The Q3 outcome remains open at this cutoff. [Issuer guidance](https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Second-Quarter-Results/default.aspx)

The original February 5 FY2026 capex outlook was approximately **$200bn**. July 30 call commentary raised cash capex to approximately **$220bn**, citing memory costs. Consequently, a 10% spending increase cannot be treated as a 10% capacity increase. [Original outlook](https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-Results/default.aspx), [readable July call](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/amzn/transcripts/657334-q2-2026/)

### Readable management evidence

- **April 9, 2026 shareholder letter:** Jassy says AWS added 3.9GW in 2025 and targets doubling total power capacity by end-2027. Capex precedes customer billing by roughly 6–24 months. The letter distinguishes long-lived buildings from shorter-lived chips/servers, reports customer commitments against much of the build, and describes Trainium3 shipping and Trainium4's approximate future availability. These are management operational claims and targets, not audited incremental ROIC. [Letter](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/company-news/amazon-ceo-andy-jassy-2025-letter-to-shareholders)
- **July 30 earnings call:** selected prepared remarks and Q&A were read in a public third-party transcription. Management describes server payback below three years, persistent capacity shortages into 2027, and an undated possibility of AWS becoming a $1tn revenue business. The last item is an aspiration with no forecast horizon, not a base-case target. The transcription is not issuer-certified. [Transcript](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/amzn/transcripts/657334-q2-2026/)
- **October 8, 2026 a16z interview with AWS CEO Matt Garman:** original publisher/video metadata were checked; the public automated transcript was read, particularly approximately 00:16–00:25. Garman discusses power, chips, memory and construction bottlenecks, reserving capacity for smaller customers, and enterprise production adoption. He frames demand as durable but provides no formal multi-year AWS growth rate. Claims about customer ROI and concentration are executive observations, not independently audited findings. Recording date was not disclosed. [Original publisher](https://a16z.simplecast.com/episodes/building-the-cloud-for-an-agentic-world-aws-ceo-matt-garman-d18BWOHC), [text read](https://podscripts.co/podcasts/the-a16z-show/building-the-cloud-for-an-agentic-world-aws-ceo-matt-garman)
- **June 23, 2026 Platformer interview:** original public page and Amazon's excerpt were read. Garman's survey of CIOs combines positive ROI already achieved with a prospective path to ROI. It cannot establish that 90% of all enterprises currently earn positive AI returns. The issuer excerpt has no visible exact publication date, so none is invented. [Original interview](https://www.platformer.news/matt-garman-aws-ceo-interview-ai-jobs/), [issuer excerpt](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/aws/aws-matt-garman-enterprise-ai-roi-interview-2026)

### Forecasting track record

The separate scorecard covers **12 consecutive target quarters, Q3 2023 through Q2 2026**, using each original preceding-quarter issuer range, not a selection of recent beats. Revenue was above range in **9**, within in **3**, below in **0**. EBIT was above in **10**, within in **2**, below in **0**. Every entry stores dates, actual-period sources, midpoint error and distance outside the range.

This is evidence of conservative ranges plus delivery, not proof that management forecasts exact demand or future AI returns. Q3 2025 GAAP EBIT was within range but contained approximately $4.3bn of new settlement/severance charges that the original guide excluded; issuer commentary excluding these put EBIT above range. Q2 2026 includes $640m tariff refunds and $551m energy-derivative gains. Subtracting both still leaves $26.270bn, above the $24bn high, but that sensitivity is not a substitute for the reported outcome. Annual capex vintages and the undated $1tn aspiration are deliberately scored separately.

## 3. Economics that the valuation must retain

**Cash and physical capital.** TTM operating cash flow was $161.403bn. Gross cash PPE purchases were $173.028bn; proceeds/incentives $4.021bn; net cash capex $169.007bn. Issuer FCF was therefore **negative $7.604bn**, not OCF minus gross capex. TTM physical depreciation was $49.741bn, while cash-flow D&A was $75.200bn and includes other amortization. Treating all D&A as physical replacement capex would overstate sustainable cash generation. H1 net cash capex was $96.3bn. [Q2 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000026/amzn-20260630.htm)

**Asset lives and margins.** In 2025 Amazon shortened the useful life of a subset of servers from six to five years, after extending server lives from five to six years in 2024. The 2025 change increased depreciation approximately $1.4bn. Longer-lived heavy equipment moved in the opposite direction. These estimates affect accounting margins but do not erase replacement spending. Q2 energy marks predominantly benefited AWS and can reverse. The base 16% mature consolidated margin rests on AWS/advertising mix and fulfillment efficiency, not indefinitely retaining today's 39% AWS segment margin.

**Working capital and tax.** Retail supplier financing and fast cash collection help fund operations, but seasonal payable swings are not perpetual free financing. Model inventories, receivables, payables and customer payments together. Accelerated tax depreciation/R&D deductions affect cash timing; normalized 24% tax is an inference, not the investment-gain-distorted recent effective tax rate. A separate deferred-tax schedule is preferable.

**SBC and dilution.** TTM SBC was $19.314bn. June common shares were 10,783m versus 10,731m at December, and H1 diluted weighted-average shares were 10,889m. Keep SBC in operating margins; do not add it back to FCFF while also assuming zero employee dilution. The unrecognized compensation backlog is not identical to a current cash liability.

**ROIC.** AWS profit growth provides evidence of monetization, but no audited incremental AI-vintage ROIC is disclosed. Consolidated equity is inflated by unrealized AI-investment marks, and lease treatment changes invested capital. This dossier therefore does not present a spurious historical ROIC precise to a decimal. The proposed 12% terminal ROIC is a transparent inference; its reinvestment identity is enforced in the scenario file.

## 4. Financing, assets and unresolved claims

June cash plus marketable securities totaled $122.988bn; debt carrying value $132.224bn; finance leases $13.451bn; operating leases $96.320bn. Uncommenced leases of $137.214bn and unconditional purchase obligations of $130.065bn are undiscounted future commitments, not automatically incremental net debt if cash-flow forecasts already include their assets/costs.

The investment bridge is substantial: Anthropic preferred carrying value **$92.5bn**, Anthropic convertible notes fair value **$97.9bn**, and OpenAI preferred **$28.7bn** at June. Another **$21.3bn** was invested in OpenAI after June, disclosed before filing. That event requires a matching cash reduction when adding investment assets. An Anthropic facility had **$15bn** remaining, with availability linked to compute-delivery milestones. Private-asset marks, customer funding, cloud commitments and future revenue are economically related; do not add each without considering dependencies, taxes, credit risk and liquidity restrictions.

AWS backlog was approximately **$496bn**, weighted-average remaining contract life **6.4 years**. Recognition depends on usage and performance; backlog is neither immediate cash nor an independent asset to add to enterprise value.

The April 13 Globalstar agreement implied approximately **$10.9bn enterprise value including debt**, with cash/stock elections, cash capped at 40% of shares, milestone adjustments and expected 2027 closing conditions. Separate Apple agreements include services and redemption of interests in a Globalstar entity. Acquisition cash, dilution and assets require a conditional transaction schedule. Do not simply subtract $10.9bn as current debt.

The proposal contains an itemized obligation/asset register with source, date, conditionality and proposed treatment. None of these uncertainties is silently assumed to be zero. [Q2 notes 2–4 and commitments](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000026/amzn-20260630.htm)

## 5. Proposed scenarios and invalidators

| Inferred scenario | Early growth, years 1–3 | Maturity | Mature margin | WACC | Terminal ROIC | Terminal growth |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Base | 18%, 17%, 15% | 15 years | 16% | 10.25% | 12% | 2.5% |
| Bull stress | 22%, 22%, 20% | 20 years | 19% | 9.25% | 16% | 2.75% |
| Bear | 10%, 8%, 6% | 10 years | 11.5% | 11.5% | 9% | 2% |

The bull stress reaches $7.867tn revenue and $1.495tn EBIT at maturity. It requires enormous global cloud/commerce expansion and durable unit economics; **it is an outer scenario, not a likely planning case**. The bear reaches $1.260tn revenue. No scenario probabilities or price target were fitted. The cost-of-capital framework uses verified October 16 Treasury 10-year 5.09%; the 4.5% ERP, beta and financing weights are chosen assumptions, not measured October forward returns.

Monitor: AWS growth and backlog conversion against actual capacity delivery; customer financing quality; capex/revenue and physical depreciation; normalized retail margin; AI pricing and server useful life; energy/power costs; net dilution and debt funding. Two ordinary quarters below 20% AWS growth despite new capacity, or continued extraordinary capex with little 2027–2028 operating-cash conversion, would materially weaken the proposed base.

bridge_method.CFO_identity: NI + PP&E depreciation + SBC + deferred tax adjustment - securities gains + other noncash + non-tax WC cash effect + income-tax WC cash effect
bridge_method.normalized_PPE_proxy: CFO - cash capex - SBC - (OI&E - securities gains reversed in CFO) + tax provision - deferred tax adjustment - tax WC cash effect - EBIT*normalized_tax - other noncash
bridge_method.equivalent_identity: EBIT*(1-normalized_tax) + PP&E depreciation - cash capex + non-tax WC cash effect
bridge_method.tax_rate: 22% is the existing proposal sensitivity, not an observed effective cash tax rate. Use 20–24% normalization sensitivity.

tax_disclosure_check.caution: H1 and TTM cash-flow-implied amounts are algebraic all-items approximations, not separately disclosed cash taxes. They include taxes on nonoperating results, settlements, temporary differences and rounding/classification effects.

bridge_method.limits: PPE-only proxy strips the entire other noncash line for exact reproducibility. Restore independently verified operating amortization and appropriate operating noncash charges; do not treat this stripped residual as precise final FCFF. H1 intangible amortization 545 yields -25,109.52 before financing-lease asset adjustments. FY2025 full intangible amortization was not separately identified in this review, so no unsupported TTM estimate is added.
bridge_method.interest: H1 interest expense 1,811 and interest income 2,811 are in OI&E, which this bridge removes together with other nonoperating amounts. Adding after-tax interest again would double count. The 628 of H1 capitalized interest requires a consistent capex/financing convention; do not assume accrued interest equals cash interest paid.
bridge_method.sbc: Retain SBC in EBIT/NOPAT and do not add it back to economic FCFF. Add the actual noncash SBC cash-flow adjustment only in the separate cash-funding bridge. Forecast employee equity dilution or its replacement cost consistently; do not charge the same SBC cost again through both an expense-retained valuation and a full replacement-cost/share-dilution penalty.
bridge_method.WC: H1 non-tax WC cash consumption is 21,406, including inventory 7,739 and receivables 6,904; tax WC is a separate +8,304. Never combine a normal WC forecast with a second customer-prepayment benefit already inside that forecast.

gross_vs_net_and_supplier_credit.treatment: Do not add the entire 29,113 unpaid PPE balance to cash capex. If reconstructing accrual investment, reconcile the change in capital payables and acquisition/FX/disposal effects, and record matching supplier-credit financing. When using cash capex directly, its eventual settlement is a timing consideration, not another current investment deduction.
gross_vs_net_and_supplier_credit.policy: Depreciation starts when assets enter service. Servers/network equipment generally depreciate over six years; buildings over seven to forty years. Model asset cohorts and in-service dates; a six-year life does not justify instantaneous depreciation of all current cash capex.

guidance_to_rolling_forecast.rolling_2027_formula: H2 2026 cash capex + H1 2027 cash capex. There is no quantified CY2027 issuer guide in the reviewed sources.
guidance_to_rolling_forecast.classification: Analytical scenario ranges anchored to guide, investment backlog, depreciation policy and observed WC. They are not management forecasts or confidence intervals; extreme component bounds need not occur together.
guidance_to_rolling_forecast.range_rationale: June2027 gross capex range assumes roughly 111–141bn H1 2027 at the matching guide endpoints. June2028 permits continuing 2027 ramp and June2029 allows stabilization or another expansion. D&A rises as the 122.8bn construction/installation pipeline and new cohorts enter service. Inventory/receivables keep WC a possible cash use; customer backlog itself supplies no cash.
normalization_conditions: Use 2027/2028 physical deliveries and cohort depreciation to decide whether 2029 capex stabilizes; do not automatically fade cash capex when revenue growth fades.
Test supplier-credit unwind, TPU inventory-to-revenue conversion, leased capacity cost and acquired-intangible amortization separately.

D&A ranges are intended as total operating D&A, including verified intangible amortization and finance-lease asset depreciation. Reconcile the finance-lease amortization disclosure to modeled PP&E depreciation before any separate addback; include it once.

After June2029, transition asset cohorts and reinvestment over several years. Do not jump from explicit capital spending to a terminal sales/capital ratio; satisfy terminal net reinvestment = growth/ROIC*NOPAT.

22% tax and original revenue/NOPAT are sensitivities. Higher depreciation, temporary third-party capacity and TPU hardware mix must also be tested through margins; preserving margins while changing D&A is not an integrated forecast.

original_model_diagnostic.interpretation: Original first-year net reinvestment lies inside the explicit range. There is no source-supported reason to force it downward purely to eliminate a deficit. The mechanically linked sales/capital path omits D&A, supplier financing, leases and cash taxes needed to explain cash funding.

forward_cash_funding_identity: Start with economic FCFF with SBC expensed and operating taxes normalized.
Add back the noncash SBC cash-flow adjustment only to measure cash available; separately recognize the employee equity claim consistently in valuation.
Add actual temporary operating tax savings (or subtract reversals), and bridge cash nonoperating receipts and cash interest; do not use unrealized securities/derivative gains as funding.

If economic reinvestment included financed lease assets or accrued capital-payable increases, add matching financing sources, then deduct actual principal/prepayments or supplier settlements only once. If using cash capex, do not add supplier financing again.
Deduct strategic equity/customer financing, acquisitions, dividends, employee award withholding, debt maturities and any other cash commitments excluded from operating FCFF.
Then apply existing liquid assets above an explicit buffer and new net debt/equity financing. This required-financing balance is distinct from cumulative economic FCFF.

liquidity_and_obligations.liquidity_caution: Do not treat equity values or unrealized gains as cash. Debt securities include longer maturities and market risk. A parent-level availability/operating-buffer adjustment is still needed; the annual filing identified 5.6bn of consolidated VIE assets restricted to those VIE obligations at December2025, with no updated June amount established in this review.
liquidity_and_obligations.financing_caution: Credit and CP capacity are contingent financing tools, not cash assets and not necessarily additive independent borrowing capacity. June balance sheet already includes H1 proceeds; do not add them again. Bridge August debt proceeds and uses together if updating anchor.
liquidity_and_obligations.treatment: Schedule commitments in the appropriate capex, inventory/COGS, rent, financing or contingent-loss line. Do not subtract notional commitments as extra debt on top of forecast spending. The 20bn contingent funding is inside 21.9bn VIE commitments, not additive. Existing lease VIE exposures are already in lease totals. Treat guarantees through default/mitigation scenarios and avoid double counting recorded derivative liabilities. Preferred conversion/capped-call terms require the existing claim model; never subtract full liquidation preference and also apply full conversion dilution.
liquidity_and_obligations.energy_guarantee_update_gap: The June filing describes terms through September2026. Do not assume all 7.6bn remains live or has expired at October17 without a later update.
liquidity_and_obligations.lease_caution: H1 repayments of debt in the cash-flow statement already include finance-lease cash amounts under the filing convention. Do not deduct lease cash again in the exact funding bridge. Finance-lease assets are in PP&E: reconcile the 485 amortization disclosure to the modeled depreciation definition rather than automatically adding it again. If EBIT includes operating rent, do not also subtract the operating lease liability unless rent/EBIT and invested capital are recast consistently.
liquidity_and_obligations.known_July2026_fine_treatment: Note10 reports the previously accrued Android fine and interest paid in July2026. Schedule 5,200 as a post-June cash use. Because previously accrued, do not also book a new recurring EBIT expense or deduct the same accrued liability twice in the valuation/funding bridge.

SBC_cash_settlements_and_ATM.ATM_treatment: Future ATM proceeds offset a cash funding use only when actually issued and are financing with dilution. They do not reduce SBC expense, make stock-award withholding disappear, or add June cash. A full SBC addback with no award-settlement deduction materially overstates cash available for infrastructure.

existing-company-base-cases.name: Alphabet Inc.
existing-company-base-cases.summary: Search and Cloud continue growing, but AI delivery costs, capital intensity and regulatory risk temper long-run margins.

rationale.growth: 18% is below the latest 24% quarter and above FY2025 growth of 15.1%. Cloud expansion supports the uplift, while Search scale and competitive substitution force a deceleration.
rationale.targetMargin: 30% is below 33.1% TTM. Search monetization and Cloud scale are offset by AI compute costs, traffic acquisition and investment in new products.
rationale.tax: 22% normalizes operating taxes above recent effective rates; very large non-operating equity gains make consolidated pretax-income tax ratios unsuitable as a direct operating forecast.
rationale.salesCapital: 0.7x requires $1.43 of net investment per extra $1 of revenue. The current AI buildout warrants much more capital than the historic search-only model.
rationale.terminalROIC: 15% retains valuable distribution and software assets but reduces returns as competition and infrastructure intensity rise.
rationale.wacc: 10.0% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.1, 5% target debt and a 0.8-point debt spread reflect strong core cash flow plus search-transition and regulatory exposure.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
rationale.otherClaims: 0 means no additional user-entered claim beyond the separate explicit current claims model. Do not enter the same modeled claims again. The separate source-dated current claims model explicitly allocates mandatory preferred dilution/dividends, finance leases and noncontrolling claims, and adds a gross noncurrent-investment carrying proxy. Capped-call recovery, investment realization taxes and employee awards remain incomplete.
rationale.otherAssets: 0 means no additional user-entered asset beyond the separate explicit current claims model. Alphabet already includes a gross noncurrent-investment proxy in that bridge; never add it again. No zero is proof of absence.

reportedAnchors.classification: reported or directly derived from reported current financials
reported results and explicitly labeled management outlook; not the base-case forecast
reportedAnchors.text: Q2 2026 revenue was $119.8bn, up 24%, with a 34% operating margin; Google Cloud revenue rose 82%.

waccBuild.classification: analyst model estimate; only riskFreeUSD is an observed input
waccBuild.equityRiskPremiumClassification: chosen long-run assumption; January reference is 4.23%, not a current estimate
waccBuild.formula: Ke = Rf + assumed beta × chosen ERP + extra equity risk; WACC = Ke × (1 − debt weight) + assumed Kd × (1 − tax) × debt weight
waccBuild.limits: Not a live beta regression, bond yield, market-value capital structure or country-default estimate. Extra equity allowances can overlap with operating downside; stress both rather than treating precision as evidence.

bridgePolicy.note: The separate source-dated current claims model explicitly allocates mandatory preferred dilution/dividends, finance leases and noncontrolling claims, and adds a gross noncurrent-investment carrying proxy. Capped-call recovery, investment realization taxes and employee awards remain incomplete.

modelLimits: Non-operating equity gains are excluded from operating income; no separate option value is assigned to Other Bets.
uncertainties: AI query economics, traffic acquisition and regulatory remedies
Mandatory-convertible preferred securities and non-marketable investment valuations

modelSuitability.note: An internally checked conditional model, not proof that business assumptions will be realized.

economicChecks.classification: computed consequences of assumptions; not reported outcomes or probabilities
economicChecks.note: Operating math only; the separate source-matched current claims model computes conditional per-share values. No result is asserted here. Terminal share is not meaningful when operating value is nonpositive.
