existing-current-claims-research.units: USD millions and shares millions except explicitly per-share terms
existing-current-claims-research.classification: Primary-source terms plus explicit analyst bridge scenarios; not a security fair-value appraisal or current quote
existing-current-claims-research.historicalFreezePolicy: No change to historical source files, hashes, dates, or forecasts. June 2026 instrument is never backfilled into December 2025.

reportedAmounts.reconciliation: 19034 - 1011 = 18023. Cash-flow proceeds differ from equity issuance presentation by 29; do not silently force equality or invent the reason.

commonSharesJune30.precision: Rounded to millions. July 15 cover counts coincidentally equal these June 30 balance-sheet counts.

securityTerms.priority: Senior to all three common classes; A and B rank equally; junior to indebtedness and any future senior stock. Liquidation preference plus accumulated unpaid dividends. No participation in residual assets after payment.
securityTerms.redemption: No issuer redemption or sinking fund. Ordinary holder early conversion uses the minimum rate, subject to adjustments.
securityTerms.voting: Preferred generally nonvoting, with protective/nonpayment exceptions. Common A has 1 vote, B 10 votes, C no vote except legally required. A/B/C economic dividend and liquidation rights are otherwise equal. Valuation does not price voting premiums.
securityTerms.mandatoryConversionDateRule: Second business day after the last trading day of the final averaging period; date can shift under contractual market-disruption rules.
securityTerms.applicableMarketValueRule: Arithmetic average of daily VWAP over 20 consecutive trading days beginning with the 21st scheduled trading day immediately preceding May 15, 2029. Each class uses its own future average.
securityTerms.conversionFormula: Below initial price: maximum rate. From initial price through threshold: 1000 / applicable future class VWAP, rounded to 4 decimal places. Above threshold: minimum rate. Subject to anti-dilution and dividend additions.
securityTerms.fundamentalChanges: Certificates grant a holder fundamental-change conversion election with special rates and potentially dividend make-whole; these are outside the ordinary mandatory-conversion model. Do not treat the abbreviated 10-Q description as a complete legal payoff.
securityTerms.adjustmentsExcluded: Stock splits, extraordinary distributions, anti-dilution adjustments, early/fundamental-change conversion, default, and extra common shares for unpaid dividends.

preferredDividendModel.firstAmountPrecision: Model uses the July declaration as rounded in the 10-Q. Prospectuses provide the expected initial stub at approximately 12.1528. Using 12.1528 changes undiscounted aggregate dividends by only 0.0539 million. Neither source establishes subsequent actual payment in this review.
preferredDividendModel.recordDates: First day of February, May, August and November.
preferredDividendModel.paymentDateRule: Nominal 15th; actual payment rolls to the next New York bank business day if needed, without extra interest.
preferredDividendModel.stockSettlementRule: Issuer may deliver common shares at 97% of the relevant five-trading-day average price, subject to a floor and possible cash shortfall; unpaid dividends can add conversion shares. Cash settlement default does not cover this extra dilution.
preferredDividendModel.paymentTimingApproximation: Uses nominal quarterly dates. Does not price the small next-business-day settlement delay.
preferredDividendModel.discountRateClassification: Analyst assumption chosen for a transparent coupon-rate reference; NOT observed yield, fair-value rate, tax-adjusted WACC, or the contractual fundamental-change make-whole discount rate.
preferredDividendModel.accrualTreatment: The full initial future payment already includes the June 30 accumulated amount. Do not subtract the reported 86 again in conversion mode. Preferred dividends are financing distributions, not deductions from operating EBIT or FCFF.

cappedCalls.coveredSharesBasis: Common shares underlying the preferred at minimum conversion rates.
cappedCalls.defaultTreatment: No future capped-call asset or share offset is assumed; historical premium is already in June cash/equity and is never charged again. Zero future recovery is a conservative scenario assumption, not a finding that the options have no value.
cappedCalls.settlement: Issuer can elect cash settlement; otherwise generally common shares based on excess over strike, limited by cap. Counterparty risk applies.
cappedCalls.sensitivityFormulaOnly: At an explicitly assumed common future settlement price P, gross economic share offset approximation = minimum underlying shares * max(0, min(P, cap) - strike) / P. This ignores detailed averaging and adjustments; do not present it as observed option fair value.

recommendedBridge.baseEquation: E = EV + reported cash/current marketables + analyst other-asset values - reported debt - finance leases - NCI value - additional non-preferred claims. v = (E - preferred-dividend PV) / (12230 + incremental preferred conversion shares).
recommendedBridge.timingRationale: Conversion occurs inside the ten-year forecast. A static fully diluted denominator allocates all residual present equity to eventual shares, with no separately modeled preconversion common payouts. It is a transparent approximation to actual timed conversion, not an exact preferred fair-value calculation. Do not discount the number of conversion shares.
recommendedBridge.timingRefinement: If A is the present value of total common distributions before conversion, a consistent payout refinement is A/12230 + (E - dividendPV - A)/(12230 + q), holding other capital structure assumptions fixed. The default assumes A=0 for this allocation; it does not predict Alphabet will cease common dividends.
recommendedBridge.maxDilutionCaveat: Maximum contractual gross shares gives the lower positive value only with other inputs held fixed, cash-paid preferred dividends, unchanged conversion terms, and no cap-call recovery. It is not a universal economic lower bound.

conversionSensitivity.formulaDriven: Requires separately labeled future Class A and Class C VWAP assumptions, never substitutes current GOOG quote for both.

alternativeModes.label: Liquidation preference plus rounded accumulated dividends; not current market/fair value and not a complete liquidation appraisal of operating assets. Future preferred dividends do not survive liquidation.

alternativeModes.formula: 192.5m GOOGM depositaries * USD market price + 192.5m GOOGN depositaries * USD market price, with consistent clean/dirty dividend convention; or an explicitly labeled analyst total claim value.
requiredInputs: Date matching valuation balance basis, or an explicit complete roll-forward
Verified sources and depositary unit basis for both securities
Dividend entitlement and ex-dividend/dirty price convention
alternativeModes.capCallAsset: Value separately if verified; never deduct the historical premium again.
alternativeModes.warning: An entire preferred fair-value claim includes conversion rights and dividend rights; subtracting additional conversion dilution or the whole dividend PV would double-count.

recommendedBridge.investmentTreatment: Current cash bridge already includes 87063 of marketable equity. Noncurrent investments 145587 may be added as an explicitly selected gross carrying-value proxy with separate editable haircuts. Neither their full book value nor a zero haircut is a fair-value conclusion.
recommendedBridge.investmentTaxes: Gross asset proxy has no implied realization-tax allowance. Add an explicit analyst tax reserve if used. Total reported deferred tax liabilities 22819 cannot be assigned wholesale to these investments without evidence.
recommendedBridge.operatingLeaseTreatment: Keep operating lease expense in forecast operating profit; do not mechanically add operating lease liabilities as debt without restating operating profit and reinvestment consistently.
recommendedBridge.otherAwards: Quarterly weighted-average diluted EPS shares already include some preferred conversion effects and cannot be combined with full preferred conversion shares. Use actual June common count; existing employee awards require their own separately documented treatment.
recommendedBridge.numericPrecision: Retain calculation precision internally, but display valuation in sensible rounded dollars, not as exact security fair value. NCI/common counts and some dividends are rounded filing facts.

subsequentEvents.treatment: Known later financing is excluded from the June 30 balance-date valuation. Do not add only the new debt while retaining June cash; a current October value requires a complete cash/debt/capex and security roll-forward.
subsequentEvents.researchScope: Checked the available current SEC submissions listing and the August 10 closing 8-K. This is not a certification of every change through October 17 or a current quote.

doubleCountingChecks: Never subtract preferred carrying balance or liquidation principal in conversion mode.
Never add full preferred dilution to an entire market-valued preferred claim deduction.
Never add June preferred financing proceeds or charge June capped-call premium again.
Never add RNCI 824 separately from NCI 7100.
Never add current marketable equity 87063 again; it is within cash/current marketables 242474.
Never combine aggregate diluted EPS shares with full conversion shares.
Do not add all reported deferred taxes or operating lease debt mechanically.
limitations: No current GOOG, GOOGL, GOOGM or GOOGN quote was used or fabricated.
These scenarios resolve the mandatory preferred mechanics sufficiently for a conditional educational valuation; they do not certify complete fair market value.
Valuation uses June 30 balances and a forward forecast; October review date is not an October balance-sheet measurement.
Potential taxation, security restrictions, employee awards and uncommenced infrastructure commitments remain explicit modeling limitations.

companies.dossierMarkdown:
# Alphabet forecast and valuation dossier

**Research cutoff: October 17, 2026. Latest reported quarter: June 30, released July 22; 10-Q filed July 23. USD billions unless stated.** This dossier concerns Alphabet's common equity economic business, using GOOG as the research ticker; class-specific preferred conversion remains separate. Proposals are analytical inference, not issuer forecasts, consensus or price calibration. No Q3 2026 actuals are included.

## Decision-useful conclusion

Cloud acceleration and TPU hardware deliveries justify a three-year explicit growth phase, but the business is becoming more capital-intensive and financially complex. Proposed base revenue growth is **22%, 20%, 18% in years 1–3**, fading to **2.5% by year 15**, with **32% mature operating margin**, **22% normalized tax**, **10% WACC** and **16% terminal ROIC**. Early sales/incremental-capital ratios are **0.50, 0.55 and 0.60**, capturing capex and inventory pressure.

This path reaches **$770bn revenue in year 3 and $2.292tn by year 15**, with $733bn mature EBIT. That scale requires sustained global Search/AI monetization and a much larger Cloud market; it is not established by today's backlog. Maintain the preferred/asset/financing review gate. **No observed GOOG price was used to choose growth, margins, duration, capital efficiency or discount rates.**

## 1. Latest operating evidence and historical context

Q2 revenue was **$119.796bn, +24.2%**, operating income **$40.770bn**, and operating margin **34.03%**. Q1 revenue was $109.896bn, +21.8%; operating income $39.696bn. Net income is unsuitable for extrapolation: Q2 other income/expense was approximately $97.983bn, primarily unrealized investment gains. TTM revenue is **$445.866bn**, EBIT **$147.628bn**, margin **33.11%**. [Q2 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000071/goog-20260630.htm)

| Q2 2026 revenue category | Revenue | Share of total | Approximate year-on-year growth |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Search and other | 63.271 | 52.82% | 17% |
| YouTube advertising | 11.055 | 9.23% | 13% |
| Network | 7.303 | 6.10% | -1% |
| Subscriptions, platforms and devices | 12.911 | 10.78% | 15% |
| Google Cloud | 24.768 | 20.68% | 82% |
| Other Bets | 0.382 | 0.32% | — |

Google Services totals $94.540bn; it includes the first four rows, so it cannot be added again. Hedge revenue adds $0.106bn. Services EBIT was $39.544bn, Cloud $8.814bn, Other Bets loss $1.799bn and Alphabet-level loss $5.789bn. Cloud's **35.59% segment margin is not a fully loaded standalone AI return**, because significant shared AI R&D is recorded centrally. [Quarterly financial statements](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000071/goog-20260630.htm)

Annual revenue increased from $307.394bn in 2023 to $350.018bn in 2024 and $402.836bn in 2025. Cloud rose from $33.088bn to $43.229bn and $58.705bn. FY2025 Services revenue was $342.721bn; Cloud EBIT $13.910bn. Cloud is now a larger share of incremental growth, while Search remains the principal cash-generating business. The facts file contains 14 quarterly observations and three annual periods, retaining a $1m reported-rounding mismatch rather than force-fitting quarterly totals. [FY2025 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm)

## 2. Management outlook and readable evidence

### Capex revisions are material, and their causes differ

| Dated communication | Target | Capex outlook | Interpretation |
|---|---|---:|---|
| February 4, 2025 | FY2025 | Approximately 75 | Original budget |
| April 24, 2025 | FY2025 | Approximately 75 | Reaffirmed |
| July 23, 2025 | FY2025 | Approximately 85 | Delivery/construction timing |
| October 29, 2025 | FY2025 | 91–93 | Further capacity investment |
| February 4, 2026 | FY2026 | 175–185 | Original range |
| April 29, 2026 | FY2026 | 180–190 | Includes Intersect investment |
| July 22, 2026 | FY2026 | 195–205 | Accelerated capacity delivery |

FY2025 actual was $91.447bn: **21.93% above the initial approximate budget**, but within the last range. The revisions are separate forecast vintages against one annual outcome, not independent quarterly successes. FY2026 remains unresolved at cutoff. [Original 2025 outlook](https://abc.xyz/2024-q4-earnings-call/), [July 2025 revision](https://abc.xyz/2025-q2-earnings-call), [October 2025 transcript](https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_events/2025/Oct/29/2025_Q3_Earnings_Transcript.pdf)

The April call explicitly attributes the $5bn range increase to Intersect, completed in March; it also anticipates a significant increase in 2027. July raises the range another $15bn at its midpoint for capacity acceleration, again expects significant 2027 growth, and warns of depreciation, energy and other infrastructure expenses. Q3 use of third-party capacity is expected to put modest pressure on Cloud margins. [April 29 issuer transcript](https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_events/2026/Apr/29/Alphabet-2026_Q1_Earnings_Transcript.pdf), [July 22 issuer transcript](https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_events/2026/Jul/22/2026_Q2_Earnings_Transcript.pdf)

### Product and demand commentary

July management commentary says TPU system deliveries to customer data centers started in Q2, with a relatively small portion of existing-agreement revenue recognized in 2026 and the vast majority in 2027. These shipments can make revenue lumpy. Management also flags tougher Search comparisons and near-term FX effects. No numerical total-revenue or operating-income quarterly range is provided. [July call](https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_events/2026/Jul/22/2026_Q2_Earnings_Transcript.pdf)

**September 8, 2026: Thomas Kurian at Goldman Sachs Communacopia.** The issuer-hosted preliminary transcript was read; no video was watched. Kurian describes large-deal/customer growth and three TPU routes: cloud consumption, systems sold for customer facilities, and infrastructure-provider partnerships. Hardware sales can move facility/power investment to customers, but introduce inventory, delivery and contract-mix risks. He describes broad AI adoption and estimates better customer lifetime economics; these are management cohort estimates, not audited realized ROI. A moderator's promotional market-leadership characterization is not treated as market-share evidence. [Issuer-hosted interview](https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_events/2026/Sep/08/Thomas-Kurian-Goldman-Sachs-Communacopia-09-08-26.pdf)

Issuer calls from Q4 2023 through Q2 2026 were reviewed for outlook, capex and relevant business commentary. The source ledger identifies exact event dates and text coverage. Their transcripts are readable issuer material; no investor-day revenue target was substituted where none was found.

### Guidance track record: do not manufacture a hit rate

The record contains **11 consecutive earnings communications**. Alphabet did not provide numerical next-quarter total-revenue or EBIT ranges in these reviewed calls. That absence is recorded as **not provided**, never zero. It would be misleading to construct a CEO revenue accuracy score from sell-side estimates or reported growth.

Quantified capex observations are scored with their original semantics: approximately $12bn-or-more quarterly levels in 2024 are floors, not narrow ranges; approximately $13bn for Q4 2024 is a point with no invented tolerance; the Q1 2025 $16–18bn range contains actual capex. Directional FY2024 operating-margin expansion was delivered. The exit-2024 YouTube-plus-Cloud run-rate target exceeded $100bn and management subsequently reported $110bn; that combined measure includes YouTube subscriptions and must not be checked against YouTube advertising alone. [2024 Q1 outlook](https://abc.xyz/2024-q1-earnings-call/), [2024 Q3 outlook](https://abc.xyz/2024-q3-earnings-call/), [2024 Q4 results/outlook](https://abc.xyz/2024-q4-earnings-call/)

## 3. Capital, cash conversion and operating quality

**Capacity and depreciation.** H1 capex was **$80.598bn**, including Q2 $44.924bn; H1 physical depreciation was $13.586bn. TTM capex $132.402bn exceeds TTM depreciation $25.237bn by over $107bn before working capital, leases and acquisitions. June net PPE was $321.212bn. A one-parameter sales/capital model must not confuse depreciation lag with permanently high free cash generation.

**Working capital.** H1 inventory absorbed **$7.739bn cash**, receivables $6.904bn and other assets $9.950bn, partially offset by payables, accrued liabilities, customer liabilities and taxes. TPU systems are not just a renamed subscription business: control-transfer hardware recognition, returns, installation/support obligations and inventory economics matter. H1 OCF was $84.859bn and FCF **$4.261bn**. Q2 OCF $39.069bn minus capex $44.924bn produced negative $5.855bn FCF. [Q2 cash flows and revenue policy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000071/goog-20260630.htm)

**Acquisitions.** Wiz closed March 11 for about $29.5bn after adjustments, excluding post-combination compensation; Intersect closed March 10 for about $5.9bn. These are not entirely organic growth or ordinary PPE purchases. Wiz creates amortization/compensation effects, and Intersect adds capacity and energy development. Model acquisition investment separately from the compressed organic sales/capital proxy.

**SBC and share count.** H1 cash-flow SBC add-back was $14.708bn, while the allocated expense disclosure rounds to $15.2bn. Do not equate the two definitions. TTM cash-flow SBC was $28.147bn. Common shares were **12,230m at June** versus 12,088m at December; H1 diluted weighted average 12,274m. There were no H1 common repurchases. Do not automatically carry historical buyback-driven per-share accretion into this financing regime.

**Margins, tax and ROIC.** The proposed mature 32% margin is below current TTM 33.11%, allowing for AI compute, energy, hardware mix and central research. A normalized 22% tax rate is an inference; huge investment marks and deferred tax changes distort current effective rates. The terminal 16% ROIC assumes durable intellectual-property/distribution advantages but meaningful physical capital. No audited marginal return for the latest AI build is available, and segment EBIT omits shared costs. Therefore, a precise historical incremental AI ROIC is not claimed.

## 4. Backlog, financing and unresolved common-share claims

June total backlog was **$519.5bn**, including **$513.9bn Cloud**. Management expects just over 50% to be recognized over the next 24 months. Timing depends on duration, delivery and utilization; amounts include deferred revenue and future invoices, exclude cancellable contracts and include TPU hardware arrangements. This supports visibility but is not a guaranteed annualized service run-rate or an asset to add separately to enterprise value.

June cash/current marketables totaled **$242.474bn**, but included **$87.063bn marketable equity**, of which $80bn was restricted SpaceX. Additional noncurrent investments totaled **$145.587bn**. These are valuation-sensitive investments, not interchangeable operating cash; current equity must not be added a second time. Debt carrying value was $100.164bn; finance leases $2.590bn; operating leases $18.037bn. Uncommenced leases were **$85.2bn undiscounted**; another **$5.8bn short-term capacity commitment** starts in Q3.

The financing structure changed materially. Common and mandatory-convertible preferred capital were raised in H1. Preferred legal liquidation preference is **$19.25bn**, while the balance-sheet book amount is $18.023bn after issuance/capped-call effects. The 6.25% preferred converts using class-specific future VWAP formulas, with ordinary gross common dilution approximately **43.56–54.46m shares**, before dividend/adjustment effects. A $40bn ATM authorization was unsold at June. The existing detailed preferred review must be retained; do not combine a full preferred-principal deduction with full conversion dilution. Do not assume book value equals fair value or claim capped calls remove every dilution outcome.

Data-center credit backstops had **$43.785bn notional maximum exposure**, energy-infrastructure guarantees approximately **$7.6bn maximum potential payments**, and contingent strategic funding equity derivatives **$20bn notional**. The amounts are not expected losses or automatically current debt: default triggers, lease takeover/sublease rights, termination rights, timing and recorded derivative liabilities matter. They are also not zero-risk footnotes. August debt issuance requires a matched cash/proceeds/uses bridge if moving beyond the June anchor. [Q2 notes on investments, derivatives, leases, debt and equity](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000071/goog-20260630.htm)

## 5. Scenarios, confidence and invalidators

| Inferred scenario | Early growth, years 1–3 | Maturity | Mature margin | WACC | Terminal ROIC | Terminal growth |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Base | 22%, 20%, 18% | 15 years | 32% | 10% | 16% | 2.5% |
| Bull stress | 30%, 28%, 24% | 20 years | 36% | 9.25% | 20% | 2.75% |
| Bear | 12%, 8%, 6% | 10 years | 26% | 11.5% | 9% | 2% |

The base first-year growth cross-check uses roughly 60% Cloud growth on a 17.4% TTM revenue weight and 14% elsewhere, producing about 22%. This is an inference from demand/capacity evidence, not a company forecast. The mature sales/capital ratio is linked algebraically to terminal ROIC and after-tax margin, rather than independently selecting incompatible favorable assumptions.

The bull stress reaches **$6.900tn revenue and $2.484tn EBIT**, a very demanding 15.5-times scale expansion. It is an upper-bound duration/market-expansion stress, not a central planning case. The bear reaches $738bn revenue. No probability weights are assigned. WACC uses the common verified October 16 Treasury input of 5.09%, with a chosen 4.5% ERP and assumed beta/financing mix; these latter inputs are not observed forward returns.

Weaken the base if Search growth drops below mid-single digits while compute/TAC rises; backlog conversion materially misses management's 24-month timing; TPU hardware carries inferior margins or inventory risks; 2027 capex grows without cash conversion; capital raises persistently dilute common owners; or regulatory/competitive changes impair distribution and ad monetization. Regulatory outcomes are scenario risks, not invented quantified liabilities.

## Deliverables and limits

The companion files preserve all financial observations, source IDs and fetch/read status, guidance vintages, annual scenario paths, qualitative management capabilities and an explicit asset/obligation register. New AI capital returns, private investment fair values, credit-loss probabilities and October balance-sheet changes remain uncertain. No full commercial transcript is stored, no video viewing is claimed and no GOOG price fit was performed.

# Meta Platforms forecast dossier

Research cutoff: 17 October 2026. Currency: USD. Financial amounts below are billions unless stated otherwise. This is a bounded evidence review, not every historical management statement. The structured files contain exact dates, units, source identifiers and scenario calculations.

## Conclusion

The core advertising franchise supports strong near-term growth, but the capital and legal commitments make a simple extrapolation of 2025 margins and free cash flow unreliable. Proposed base revenue growth is 20%, 18%, 16% in the first three forecast years, then a rate fade to 2.5% by year 10. The proposed mature EBIT margin is 33%, normalized tax 20%, direct early capital-spend/D&A/working-capital assumptions (derived S:C approximately 0.34, 0.36, 0.39, followed by normalization and a terminal-consistent transition), WACC 10%, and terminal ROIC 12%. These are our assumptions, not management forecasts. Forecast year one is the rolling year after June 2026, not calendar 2026. The claims bridge remains unresolved, so these are operating-value scenarios rather than finished share-price targets.

## Evidence and business mix

- Latest reported quarter: Q2 2026, released 29 July. Revenue $60.801bn grew 28% reported and 27% in constant currency. Advertising was $59.363bn, 97.6% of revenue. Impressions grew 14% and average price 12%; daily active people were 3.6bn, up 3%. This supports an engagement/monetization explanation, not an invented standalone AI revenue stream. Other Family of Apps revenue was $1.007bn; Reality Labs revenue $0.431bn. [Quarterly release](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx)
- FY2025 revenue was $200.966bn and EBIT $83.276bn. Reality Labs lost $19.193bn on $2.207bn revenue. TTM revenue through June 2026 was $228.247bn and EBIT $86.926bn, a 38.1% margin. Quarterly standalone revenue, EBIT and SBC sums differ from filed year-to-date figures by $1m; the filed YTD-based TTM is the anchor. [2025 annual release](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx), [June filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026050705/meta-20260630.htm)
- Q2 EBIT was $18.775bn, a 30.9% reported margin. The quarter included $2.400bn legal expense and $1.180bn severance; removing only those identified items gives about 36.8%. This is an analytical normalization, not reported EBIT. SBC was $7.658bn and D&A $6.356bn. Ongoing SBC remains an expense in valuation. Q2 capex including finance-lease principal was $31.078bn, leaving reported FCF only $0.784bn. [Quarterly release](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx)

## Guidance and management commentary

July formal guidance put Q3 revenue at $61–64bn, with an approximately 1% FX headwind; FY2026 capex at $130–145bn and expenses at $165–169bn. The August legal agreement adds approximately $10bn Q3 legal expense that was not included in July expense guidance. Other July guidance ranges were stated to be unchanged. Do not keep July's profitability interpretation without this update. [July release](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx), [26 August update](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Metas-Agreement-With-Bipartisan-Attorneys-General-Calling-on-TikTok-and-YouTube-to-Join-Us-in-Supporting-Teens/default.aspx)

Issuer-hosted July earnings and follow-up transcripts were read, not videos watched. Management described AI improvements to engagement, ad ranking and monetization; messaging, subscriptions and business agents are additional opportunities. Capacity procurement is aimed at 2026–27 constraints, with lower visibility beyond 2028 and more flexible land/power/shell commitments. No quantified 2027 capex outlook was supplied. The CEO's 2025 personal-superintelligence letter is strategic ambition rather than a financial forecast. [Earnings transcript](https://s21.q4cdn.com/399680738/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/META-Q2-2026-Earnings-Call-Transcript.pdf), [follow-up transcript](https://s21.q4cdn.com/399680738/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/META-Q2-2026-Follow-Up-Call-Transcript.pdf), [CEO letter](https://www.meta.com/superintelligence/)

## Guidance track record and management capabilities

The original next-quarter revenue range was matched to actual revenue for 12 consecutive target quarters, Q3 2023 through Q2 2026. Seven outcomes exceeded the high end, five were within range, and none were below. Mean midpoint error was +3.72%. This is evidence of conservative short-horizon revenue guidance, not proof of reliable decade-long AI returns. The original 2025 capex range of $60–65bn was repeatedly raised; actual capex including finance-lease principal was $72.215bn. Revenue accuracy and capital-spend forecasting deserve different assessments.

Mark Zuckerberg was CEO throughout this sample. Susan Li was CFO throughout, having taken office on 1 November 2022. Attribution is to the management system and business, not a personality score. The five-dimension capability file records evidence and counterexamples: strong core ad monetization and conservative quarterly revenue forecasts; uncertain new AI/Reality Labs product returns and capacity economics; historical cost leverage now facing substantial spending pressure.

## Capital, accounting and claims

- Most server/network useful lives became 5.5 years from January 2025, reducing 2025 depreciation by $2.920bn and increasing net income by $2.590bn. Longer accounting lives do not reduce cash replacement costs. [2025 annual filing, Note 1](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm)
- June cash and marketables were $90.260bn and debt carrying value $83.664bn. Nonmarketable equity investments were $30.157bn; $13.809bn restricted cash should not be treated as freely distributable. Asset carrying values require a valuation/tax assessment, not automatic dollar-for-dollar inclusion. [June filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026050705/meta-20260630.htm)
- The filing reports $278.990bn not-yet-commenced lease obligations, another $68bn of July leases, and $349.310bn noncancelable contractual commitments. These categories must be checked for overlap. They belong in a cash-cost/reinvestment schedule or consistent lease treatment, not mechanically summed as debt. Cloud-capacity support of up to $14.720bn and venture residual-value guarantees are conditional exposures. [June filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026050705/meta-20260630.htm)
- The El Paso venture targets 1GW online in 2028. Meta owns 20%, BlackRock 80%; approximately $14bn is long-lived development cost, with servers additional. The initial lease is four years with extension options up to 20 years. Low initial equity funding does not eliminate future rent or guarantee exposure. [28 July issuer announcement](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Announces-New-Strategic-Venture-with-BlackRock-to-Develop-Data-Center-in-El-Paso/default.aspx)
- The proposed state settlement is approximately $18bn over ten years: about $12.7bn committed and $5.3bn conditional on specified TikTok/YouTube actions and contributions. Judicial approval was pending in the announcement. Under an illustrative equal year-end installment assumption and 10% discount rate, the committed portion is worth about $7.8bn today; this is not a disclosed payment schedule. Do not both deduct that PV and include the same cash payments in forecast FCFF. [26 August announcement](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Metas-Agreement-With-Bipartisan-Attorneys-General-Calling-on-TikTok-and-YouTube-to-Join-Us-in-Supporting-Teens/default.aspx)

## Forecast interpretation and limits

The base reaches approximately $652bn revenue in year 10, 2.85 times the June TTM base. The bear reaches $371bn; the conditional 15-year bull $1.304tn. These are scale checks, not total-addressable-market evidence. The file also shows all six combinations of 3/5 explicit years and 10/15/20 maturity horizons, as constant-S:C duration diagnostics. These diagnostic values omit the selected scenarios' final capital transition and are not identical to the selected base. Longer runway must be supported economically; it is not a free valuation uplift.

At the illustrative base settings, operating enterprise value is about $800bn before the cash/debt/investment/legal/contingent-claim bridge. Roughly 90% comes from discounted terminal value, so terminal assumptions and capital efficiency dominate the result. The bear includes fixed near-term reinvestment floors because committed construction does not disappear when ad growth slows. Those floors and lease/depreciation schedules are model gaps in a single sales-to-capital implementation.

Invalidate or lower confidence if ad growth repeatedly falls below 10%, capacity spending fails to improve monetization, normalized margin stays below 30%, spending commitments exceed modeled cash generation, or legal/venture claims crystallize beyond the scenarios. The current evidence does not establish October cash balances, the precise settlement schedule, all contract overlap or realized returns on the AI buildout. No current share price was used to fit the assumptions.

## Capital and funding refinement

The first three base years now use the [direct capital and cash-funding reconciliation](shared-evidence.html#meta-tesla-funding-reconciliation-narrative), rather than a fixed early sales-to-capital ratio. Economic FCFF retains SBC expense; the separate cash view accounts for noncash SBC and employee share-settlement cash. The central three-year cash proxy needs about $77.8bn before interest, dividends and legal payments, versus $90.3bn June cash/marketables. This is a conditional planning range, not an additional debt deduction.

companies.dossierMarkdown:
# NVIDIA forecast and valuation dossier
As of 2026-10-17. Financial amounts in USD unless indicated. This is research, with provisional scenario proposals and unresolved valuation gates, not a per-share recommendation.

## What changes the base case
The current operating ramp warrants a steeper early revenue path than the old flat 40% input, but financing support and supplier commitments now warrant an equally explicit downside model. The latest quarter was $96.221bn revenue, 106% year-over-year growth and $63.734bn GAAP operating income. Latest TTM revenue/EBIT were $302.970bn/$197.579bn. A low reported physical-capex ratio no longer captures the whole economic commitment.

The [August 26 issuer results](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/) and [original Q2 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000075/nvda-20260726.htm) are the primary anchors. FY2027 Q2 ended July 26. FY2027 has 53 weeks, including a 14-week Q4; this matters when comparing annual growth.

## Business and trajectory
Data Center was $89.023bn, 92.5% of quarterly revenue; Edge Computing $7.198bn. Hyperscale $48.710bn and ACIE $40.313bn subdivide Data Center. Compute & Networking $88.299bn and Graphics $7.922bn are a different reportable-segment classification. Do not add across classifications. Prior market presentation was recast and one ACIE customer moved into hyperscale in Q2. On that latest recast basis, Q1 FY2027 Data Center/Edge were $75.246bn/$6.370bn, versus $41.096bn/$5.647bn in Q2 FY2026. The full preceding-quarter mix series and derivations are in evidence-NVDA.html#facts.

Annual revenue grew 125.9% in FY2024, 114.2% in FY2025 and 65.5% in FY2026; GAAP EBIT margins were 54.1%, 62.4% and 60.4%. The latest TTM margin is 65.2%. These are extraordinary cycle/platform economics, not a credible perpetual extrapolation. Annual source-level financial history, capex, tax, R&D, SBC and capital proxies are retained in evidence-NVDA.html#facts.

## Management outlook and revisions
The [August 26 corrected earnings-call text](https://investor.nvidia.com/files/content_files/TRANSCRIPT_-NVIDIA-Corp-NVDA-US-Q2-2027-Earnings-Call-26-August-2026-5_00-PM-ET.pdf) gives Q3 revenue $108bn ±2%, excluding China Data Center compute. Management discussed preliminary FY2028 growth around 70%, constrained by supply. That remains an unseasoned forecast, not an actual or analyst consensus.

Rising memory costs changed the margin outlook: Q4 FY2027 gross margin 71–72%, followed by FY2028 72–73% after price increases. This should flow into EBIT forecasts. Rubin production shipments reportedly began in August, consistent with the preceding May call's Q3 start expectation; shipment timing is management-reported, not independently audited. Corporate revenue guidance, product visibility and broad customer-capex estimates have different scopes.

The November 19, 2025 Blackwell-plus-Rubin $500bn calendar-2025/2026 visibility statement cannot yet be scored against full-year corporate revenue. Industry cloud backlog, customer capex and the August third-party financing target are not NVIDIA backlog. September 10 Jensen Huang conference Q&A was read as a public transcript; no video was watched. His confidence in compute-asset fungibility and physical AI is a thesis requiring evidence, not a quantitative quarterly target.

## Like-for-like guidance record
| Target period | Original date | Revenue guide, $bn | Actual, $bn | Error vs midpoint/point | Result |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| FY2025Q1 | 2024-02-21 | 24.000 ±2% | 26.044 | 8.52% | above |
| FY2025Q2 | 2024-05-22 | 28.000 ±2% | 30.040 | 7.29% | above |
| FY2025Q3 | 2024-08-28 | 32.500 ±2% | 35.082 | 7.94% | above |
| FY2025Q4 | 2024-11-20 | 37.500 ±2% | 39.331 | 4.88% | above |
| FY2026Q1 | 2025-02-26 | 43.000 ±2% | 44.062 | 2.47% | above |
| FY2026Q2 | 2025-05-28 | 45.000 ±2% | 46.743 | 3.87% | above |
| FY2026Q3 | 2025-08-27 | 54.000 ±2% | 57.006 | 5.57% | above |
| FY2026Q4 | 2025-11-19 | 65.000 ±2% | 68.127 | 4.81% | above |
| FY2027Q1 | 2026-02-25 | 78.000 ±2% | 81.615 | 4.63% | above |
| FY2027Q2 | 2026-05-20 | 91.000 ±2% | 96.221 | 5.74% | above |

All ten original revenue ranges were exceeded; mean signed midpoint error was +5.57%. This supports conservative short-horizon revenue guidance during this ramp, rather than exact unbiased demand prediction. Seven of ten GAAP gross-margin outcomes were inside guidance, two above and one below. FY2026 Q1 was 60.5% versus 70.6% ±0.5 points after H20 export restrictions: retain that 10.1-point miss. Non-GAAP definitions changed in FY2027 to retain SBC, so the matched margin series uses GAAP. Exact sources, actual publication dates and errors appear in evidence-NVDA.html#guidance. No longer-horizon CEO credibility score or valuation multiplier is inferred.

## Cash investment, accounting and returns
Six-month CFO was $74.421bn; physical/intangible purchases $4.434bn, D&A $2.124bn and SBC $3.954bn. Receivables and inventories absorbed $34.794bn combined before other working-capital changes. Payment terms can extend 90 days to one year for investment-grade customers. Equity purchases were another $42.404bn; these are not ordinary capex, but are real capital deployed into an ecosystem linked to product demand. Reported net income includes large investment gains; use operating EBIT for enterprise valuation.

Historical book ROIC and incremental sales/capital proxies are useful diagnostics, not adjusted economic returns: they omit capitalized R&D, complete lease/guarantee exposure and a clean separation of nonoperating assets. A 2x forward incremental sales/capital assumption is therefore judgment, requiring cash-flow and capacity reconciliation. Do not release capital mechanically in a revenue contraction while purchase obligations remain.

## Obligations and asset bridge: unresolved
The [issuer 10-Q, Note 12](https://investor.nvidia.com/files/doc_financials/2027/NVDA-2027-Q2-10Q-Final-including-exhibits.pdf) separates own-use commitments from customer support. The register in evidence-NVDA.html#judgment records measurement date, source, conditionality and proposed treatment for every following item:
- $366bn own-use investment/procurement commitments: $279bn supply/capacity, $29bn cloud, $25bn future leases, $25bn equity investments and $8bn capex.
- Additional $36bn AI-cloud agreements and $20bn third-party leases intended for reassignment. Capacity sales/use may reduce the former; reassignment of the latter is intended, not guaranteed.
- $3.529bn existing land/power/shell guarantees and $712m partner escrow; default-triggered with declining exposure.
- August $105bn SB Energy/OpenAI guarantee cap, for nine phases of 4.25GW. First phase expected FY2029; covered obligations run over 20-year leases, decline and have defined termination conditions. Another 3.8GW is discretionary. This is not $105bn funded debt, nor harmless merely because no payment is currently due.
- $33.366bn debt; $5.494bn recognized operating leases; $986m accrued Groq consideration; $56.586bn cash/current debt securities before operating-liquidity review.
- $42.783bn marketable equity, $47.898bn nonmarketable equity and $3.3bn equity-method investments require after-tax realizable valuation. Do not add investment gains to EBIT and then add assets again.
- 168m outstanding unvested awards, versus 24.1bn cover shares on August 21. Unrecognized compensation $19.4bn is not award fair value.

The August 10 financing MOUs seek over $500bn of third-party capital over time. They are not NVIDIA cash, debt or signed customer revenue. Default probability, construction phase, recovery and correlation with operating downside are needed to value conditional support. Missing additional claims/assets remain null, not zero.

## Provisional scenarios and implied scale
| Scenario | Early years / annual growth | Total years | Mature revenue, $bn | Mature EBIT margin | Sales/capital | Tax | WACC | Terminal ROIC |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| base | 3: 80%/45%/25% | 10 | 2,179.4 | 45% | 2.0x | 20% | 11% | 25% |
| bull | 5: 95%/65%/35%/25%/18% | 15 | 4,759.9 | 53% | 2.4x | 20% | 10% | 30% |
| bear | 3: 50%/5%/-10% | 10 | 348.9 | 30% | 1.5x | 20% | 13% | 15% |

All scenarios fade linearly after their explicit early years to 2.5% terminal growth. Base EBIT margins are 62/59/56% in years 1–3, then fade to 45% by year 10. Years are rolling 12-month periods after July 26, not fiscal labels. Fiscal cross-check: actual H1 $177.837bn + Q3 guide $108bn + analyst Q4 $120bn gives FY2027 $405.837bn; management's 70% would imply FY2028 about $690bn. This is a cross-check, not a validated quarterly bridge.

The base's $2.18trn mature sales and bull's $4.76trn are demanding scale requirements, not concealed outputs. A 10-year base is preferred over 15/20 because customer economics beyond the current platform cycle are uncertain. The bull's longer runway tests durable full-stack expansion. Terminal ROIC requires reinvestment, rather than treating terminal profit as entirely distributable. Base WACC 11% is judgment, informed by October 16 USD10-year Treasury 5.09% and chosen ERP 4.5%; no current measured beta or credit spread is claimed. Normalize operating tax at 20% rather than automatically perpetuating management's near-term 16–18%.

## Management strengths and invalidators
The evidence supports rapid product monetization, supplier coordination and operating leverage. It is weaker on the realized returns of recent financing support and strategic investments, which have not seasoned. Jensen Huang and Colette Kress led throughout the matched period, but outcomes belong to the team and environment. Export controls, customer monetization, financing deterioration, memory/power constraints, custom silicon and extended receivables are primary invalidators. Review evidence-NVDA.html#management for dimension-specific evidence and counterexamples.

## Source limitations and adoption gate
Primary releases, annual/current filings, issuer-hosted call text, investor/keynote materials and a public leadership Q&A were inspected. No audio/video was watched. Some interview pages failed; no paywall bypass was attempted. Analyst consensus was not collected. evidence-NVDA.html#sources distinguishes source types and gaps. These proposals remain research illustrations until segment/fiscal, cash-investment, conditional-credit, tax/lease and share/asset bridges are reconciled. No app default was edited and no price calibration was used.

rationale.growth: The old40% next-TTM assumption is difficult to reconcile with Q3$108bn and management preliminaryFY28+70%.80/45/25% staged next-TTM growth recognizes an elevated ramp while fading much faster after year3; it is not a direct70% transcription. Near-term fiscal reference: H1FY27 actual177.837bn + Q3guide108bn + analyticalQ4 120bn impliesFY27~405.837bn; management70% FY28 would imply~689.9bn. A nextTTM of545.346bn lies between those fiscal totals and remains conditional.
rationale.earlyHorizon: 3 years capture current Blackwell/Rubin ramp and a subsequent adoption window; ten-year total is preferred to15/20 because visibility beyond the current platform/customer-capex cycle is weak. Bull15-year persistence tests a sustained platform, not higher certainty.
rationale.margin: Explicit annual operating margin should be62/59/56% in years1–3 then fade to45% byyear10, reflecting memory gross-margin guidance72–73%, compute/R&D cost, and scarcity normalization. GAAP margin afterSBC/DA; investment gains excluded.
rationale.reinvestment: 2x incremental sales/net reinvestment is a forward judgment. Cash-flow AR/inventory growth and project support mean fabless does not imply capital-free; separate long-lived strategic investment and guarantee analysis is required.
rationale.tax: 20% normalized versus16–18% FY27 management outlook; all model tax rates are operating assumptions.
rationale.discount: 11% nominalUSD retained as a rounded risk judgment, not a live regression; test10–13%. Do not lower it mechanically because management beat near-term guidance.
rationale.terminal: 2.5% nominal growth and25% terminalROIC preserve a substantial moat but force reinvestment10% of terminalNOPAT. No terminal ROIC equals historical book proxy.
rationale.claims: Keep bridge gated. Review debt, leases, awards, strategic equity, financing guarantees and post-quarter arrangements; null additional claims/assets means unresolved, not zero.

analystJudgment.guidanceUse: Strong10-quarter record permits giving the stated near-term ramp substantial evidentiary weight. It does not justify a CEO premium, indefinite growth or blind acceptance of unseasonedFY28 forecasts.

companies.dossierMarkdown:
# Tesla forecast dossier

Research cutoff: 17 October 2026. Currency: USD. Financial amounts are billions unless stated otherwise. Thirteen issuer shareholder updates were acquired; twelve consecutive outlook sections from Q3 2023 to Q2 2026 were reviewed for guidance policy. This is bounded coverage, not every historical statement.

## Conclusion

Tesla requires an explicit capital-spending and contingent-dilution model before a renewed share-price default. The latest quarter's 26% revenue growth coexists with a 1.4% operating margin and more than $25bn planned 2026 capex. A base case of 12%, 12%, 10% initial growth and eventual 10% EBIT margin requires a recovery in vehicle economics and growth in energy/services; major Robotaxi or Optimus profits remain conditional. A constant sales-to-capital ratio cannot faithfully represent both the present buildout and later capital normalization.

The old debt input also needs a verified correction: $7.721bn is long-term debt, not total debt. The June filing adds $1.340bn current debt and $0.281bn finance leases, for $9.342bn debt plus finance leases. No application files were changed. [June filing, debt table](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026049270/tsla-20260630.htm)

## Actual business mix and current evidence

Q2 2026 revenue was $28.236bn: automotive $20.516bn, energy $3.139bn, services/other $4.581bn. EBIT was $0.398bn, SBC $1.151bn, D&A $1.619bn, operating cash flow $4.697bn and cash capex $5.789bn. Revenue growth was 26%, automotive 23%, energy 13% and services/other 50%. TTM revenue through June was $103.619bn and EBIT $4.372bn, a 4.2% margin. Automotive was 73.0% of TTM revenue, energy 12.4%, services/other 14.6%. Services revenue is not synonymous with high-margin software. [Q2 issuer update](https://assets-ir.tesla.com/tesla-contents/IR/TSLA-Q2-2026-Update.pdf), [June filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026049270/tsla-20260630.htm)

FY2025 deliveries were 1,636,129 versus 1,789,226 in 2024 and 1,808,581 in 2023. Energy deployments grew from 14.7GWh in 2023 to 31.4GWh in 2024 and 46.7GWh in 2025. FY2025 revenue was $94.827bn and EBIT $4.355bn. [2025 update](https://assets-ir.tesla.com/tesla-contents/IR/TSLA-Q4-2025-Update.pdf)

The 2 October announcement gives Q3 2026 production of 464,391 vehicles, deliveries of 486,532 and 13.7GWh deployed. Q3 deliveries were 2.1% below Q3 2025. This is operating data only. Financial results are scheduled for 21 October, after the research cutoff; Q3 revenue, margin and cash flow are not yet known. [Operating announcement](https://ir.tesla.com/press-release/tesla-third-quarter-2026-production-deliveries-and-deployments)

## Guidance, interviews and product milestones

No formal numerical quarterly consolidated revenue or EBIT range was found in the twelve consecutive shareholder outlooks reviewed. This means no comparable quarterly revenue-guidance score is available, not a 0% accuracy score. Annual volume/energy guidance and product timelines must be assessed separately.

- The 2023 approximately 1.8m vehicle target appears in a production outlook. Actual production was approximately 1.846m, about 2.6% above that approximate target. Deliveries are a different metric.
- October 2024's expectation of slight delivery growth for 2024 missed: deliveries fell 1.1%. Its expectation that energy deployments would more than double was met, with 113.6% growth.
- January 2025's return-to-growth vehicle outlook missed on both deliveries and automotive revenue. The at-least-50% energy deployment expectation was narrowly missed at 48.7%. April guidance was withdrawn amid trade-policy uncertainty; preserve that revision separately rather than erase the original promise.
- The first-half-2025 affordable-model initial-production milestone was met by June first builds. That does not establish volume sales. Cybercab initial production in 2026 does not by itself satisfy a volume-production target. Semi/Megapack 3 volume/start milestones remain pending as of the cutoff.

The files preserve original forecast dates, definitions, revisions and outcome sources. Do not compare a selected long-range Musk product promise with Jensen Huang's short-quarter revenue range as if they were the same forecasting task.

The original World Economic Forum publisher's January 2026 interview metadata and accessible indexed transcript portions were read. Musk discussed possible public Optimus sales by the end of 2027, conditional on reliability, safety and functionality, and power constraints on AI. The full video was not watched; the page's full transcript was not accessible in rendered text. These are conditional future aspirations, not formal revenue guidance or overdue promises. [Original WEF interview](https://www.weforum.org/podcasts/meet-the-leader/conversation-with-elon-musk-davos-2026)

A public secondary Q2 call transcript was also read. The CFO described more than $25bn 2026 capex, further growth over the following two to three years, and possible borrowing facilities up to $30bn. The latter is financing intent, not drawn debt. Remarks also explain warranty/tariff effects, subscription mix and uncertain new-product ramps. No full commercial transcript was copied; financial claims are anchored to the issuer deck and filing where available. [Public transcript](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/tsla/transcripts/653184-q2-2026/)

The issuer's 17 July analyst survey is an analyst estimate snapshot, not management guidance and not current October consensus. It is retained only with that label. [Dated survey](https://ir.tesla.com/press-release/earnings-consensus-second-quarter-2026)

## Management capability assessment

Elon Musk was CEO throughout the reviewed period. Vaibhav Taneja became CFO on 4 August 2023; Zachary Kirkhorn preceded him. Outcome attribution must also consider engineering, operations, policy, price competition and product mix. [Appointment filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000095017023038779/tsla-20230804.htm)

The evidence supports successful energy capacity expansion and some initial production milestones. It is weaker for recent annual vehicle-demand forecasts and for assuming that announced autonomy/robotics capacity will translate promptly into profitable customer revenue. Cost control is mixed: high revenue growth has not produced consolidated operating leverage. Capital allocation into autonomy, robotics and outside investments has substantial optionality but not yet an observable incremental return sufficient to support a blanket credibility premium. The capability matrix provides a counterexample and confidence level for each dimension.

## Capital, financing and dilution

- More than $25bn gross 2026 capex is stated in the June filing. Net reinvestment is gross capex minus economic depreciation plus working-capital and other operating investment. It cannot be equated directly to capex, and it cannot fall automatically to zero when revenue is flat. [June filing, MD&A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026049270/tsla-20260630.htm)
- June cash/investments were $43.524bn. SpaceX investment carrying value was $3.007bn on $2.002bn cost; the $1.005bn mark-up was below EBIT. Digital assets were $0.674bn. These are separate nonoperating assets, with valuation, tax and liquidity uncertainty. Nonredeemable NCI was $0.607bn and redeemable NCI $0.054bn. [June filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026049270/tsla-20260630.htm)
- Approximately 304m 2018 CEO options were exercised during Q2, with roughly 17.5m shares used in net exercise settlement; resulting restricted shares have a January 2028 service condition. The 96m interim 2025 shares were forfeited in April. Do not count the forfeited interim award or the exercised option claim again. Cover-page common shares were 3,949,547,394 on 16 July. [June filing, awards and cover page](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026049270/tsla-20260630.htm)
- The 2025 CEO award covers up to 423,743,904 restricted performance shares in twelve tranches, requiring market-cap and operating milestones, service periods and an offset of $334.09 per share unless paid in cash. It is neither an unconditional 423.7m extra shares nor a zero economic claim. Issued/restricted shares, potential forfeiture, offsets and share-count treatment must be reconciled before valuation. [June filing, compensation note](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026049270/tsla-20260630.htm)

## Forecast proposal and what would invalidate it

The base's 12%, 12%, 10% initial revenue growth is an analytical mix-based recovery assumption. Year one is the rolling year after June 2026, not calendar 2026. At the TTM mix, roughly 8% automotive growth and 20% growth in energy and services imply about 11.2% consolidated growth. Growth fades to 2.5% by year 10, reaching about $211bn revenue. The 10% target operating margin, 25% normalized tax, 12% WACC and 12% terminal ROIC are judgments, not management guidance. A 15-year conditional bull reaches approximately $686bn and requires materially more software-heavy paid autonomy economics.

Near-term capital intensity is modeled separately from eventual normalization, with a final fade to capital efficiency consistent with terminal ROIC. The structured scenario file preserves the highly capital-intensive constant-S:C diagnostic as well as the proposed normalization path. This distinction is material: ongoing heavy capital spending without high-margin autonomous services consumes most operating value. The bear retains explicit near-term investment floors. A negative operating-value diagnostic signals that the assumed investment program is not self-funding; equity has abandonment, financing and business-model options that a mechanical negative DCF does not capture.

All six 3/5-year early-phase and 10/15/20-year horizon combinations are shown as duration sensitivities. Twenty years of elevated growth is not justified merely because the controls permit it. No share price was used to fit inputs.

The base fails if vehicle volume/price economics do not recover, energy costs and warranties erode margins, capital spending stays elevated without cash returns, or autonomy cannot demonstrate paid utilization and acceptable safety/intervention performance. The historical promise sample is bounded, older autonomy promises were not exhaustively reconstructed, and future milestones remain unscored until their deadlines and definitions are observable.

## Capital and funding refinement

The first three base years now use [explicit capital-spend, D&A and working-capital scenarios](shared-evidence.html#meta-tesla-funding-reconciliation-narrative). The central cash proxy requires about $49.7bn over three years, versus $43.5bn June cash/short-term investments, before reserve and award-settlement requirements. The resulting core-business-plus-buildout operating value is low because the case funds a large program without presuming major autonomy/robotics profits. It is a diagnostic of required investment returns, not a complete probability-weighted Tesla value or a final per-share target.


### Final capital-transition refinement

The selected base extends explicit capex/D&A/WC through year7 rather than assuming investment drops abruptly after year3. Gross capex34/38/42/38/35/34/34bn and D&A8/11/15/20/24/27/28bn are analytical budgets, conditional on commissioning and utilization. Years8–10 normalize to terminal ROIC with a disclosed derived component bridge. This produces about $3.064bn illustrative operating value before assets/claims, superseding the earlier $11bn calculation. Holding year4 net reinvestment at $29bn would reduce it by another $6.037bn. This fragile core-plus-buildout scenario is not a complete probability-weighted Tesla equity valuation. See the full capital bridge and stress test in evidence-TSLA.html#judgment.

baseline-reference.name: COHERENT CORP.
baseline-reference.summary: Optical datacenter demand and integration benefits lift profitability, balanced against manufacturing investment and a mixed industrial portfolio.

rationale.growth: 25% is near FY2026 growth of 22.5% and below the latest 34% reported quarter. AI optics supports expansion; industrial exposure and eventually normalizing customer investment require a fade.
rationale.targetMargin: 20% improves on FY2026 GAAP EBIT margin of 12.6% through utilization, mix and integration. It is an EBIT assumption after ongoing compensation and depreciation, not a non-GAAP gross-margin target.
rationale.tax: 24% normalizes the very low FY2026 effective rate and prior loss-related volatility; acquisition and restructuring tax effects are not extended indefinitely.
rationale.salesCapital: 1.25x implies $0.80 of net investment for each incremental $1 of sales. Vertical manufacturing, capacity and working capital remain important even if acquired capacity improves utilization.
rationale.terminalROIC: 12% assumes moderate enduring photonics know-how benefits but much less than current high-growth incremental economics.
rationale.wacc: 10.5% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.5, 20% target debt and a 2.5-point spread reflect optical/industrial cyclicality and a more levered acquisition history.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
rationale.otherClaims: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not evidence that no additional claims exist. Review preferred securities, minority interests and debt terms; acquisition accounting and claims cannot be inferred from a historical book-capital ratio.
rationale.otherAssets: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not a statement that all non-operating assets are absent or worthless. Review assets not already included in snapshot cash and avoid double counting.

waccBuild.limits: Not a live beta regression, bond yield, market-value capital structure or country-default estimate. Extra equity allowances can overlap with operating downside; stress both rather than treating precision as evidence.

companies.dossierMarkdown:
# Coherent (COHR): forecast and valuation dossier

**Decision:** A steeper, shorter early-growth profile is better supported than the old flat 25% assumption. Propose 45%, 30%, 20% growth for FY2027–FY2029 and a ten-year total maturity horizon, with 20% mature EBIT margin. Treat this as an operating proposal; do not publish a refreshed per-share value until cash, minority interests and dilution are reconciled.

**Cutoff:** October 17, 2026. Fiscal years end June 30. Unless stated otherwise, financial figures are USD millions. The latest actual quarter is June 2026, released August 12; the annual report was filed August 14. First-quarter FY2027 results were not yet in this evidence set. Forecasts below are our analysis, not issuer guidance or consensus.

## What changed and what drives growth

Annual revenue increased from $4,707.7m in FY2024 to $5,810.1m in FY2025 and $7,118.2m in FY2026. Latest-quarter revenue was $2,045.5m, up 33.8% year on year and 13.3% sequentially. Datacenter and Communications reached $5,274.6m for FY2026, approximately 74.1% of revenue, versus $3,755.2m a year earlier. Industrial declined to $1,843.6m from $2,055.0m, with portfolio sales affecting comparability. Treat AI optics as the principal current growth driver rather than extrapolating equal growth across both segments.

Management's August 12 formal next-quarter revenue range is $2,200–2,400m, with non-GAAP gross margin of 39.5–41.5% and EPS of $1.85–2.05. In the readable call, management also expected its first quarter above $3bn by the end of FY2027. That is a conditional exit-quarter expectation, not a $12bn annual forecast. The same discussion covers InP capacity expansion and OCS/CPO opportunities. Orders extending into later years improve visibility but do not remove qualification, shipment or customer acceptance conditions.

Our FY2027 base revenue of $10.321bn is consistent with a ramp from the formal first-quarter range toward that potential exit pace. Growth in FY2028 and FY2029 is judgment, not a management forecast. Three early years are preferable to locking peak scarcity-driven growth in for five. The bull case separately tests five years of stronger optical-content expansion.

## Earnings quality and capital requirements

FY2026 reported EBIT was $897.9m. Removing $124.1m of business-sale gains gives a simple operating normalization of $773.8m, or 10.9% of sales; this calculation does not claim to remove every unusual item. Q4 GAAP operating margin was 12.4%, compared with 21.8% non-GAAP. Segment profit is not consolidated EBIT and must not replace it in the DCF.

Cash from operations fell to $79.5m from $633.6m while PPE cash spending rose to $1,102.9m from $440.8m. FY2026 depreciation was $241.6m, intangible amortization $280.3m and cash-flow-statement SBC $186.5m. Inventory consumed roughly $1,183m of cash; payables provided $748.5m, while other operating assets consumed $408.3m. Inventory ended at about $2,581m. Strong bookings and adjusted earnings therefore have not yet translated into comparable free cash flow.

Use a staged EBIT path of 17%, 19%, then 20%, retaining continuing SBC, depreciation and R&D. Early incremental sales-to-capital ratios of 0.8, 1.0 and 1.25 deliberately recognize build-out and working-capital demands. These ratios measure incremental sales relative to net operating reinvestment, not sales divided by gross capex. The later ratio must reconcile with terminal margin, tax and ROIC; the supplied annual schedule does so.

The old extracted book ROIC proxy is not decision-ready: disposal gains, a low reported effective tax rate, acquired intangibles and changes in the equity structure affect it. A 12% terminal ROIC and 24% normalized tax rate are judgments, not a verified through-cycle return. Likewise, the 10.5% base WACC is a scenario input, not a newly measured beta/spread estimate.

## Contracts, concentration and capital claims

The March 2 NVIDIA $2bn equity investment and commercial capacity arrangement provide financing and demand visibility, but investment proceeds are not sales. The annual report describes potential equipment, labor and working-capital investment through 2030; a zero recorded liability does not establish a zero future cash requirement. Two customers represented 20% and 12% of annual revenue. Firm supplier purchases can coexist with customer retiming or cancellation risk.

June unrestricted cash and short-term investments total $1,987.0m, separate from $606.4m of restricted cash. Book debt is $3,222.2m and minority interest $334.7m. Existing Series B preferred converted in FY2026 Q2; retaining its old claim after counting conversion shares would double-count it. The August 27 executive PSU awards introduce another contingent equity claim with $100m aggregate target value. This is compensation, not an operating target; eventual award shares and fair value remain unbridged.

## Management interpretation

Jim Anderson joined as CEO on June 3, 2024, so all eight original quarterly forecasts in this review were issued under his tenure. The stronger quarterly record supports short-horizon revenue planning. It does not establish that portfolio restructuring, capital spending or acquired assets will earn an adequate long-run return. The demand, product, capacity, cost and capital-allocation assessments below deliberately retain counterexamples.

Primary financial evidence: [FY2026 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/820318/000082031826000020/iivi-20260630.htm); [FY2026-Q4 results and next-quarter outlook](https://ir.coherent.com/node/18091/pdf). Exact fact/source links are in evidence-COHR.html#facts and evidence-COHR.html#sources.

## Guidance track record

All consecutive quarterly revenue observations in the stated window are included. Ranges are inclusive; error is actual divided by original midpoint minus one. Original guidance and later revisions are separate.

| Target quarter | Original issue | Revenue range | Actual release | Actual | Result |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| FY2025-Q1 | 2024-08-15 | 1,270.000–1,350.000 | 2024-11-06 | 1,348.100 | within |
| FY2025-Q2 | 2024-11-06 | 1,330.000–1,410.000 | 2025-02-05 | 1,434.700 | above |
| FY2025-Q3 | 2025-02-05 | 1,390.000–1,480.000 | 2025-05-07 | 1,497.900 | above |
| FY2025-Q4 | 2025-05-07 | 1,425.000–1,575.000 | 2025-08-13 | 1,529.400 | within |
| FY2026-Q1 | 2025-08-13 | 1,460.000–1,600.000 | 2025-11-05 | 1,581.400 | within |
| FY2026-Q2 | 2025-11-05 | 1,560.000–1,700.000 | 2026-02-04 | 1,685.600 | within |
| FY2026-Q3 | 2026-02-04 | 1,700.000–1,840.000 | 2026-05-06 | 1,805.600 | within |
| FY2026-Q4 | 2026-05-06 | 1,910.000–2,050.000 | 2026-08-12 | 2,045.500 | within |

Revenue: 6 within, 2 above, 0 below; mean absolute midpoint error 3.26%. This is not a probability estimate or a management-quality multiplier.

Non-GAAP definitions changed starting FY2025 Q2. Old adjusted EPS/margins are not scored against newly restated actuals without a definition bridge. The revenue series also flags portfolio-sale perimeter changes. The investor-day summary was reviewed; an unread deck or video is not treated as evidence for a long-term target.

## Proposed scenarios and scale check

All rows are our analytical scenarios. Stable growth is 2.5%; no case was calibrated to the share price. Normalized positive-profit cash tax is 24%. Loss-year tax benefits are not assumed realizable.

| Case | Explicit early annual growth | Early years / total horizon | Revenue at early-phase end | Revenue at maturity | Mature EBIT margin | WACC | Terminal ROIC |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bear | 30%, 10%, 5% | 3 / 10 | $10.69bn | $13.66bn | 14% | 12% | 9% |
| base | 45%, 30%, 20% | 3 / 10 | $16.10bn | $31.15bn | 20% | 10.5% | 12% |
| bull | 55%, 40%, 30%, 25%, 20% | 5 / 15 | $30.12bn | $79.99bn | 25% | 9.5% | 15% |

The very large maturity values, especially the bull cases, are feasibility tests, not verified market forecasts. The early phase ends in FY/calendar 2029 for three-year cases and 2031 for five-year cases; maturity is 2036 or 2041. Require a market-share and capital-capacity check before assigning probabilities. Early revenue growth fades to stable growth; capital efficiency then reconciles with terminal margin, tax and ROIC. Full annual paths, net-reinvestment diagnostics and FCFF illustrations are stored in evidence-COHR.html#judgment. A fiscal/calendar anchor is not the October 17 valuation date: use the appropriate stub period.

The common risk-free input is the October 16 USD 10-year Treasury yield of 5.09%; chosen ERP is 4.5%. Beta, debt spread and weights were not newly measured. WACC values are explicit scenario judgments, not falsely precise empirical estimates. Terminal reinvestment is stable growth divided by terminal ROIC, rather than a free-growth assumption.

## Management capabilities: evidence rather than a single score

| Capability | Assessment | Confidence | Counterexample / limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| demand forecasting | Quarterly revenue forecasting has been useful over the reviewed window. | moderate-high for quarter, low for long-term | Multi-year demand visibility depends on customer expansion and is not fully contracted recognized revenue. |
| product delivery | Broad optical portfolio is translating into datacenter growth; next architectures remain execution tests. | moderate | New OCS/CPO/multi-rail and InP timelines are management expectations, not independently complete. |
| capacity execution | Capacity is being funded and expanded, with cash conversion under pressure. | moderate | CFO fell to $79.5m; yield/utilization and inventory realization still need verification. |
| cost control | Operating leverage and portfolio simplification improved profitability. | moderate | FY2026 GAAP EBIT includes $124.1m sale gain; restructuring, SBC and amortization cannot all be erased. |
| capital allocation | Equity financing and preferred conversion increased flexibility, but returns on the new build are unproven. | moderate-low | Large reinvestment and minority/restricted-cash complexity; inherited acquisition assets complicate ROIC. |

The JSON records the evidence, sources and leadership attribution for each dimension. Outcomes are team and market results; inherited assets and supply conditions are not assigned entirely to the current CEO.

## Unresolved obligation and asset register

Every item below has an exact date, source IDs, conditions, treatment and remaining gap in evidence-COHR.html#obligation-asset-register, also embedded in the proposal. Values overlap and must not be summed mechanically.

| Item | Date | Treatment / unresolved issue |
|---|---|---|
| Borrowings, carrying amount | 2026-06-30 | Reconcile debt economic claim and post-June cash payments before deducting from enterprise value. No October debt/cash roll-forward or current debt fair value. |
| Restricted cash | 2026-06-30 | Exclude from unrestricted excess cash; recognize related subsidiary economics consistently. Confirm permitted uses, release timing and links to SiC minority arrangements. |
| Noncontrolling interests, book amount | 2026-06-30 | Deduct economic minority value once if valuing 100% consolidated cash flows. Book value is not independently valued minority claim. |
| Cash and short-term investments | 2026-06-30 | Add only excess unrestricted cash after valuation-date roll-forward. October balance, cash taxes and minimum operating cash not reconciled. |
| Operating and finance lease liabilities | 2026-06-30 | Match lease treatment to EBIT and invested capital; avoid subtracting operating rent twice. Future lease commitments and lease-adjusted capital bridge not independently modeled. |
| NVIDIA capacity agreement and supplier commitments | 2026-03-02 | Model incremental spending and fulfillment costs; equity investment is financing, customer orders are not immediate revenue. Complete commitment schedule and enforceable cancellation/shortfall exposure not quantified. |
| Employee awards and converted preferred | 2026-06-30 | Do not retain obsolete preferred deduction after counting conversion shares. Include ongoing SBC and reconcile outstanding award dilution. October fully diluted share bridge and current award valuation pending. |
| August special executive PSUs, target value | 2026-08-27 | Model contingent dilution and compensation expense; do not deduct target dollars as debt and also add all possible shares. Grant-date fair value, target share units and expense schedule are not fully disclosed in reviewed 8-K. |

## Invalidators and next evidence

1. Q1 FY2027 shipments fall materially below the $2.2bn guide floor or the fiscal-year exit ramp is delayed.
2. Inventory/payables growth continues to consume cash without matching shipment and collection growth.
3. InP yield or customer qualification limits prevent the stated capacity ramp.
4. Industrial weakness offsets datacenter gains, or new optical architectures shift content to competitors.
5. New capacity/purchase commitments earn below-cost returns despite reported revenue growth.

## Coverage and limitations

current primary financial sources verified through cutoff; bounded event coverage. 

The source ledger distinguishes readable primary filings/decks/letters, readable third-party transcripts and reused previously verified extracts. Dates refer to publication/event dates rather than URL cache timestamps. Public transcripts were used for summarized management statements, not copied wholesale; no accounts, purchases or paywall bypasses were used. Sources were available as of the cutoff, but this is not a claim to have read every filing, interview or event. Inherited historical series preserve original units and provenance and are not an as-known-then backtest.

Key additional evidence:
- [Q4 FY2026 earnings call, Jim Anderson and Sherri Luther](https://earningscalls.dev/transcripts/coherent-corp_cohr_earnings_call_transcript_2026-08-12)
- [Analyst and investor day release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/820318/000119312525129060/d908147dex991.htm)
- [Special executive performance awards approved August 27](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/820318/000119312526375462/d110649d8k.htm)

rationale.growth: 35% is well below FY2026 growth of 83% and the latest 109% quarter. It still compounds into a much larger business over ten years; optical adoption supports growth but current capacity shortages are not permanent.
rationale.targetMargin: 25% improves on FY2026 annual GAAP EBIT margin of 17.4% but is below the latest quarter’s 27.8%. It preserves operating leverage without using non-GAAP guidance as GAAP EBIT.
rationale.tax: 22% is a normalized profitable-company assumption. Recent loss periods and the FY2026 tax benefit do not support a negative long-run cash-tax rate.
rationale.salesCapital: 1.2x requires about $0.83 of net reinvestment per added $1 of sales. Capacity additions and working capital make the ramp less capital-light than a pure design/software business.
rationale.terminalROIC: 14% retains a limited technology advantage while allowing competition and product replacement to erode peak returns.
rationale.wacc: 11.5% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.6, 15% target debt and a 2.5-point debt spread reflect a concentrated, volatile optical cycle and financing exposure.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
