companies.dossierMarkdown:
# Lumentum (LITE): forecast and valuation dossier

**Decision:** Replace the old smooth 35% early-growth assumption with a front-loaded 70%, 35%, 25% FY2027–FY2029 proposal over a ten-year maturity horizon. Use 25% mature EBIT margin, below the current adjusted peak. The operating case can be considered for renewal, but the convertible settlement and dilution bridge is still necessary before a per-share valuation.

**Cutoff:** October 17, 2026. FY2026 ended June 27; results were released August 11 and the annual report filed August 17. Figures are USD millions unless specified. Next-quarter guidance remains pending at the cutoff. Our scenarios are neither management guidance nor analyst consensus.

## Operating trajectory and revenue mix

Annual revenue was $1,359.2m in FY2024, $1,645.0m in FY2025 and $3,014.0m in FY2026. EBIT moved from losses of $434.0m and $180.1m to positive $524.8m. Q4 revenue reached $1,006.3m, up 109.3% year on year and 24.5% sequentially. Components contributed $649.4m and Systems $356.9m; the preceding quarter was $533.3m and $275.1m. Both product groups accelerated, rather than all growth being confined to one small pilot product.

Formal Q1 FY2027 guidance is revenue of $1,225–1,275m, non-GAAP operating margin of 39.5–40.5%, and adjusted EPS of $4.05–4.35. Our $5.124bn FY2027 revenue base begins near the annualized first-quarter midpoint, while allowing growth, shipment variability and concentration risk. The following two years have no matching issuer annual forecast and are our judgment.

The latest readable call describes a 50% year-on-year EML unit-output expansion by December 2026 and later capacity including Greensboro revenue beginning in early 2028. OCS and CPO create additional opportunities, but backlog is not current revenue. The February OCS backlog and CPO delivery expectations are useful indicators only when matched to customer qualification, delivery, acceptance and recognized revenue. Sustained margins also depend on pricing as supply expands.

## Profit, cash and reinvestment

Q4 GAAP gross margin was 47.4% and operating margin 27.8%, versus non-GAAP figures of 50.4% and 36.6%. Annual EBIT of $524.8m is positive even though net loss was $6,935.1m: the $7,756.6m debt-extinguishment loss is a financing item. It should not destroy operating EBIT in a DCF, and its economic cost to common holders should not disappear from the financing/claims bridge.

FY2026 CFO was $751.4m and PPE cash spending $451.3m, compared with $126.3m and $231.0m in FY2025. Depreciation was $128.8m, intangible amortization/write-offs $138.2m, and SBC $170.2m. Receivables and inventory absorbed $270.4m and $228.4m. Purchase obligations of $2,354.4m, including $2,112.5m within one year, make future working-capital and capacity funding important even after the recent CFO improvement.

Our EBIT margin path is 30%, 29%, 27%, then 25%. It assumes a strong current mix and utilization benefit but fades exceptional pricing, rather than perpetuating next-quarter non-GAAP guidance. Continuing SBC, R&D and depreciation remain expenses. Early incremental sales-to-capital ratios are 1.1, 1.2, 1.4 and 1.6, then fade to terminal consistency. The ratios still need an explicit procurement, capex, depreciation and working-capital schedule.

A 22% normalized tax rate and 14% terminal ROIC are judgments. Reported tax, debt losses, acquisitions and conversion accounting make a simple historical net-income return misleading. There is no claim that 14% has been proven through a full investment and replacement cycle. The 11.5% WACC is a transparent scenario assumption, not a fresh market-beta estimate.

## Financing and concentration are central

June cash of $2,043.5m and investments of $694.9m must be rolled against note settlements. Book debt totaled $1,637.4m, including $1,544.6m of convertible carrying value and $92.8m of term loans. Convertible principal was $1,554.3m. All note series were current because holders could elect conversion; this is not equivalent to all principal being contractually due on that date.

As of August 14, $757.8m principal had been submitted for conversion. Principal must settle in cash, while excess conversion value may use cash, shares or both. Capped calls, early settlements and inducement transactions require series-specific treatment. A model cannot subtract the full note claim and also include full if-converted shares without a consistent reconciliation.

NVIDIA's March investment created approximately 2.9m preferred shares that are economically common-like, with one-for-one common conversion and no economic preference. They should not be modeled as both a $2bn senior deduction and common-equivalent shares. The two largest customers represented 26.6% and 15% of annual revenue. Much of the order book lacks enduring volume commitments, so customer concentration and rapid product transitions remain material risks.

## Management interpretation

Michael Hurlston's appointment was announced February 3, 2025 and became effective February 7. Several forecasts in the eight-quarter sample predate his tenure, including the FY2025 Q3 guide issued February 6. Attribution therefore distinguishes his team's later execution from inherited designs, capacity and earlier guidance. June 3, 2025 guidance was raised before the quarter closed; a February 3 preliminary revenue result is a post-period update, not a new ex-ante forecast.

Primary financial evidence: [FY2026 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828026057358/lite-20260627.htm); [FY2026-Q4 results and outlook](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results/default.aspx). Exact fact/source links are in evidence-LITE.html#facts and evidence-LITE.html#sources.

## Guidance track record

All consecutive quarterly revenue observations in the stated window are included. Ranges are inclusive; error is actual divided by original midpoint minus one. Original guidance and later revisions are separate.

| Target quarter | Original issue | Revenue range | Actual release | Actual | Result |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| FY2025-Q1 | 2024-08-14 | 315.000–335.000 | 2024-11-07 | 336.900 | above |
| FY2025-Q2 | 2024-11-07 | 380.000–400.000 | 2025-02-06 | 402.200 | above |
| FY2025-Q3 | 2025-02-06 | 410.000–425.000 | 2025-05-06 | 425.200 | above |
| FY2025-Q4 | 2025-05-06 | 440.000–470.000 | 2025-08-12 | 480.700 | above |
| FY2026-Q1 | 2025-08-12 | 510.000–540.000 | 2025-11-04 | 533.800 | within |
| FY2026-Q2 | 2025-11-04 | 630.000–670.000 | 2026-02-03 | 665.500 | within |
| FY2026-Q3 | 2026-02-03 | 780.000–830.000 | 2026-05-05 | 808.400 | within |
| FY2026-Q4 | 2026-05-05 | 960.000–1,010.000 | 2026-08-11 | 1,006.300 | within |

Revenue: 4 within, 4 above, 0 below; mean absolute midpoint error 2.62%. This is not a probability estimate or a management-quality multiplier.

FY2025 Q4 guidance was raised on June 3 from $440–470m to $465–475m; actual $480.7m exceeded both ranges. The earlier $500m-quarter timing milestone was met in FY2026 Q1, and the $600m-quarter threshold was exceeded in FY2026 Q2. February 3 preliminary FY2025 Q2 revenue is recorded as a post-period update, not a successful advance forecast. The FY2025 Q3 upper-bound exceedance was only $0.2m at published precision.

## Proposed scenarios and scale check

All rows are our analytical scenarios. Stable growth is 2.5%; no case was calibrated to the share price. Normalized positive-profit cash tax is 22%. Loss-year tax benefits are not assumed realizable.

| Case | Explicit early annual growth | Early years / total horizon | Revenue at early-phase end | Revenue at maturity | Mature EBIT margin | WACC | Terminal ROIC |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bear | 45%, 10%, 5% | 3 / 10 | $5.05bn | $6.45bn | 18% | 13% | 10% |
| base | 70%, 35%, 25% | 3 / 10 | $8.65bn | $19.06bn | 25% | 11.5% | 14% |
| bull | 85%, 50%, 35%, 30%, 25% | 5 / 15 | $18.35bn | $59.26bn | 32% | 10% | 18% |

The very large maturity values, especially the bull cases, are feasibility tests, not verified market forecasts. The early phase ends in FY/calendar 2029 for three-year cases and 2031 for five-year cases; maturity is 2036 or 2041. Require a market-share and capital-capacity check before assigning probabilities. Early revenue growth fades to stable growth; capital efficiency then reconciles with terminal margin, tax and ROIC. Full annual paths, net-reinvestment diagnostics and FCFF illustrations are stored in evidence-LITE.html#judgment. A fiscal/calendar anchor is not the October 17 valuation date: use the appropriate stub period.

The common risk-free input is the October 16 USD 10-year Treasury yield of 5.09%; chosen ERP is 4.5%. Beta, debt spread and weights were not newly measured. WACC values are explicit scenario judgments, not falsely precise empirical estimates. Terminal reinvestment is stable growth divided by terminal ROIC, rather than a free-growth assumption.

## Management capabilities: evidence rather than a single score

| Capability | Assessment | Confidence | Counterexample / limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| demand forecasting | Strong recent sales-range delivery, with repeated early upside. | moderate-high near term | Concentrated customer exposure and cancelable/retimed orders limit distant forecast confidence. |
| product delivery | EML and new optical systems have translated into material sales expansion. | moderate | Future CPO and Greensboro delivery milestones have not matured at cutoff. |
| capacity execution | Production expansion supports current growth; larger planned supply remains to be proven. | moderate | Over50% EML output growth by December and 2028 Greensboro revenue still pending. |
| cost control | Strong operating leverage and mix/pricing gains. | moderate-high recent, moderate-low durable | Ongoing SBC $170.2m and acquired-asset amortization remain economic/accounting differences; scarcity pricing may reverse. |
| capital allocation | Financing removed debt but produced very large conversion-related economics. | mixed, moderate | $7.7566bn extinguishment loss and cash-settled principal show why debt face value and simple share count alone are inadequate. |

The JSON records the evidence, sources and leadership attribution for each dimension. Outcomes are team and market results; inherited assets and supply conditions are not assigned entirely to the current CEO.

## Unresolved obligation and asset register

Every item below has an exact date, source IDs, conditions, treatment and remaining gap in evidence-LITE.html#obligation-asset-register, also embedded in the proposal. Values overlap and must not be summed mechanically.

| Item | Date | Treatment / unresolved issue |
|---|---|---|
| Convertible principal | 2026-06-27 | Use either instrument economic value or cash principal plus explicit excess-conversion dilution, not both. Conversion elections, capped-call proceeds and post-June settlement bridge pending. |
| Early conversion requests | 2026-08-14 | Roll requested cash principal out of cash and debt together when settled. Do not add as another debt obligation. Settlement dates, actual share/cash premium and residual series amounts not fully rolled. |
| Term-loan principal | 2026-06-27 | Deduct once in debt bridge; interest belongs below operating profit. October repayments not reconciled. |
| NVIDIA preferred shares | 2026-03-02 | Treat as common-like dilution; do not subtract $2bn and also include common-equivalent shares. Exact current share count and any conversions need reconciliation. |
| Purchase obligations | 2026-06-27 | Model inventory, capacity and procurement cash needs; these purchases are not an extra debt deduction if already in forecast cash costs. Determine cancellation, overlap with payables/capex and demand-downside exposure. |
| Cash and short-term investments | 2026-06-27 | Add excess cash after settlement and operating-liquidity bridge. Do not present June cash as October cash. |
| Operating lease liability | 2026-06-27 | Use consistent operating-rent or capitalized-lease treatment. Lease/capacity commitments after June remain to be reconciled. |
| Employee awards and capped calls | 2026-06-27 | Keep continuing SBC in EBIT; use explicit legacy award and capped-call claim scenarios without double counting. Current valuation and complete settlement bridge pending. |

## Invalidators and next evidence

1. Q1 FY2027 revenue misses the $1.225bn guide floor or margin gains rely primarily on temporary scarcity pricing.
2. EML output, OCS deliveries or CPO customer milestones slip relative to dated management expectations.
3. Cash conversion weakens as $2.354bn purchase commitments and inventory growth meet demand digestion.
4. Mandatory cash principal settlement drains liquidity before expansion earns cash.
5. Customer concentration and changes in optical architecture reduce durable pricing power.

## Coverage and limitations

current primary financial sources verified; bounded event coverage. 

The source ledger distinguishes readable primary filings/decks/letters, readable third-party transcripts and reused previously verified extracts. Dates refer to publication/event dates rather than URL cache timestamps. Public transcripts were used for summarized management statements, not copied wholesale; no accounts, purchases or paywall bypasses were used. Sources were available as of the cutoff, but this is not a claim to have read every filing, interview or event. baseline-reference.name: APPLIED OPTOELECTRONICS, INC.
baseline-reference.classification: conditional staged capacity research assumptions; not a validated fair-value estimate
baseline-reference.summary: Provisional research assumptions only. A high-risk capacity-led turnaround in datacenter optics, with substantial funding needs before durable GAAP profitability.

rationale.growth: 60% is year 1 growth. The staged profile then uses 40%, 30%, 20%, 15%, 10%, 8%, 5%, 3%, and 2.5% at these defaults. Quarter 3 guidance and capacity expansion support a front-loaded structure; the annual path is analyst judgment, not management guidance. Each simulated initial-growth input changes the whole same weighted path.
rationale.targetMargin: 12% mature GAAP EBIT margin is reached in year 6. At the reported starting loss, the staged path is −5%,0%,5%,8%,10%,12% before maturity. This is a conditional utilization and operating-leverage judgment; no non-GAAP net margin is substituted.
rationale.tax: 25% applies only to positive modeled EBIT. This is a normalized mature rate; no tax refund or verified NOL benefit is assumed during losses.
rationale.salesCapital: 0.8x is initial incremental sales/capital, requiring $1.25 investment per $1 extra revenue in years 1–2. It rises to 1.6x by years 6–7 as capacity is used. Years 8–10 fade capital intensity toward (1 + terminal growth) × margin × (1 − tax) / terminal ROIC, ending at 1.084x at defaults to align year 10 and terminal economics. The whole path is an explicit assumption, not a reported ratio.
rationale.terminalROIC: 10% assumes capital utilization improves in maturity but grants no excess return versus the high constant model discount rate.
rationale.wacc: 13.5% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.8 plus a 1-point extra equity allowance, 10% target debt and a 3.5-point debt spread reflect concentrated customers, execution and funding risk. These are judgments, not quoted borrowing terms.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
rationale.otherClaims: 0 means no additional user-entered claim beyond the separate explicit current claims model. Do not enter the same modeled claims again. The separate source-dated current claims model deducts the disclosed convertible fair-value proxy and vendor financing once, and uses an explicit intrinsic customer-warrant scenario. Counterfactual note conversion and the incomplete known-ATM pro forma are separate sensitivities. Current employee awards and warrant time value remain incomplete.
rationale.otherAssets: 0 is an additional-asset assumption beyond source cash and any explicitly selected financing proceeds. It is not proof that every other nonoperating asset is absent.

reportedAnchors.classification: reported or directly derived from reported current financials
reported results and explicitly labeled management outlook; not the base-case forecast
reportedAnchors.text: Q2 2026 revenue was $191.9m; GAAP gross margin was 27.7% and GAAP net loss $22.8m. Q3 revenue guidance was $255–290m.

waccBuild.classification: analyst model estimate; only riskFreeUSD is an observed input
waccBuild.equityRiskPremiumClassification: chosen long-run assumption; January reference is 4.23%, not a current estimate
waccBuild.formula: Ke = Rf + assumed beta × chosen ERP + extra equity risk; WACC = Ke × (1 − debt weight) + assumed Kd × (1 − tax) × debt weight
waccBuild.limits: Not a live beta regression, bond yield, market-value capital structure or country-default estimate. Extra equity allowances can overlap with operating downside; stress both rather than treating precision as evidence.

bridgePolicy.note: The separate source-dated current claims model deducts the disclosed convertible fair-value proxy and vendor financing once, and uses an explicit intrinsic customer-warrant scenario. Counterfactual note conversion and the incomplete known-ATM pro forma are separate sensitivities. Current employee awards and warrant time value remain incomplete.

modelLimits: This staged capacity assumption set produces negative operating enterprise value and five cash-burning forecast years. It is a conditional operating stress case, not a standalone fair-value estimate; financing, default, recovery and detailed maintenance replacement remain unmodeled.
The simple model has no financing or default-probability schedule; a large terminal value can conceal years of cash burn.

Convertible notes, vendor financing, dilution and warrants

formulas.fcff: EBIT - cash tax on EBIT + D&A - gross capital cash spending - increase in other operating working capital + increase in customer advances.
formulas.capitalCashSpending: PPE/intangible cash purchases + capital supplier advances not already in those purchases + capitalized site purchases. Reclassification of existing prepayments/CIP is not a new cash use.

formulas.fundingNeed: Peak cash uses + debt service + cash reserve - opening usable cash - net cash proceeds actually received - available committed credit draws. FCFF alone omits financing costs and principal maturity timing.
formulas.terminal: Terminal net reinvestment = terminal NOPAT * stable growth / terminal ROIC; customer-advance movement must be included consistently.

cautions: All future investment schedules are analytical sensitivities anchored to disclosed spending/capacity, not disclosed future budgets. Cumulative peaks are not precise financing forecasts.

normalizedStagedAdapter.status: Recommended source-reasoned analyst shape; no market-price calibration
normalizedStagedAdapter.growthFormula: yearGrowth = terminalGrowth + (sampledGrowth - terminalGrowth) * growthWeight; first year equals sampled growth; last year equals stable growth.
normalizedStagedAdapter.marginFormula: yearMargin = actualAdjustedStartingMargin + (sampledTargetMargin - actualAdjustedStartingMargin) * marginWeight; from year 6 equals sampled target. normalizedStagedAdapter.capitalDriverMeaning: Initial incremental sales/capital; 0.8x baseline. Early-stage utilization raises it toward 2 times input in years 6–7.

normalizedStagedAdapter.terminalConsistencyProof: With constant final growth g and margin m, explicit reinvestment = (R_t - R_t-1) * (1+g)*m*(1-tax)/ROIC = NOPAT_t*g/ROIC. Thus final FCFF*(1+g) equals terminal-year NOPAT*(1-g/ROIC). The (1+g) factor matches the existing engine contemporaneous delta-sales convention to its terminal g/ROIC convention.
normalizedStagedAdapter.discounting: Use sampled WACC each year and same terminal WACC; taxes fixed unless user changes the scalar tax rate.
normalizedStagedAdapter.controls: Keep scalar assumptions editable, derive overrides inside the shared current valuation path. Do not persist generated arrays as user-authored overrides. Every Monte Carlo draw must run the same adapter.
normalizedStagedAdapter.zeroMarginBoundary: When targetMargin=0, terminal intensity is zero. If the existing engine requires a finite positive salesCapital override, use Number.MAX_VALUE as a documented numerical limiting representation instead of Infinity; its resulting investment is negligible at monetary precision. Deterministic and simulation must share the same convention.
rationale: The issuer reported Q2 2026 revenue of $191.9m and guided Q3 to $255–290m. A front-loaded growth path with a fast decline from 60% to 40%, 30% and 20% is a bounded analyst illustration of ramp then slowdown, not a forecast derived directly from units or guidance.

The initial margin is reported GAAP TTM EBIT/revenue. Conditional break-even by year 2 and 12% mature margin by year 6 are analyst operating-leverage judgments; non-GAAP net income is not substituted for GAAP EBIT.

Initial 0.8x sales/capital remains a conservative capital-heavy input; the temporary twofold utilization improvement is assumed, motivated by already funded construction and equipment prepayments, not by a verified incremental asset-turnover ratio.

Capital intensity subsequently converges to the independently specified mature marginal ROIC, allowing competitive erosion of the higher mid-ramp return and eliminating a mechanical terminal reinvestment jump.
All forecast growth, margin, capital-efficiency and risk values remain editable or sampled. The fixed weights describe transition shape, not independent reported facts or probabilities.

companies.dossierMarkdown:
# Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI): forecast and valuation dossier

**Decision:** Keep a conditional capacity-ramp scenario rather than install a confident new default. A calendar-2026 revenue bridge and explicit factory/funding/dilution model are necessary. The illustrative base uses approximately $1.1bn in 2026 and growth of 150%, 60%, 35% in 2027–2029, but this is a demanding execution scenario, not an issuer forecast for those years. Existing conservative staged sensitivities should remain visible.

**Cutoff:** October 17, 2026. Calendar-year reporter. Latest actuals cover June 30, released August 6; the investor deck was posted September 21 but explicitly dates its outlook to August 6. Financial amounts are USD millions unless specified. The latest completed ATM financing is dated October 5. There are no analyst-estimate inputs in the proposed scenarios.

## Revenue ramp: what is actual and what is conditional

Revenue grew from $217.6m in 2023 to $249.4m in 2024 and $455.7m in 2025. Operating losses were $41.3m, $70.9m and $54.6m respectively. Q2 2026 revenue of $191.922m compared with $102.952m a year earlier and $151.144m in Q1. Datacenter contributed $107.662m, CATV $80.578m, telecom $3.411m and other $0.271m. Datacenter is now about 56% of quarterly revenue; a single blended optical-growth assumption obscures CATV exposure and product-transition risk.

Formal Q3 revenue guidance is $255–290m, non-GAAP gross margin 29–30.5%, and adjusted EPS $0.11–0.26. The approximately $1.1bn annual outlook is separately quantified management guidance. With H1 revenue of $343.066m and Q3 at its midpoint, it requires Q4 revenue of $484.434m, more than 2.5 times Q2. The strong quarterly forecasting record does not make that acceleration automatic.

The issuer presentation targets combined 800G/1.6T monthly capacity of 650,000 units in Q4 2026 and 930,000 in Q4 2027. Nameplate capacity is not shipments or paid revenue. Installation, customer qualification, yields, components, order allocation and collections must all occur. The latest readable call reports Q2 800G revenue of only $12.8m and describes future 1.6T qualification/delivery. Timing descriptions for a large order differ within the transcript, so no single precise delivery schedule is imposed here. The August 18 CFO interview describes domestic automation and laser integration as advantages; the valuation does not assume a future regulatory ban on competitors or a guaranteed domestic premium.

## Operating profit has not caught up

Q2 GAAP operating loss was $24.727m. Non-GAAP net income of $5.5m and EPS of $0.06 should not be mistaken for operating profitability: the presentation still reports a non-GAAP operating loss of about $10.3m. Q2 GAAP gross margin was 27.7%, versus 29.8% adjusted. H1 operating loss was $37.718m. Cost execution and revenue forecasting need separate assessments.

H1 CFO was negative $73.781m. Cash PPE purchases of $335.132m, capital prepayments of $289.744m and land of $8.581m sum to $633.457m of capital cash uses. D&A was only $19.729m and SBC $9.254m. Receivables consumed $69.649m and inventories $94.092m, partly offset by $142.156m from payables. Net PPE of $697.086m includes $168.805m construction in progress, while capital prepayments stand at $324.045m. This spending creates future depreciation and operating obligations; it is not excess cash and should not be counted again on equipment delivery.

Our conditional EBIT path of 6%, 12%, then 15% requires much stronger utilization and mix. Early incremental sales-to-capital of 0.6, 0.85 and 1.1 is only a funding diagnostic. Mature tax of 25%, ROIC of 11% and WACC of 13.5% are judgments. Current losses establish no positive economic ROIC; the base intentionally has a terminal return below the funding cost. A large revenue outcome can still destroy capital.

## Financing and customer-linked dilution

June cash was $499.737m, bank debt $58.915m and vendor bank acceptances $33.940m. Convertible principal was $124.925m versus book value $129.142m and disclosed June fair value $445.1m. The deck excludes the note from its debt presentation because management expects stock settlement; that convention does not remove the economic claim. Use mutually exclusive claim/dilution treatments and reconcile vendor financing with working capital.

The October 5 completed ATM adds about $588m net and 5.695m shares. June cash plus those proceeds is not current cash because factory, property and lease spending continued. The known-transaction share calculation of 90.601m is not an independently verified October outstanding count. Houston leases, the September property purchase and Ningbo's ten-year lease must enter the forward cash model.

Amazon's warrant can cover up to 7.945399m shares at $23.6956; only 1.324233m were initially vested. Later vesting depends on purchases, with a $4bn threshold. That threshold is not guaranteed revenue. Contra-revenue, vesting and dilution must be modeled without double-charging the same warrant economics. Existing employee RSUs and PSUs add separate claims.

## Management interpretation

Founder/CEO Thompson Lin and CFO Stefan Murry led throughout the reviewed period. The presentation's 28-plus-year company tenure is not assumed to mean that many years continuously in the same title. Their revenue guidance record is useful, while product delivery, factory utilization, cash conversion and allocation of expansion capital remain less proven. Earlier capacity expectations and profitability misses are retained rather than selecting only recent revenue successes.

Primary financial evidence: [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1158114/000143774926005875/aaoi20251231_10k.htm); [June 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1158114/000143774926026278/aaoi20260630_10q.htm). Exact fact/source links are in evidence-AAOI.html#facts and evidence-AAOI.html#sources.

## Guidance track record

All consecutive quarterly revenue observations in the stated window are included. Ranges are inclusive; error is actual divided by original midpoint minus one. Original guidance and later revisions are separate.

| Target quarter | Original issue | Revenue range | Actual release | Actual | Result |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| FY2024-Q1 | 2024-02-22 | 41.000–46.000 | 2024-05-09 | 40.673 | below |
| FY2024-Q2 | 2024-05-09 | 41.500–46.500 | 2024-08-06 | 43.300 | within |
| FY2024-Q3 | 2024-08-06 | 60.000–66.000 | 2024-11-07 | 65.200 | within |
| FY2024-Q4 | 2024-11-07 | 94.000–104.000 | 2025-02-26 | 100.300 | within |
| FY2025-Q1 | 2025-02-26 | 94.000–104.000 | 2025-05-08 | 99.859 | within |
| FY2025-Q2 | 2025-05-08 | 100.000–110.000 | 2025-08-07 | 102.952 | within |
| FY2025-Q3 | 2025-08-07 | 115.000–127.000 | 2025-11-06 | 118.600 | within |
| FY2025-Q4 | 2025-11-06 | 125.000–140.000 | 2026-02-26 | 134.300 | within |
| FY2026-Q1 | 2026-02-26 | 150.000–165.000 | 2026-05-07 | 151.144 | within |
| FY2026-Q2 | 2026-05-07 | 180.000–198.000 | 2026-08-06 | 191.922 | within |

Revenue: 9 within, 0 above, 1 below; mean absolute midpoint error 2.46%. This is not a probability estimate or a management-quality multiplier.

The ten-quarter record also matches every non-GAAP gross-margin and EPS range in the JSON. Q1 and Q2 2024 gross margins missed, and Q3 2024/Q2 2025 EPS missed despite largely in-range revenue. The exact realized year-end 2025 capacity measure was not recovered, so the earlier capacity target is not assigned an invented pass/fail.

## Proposed scenarios and scale check

All rows are our analytical scenarios. Stable growth is 2.5%; no case was calibrated to the share price. Normalized positive-profit cash tax is 25%. Loss-year tax benefits are not assumed realizable.

| Case | Explicit early annual growth | Early years / total horizon | Revenue at early-phase end | Revenue at maturity | Mature EBIT margin | WACC | Terminal ROIC |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bear | 55%, 25%, 10% | 3 / 10 | $1.92bn | $2.83bn | 8% | 15.5% | 8% |
| base | 150%, 60%, 35% | 3 / 10 | $5.94bn | $16.85bn | 15% | 13.5% | 11% |
| bull | 200%, 80%, 50%, 35%, 25% | 5 / 15 | $15.72bn | $50.77bn | 24% | 12% | 16% |

The very large maturity values, especially the bull cases, are feasibility tests, not verified market forecasts. The early phase ends in FY/calendar 2029 for three-year cases and 2031 for five-year cases; maturity is 2036 or 2041. Require a market-share and capital-capacity check before assigning probabilities. Early revenue growth fades to stable growth; capital efficiency then reconciles with terminal margin, tax and ROIC. Full annual paths, net-reinvestment diagnostics and FCFF illustrations are stored in evidence-AAOI.html#judgment. A fiscal/calendar anchor is not the October 17 valuation date: use the appropriate stub period.

The common risk-free input is the October 16 USD 10-year Treasury yield of 5.09%; chosen ERP is 4.5%. Beta, debt spread and weights were not newly measured. WACC values are explicit scenario judgments, not falsely precise empirical estimates. Terminal reinvestment is stable growth divided by terminal ROIC, rather than a free-growth assumption.

## Management capabilities: evidence rather than a single score

| Capability | Assessment | Confidence | Counterexample / limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| demand forecasting | Quarterly revenue ranges reasonably calibrated; mix and profitability less reliable. | moderate | Q1 2024 / Q2 2024 gross margin misses and Q3 2024 / Q2 2025 EPS misses despite revenue largely in range. |
| product delivery | 400G and 800G sales demonstrate progress; larger 1.6T/CPO thesis is still conditional. | moderate-low | 2025 datacenter shipments delayed; repeated final-stage qualification language. The 1.6T order delivery timing differs within latest call. |
| capacity execution | Meaningful physical investment, but installed productive capacity lags expenditure. | moderate-low | March 2026 capacity nearly100k/month after earlier year-end 2025 target >100k; exact year-end outcome not verified. |
| cost control | Gross margin recovered from 2024, but rising opex offsets volume. | mixed, moderate | Q2 2026 non-GAAP operating loss of $10.3m despite adjusted net profit; operating cash losses remain. |
| capital allocation | Financing raised expansion capital, while dilution and returns remain substantial risks. | moderate-low | H1 capital cash uses were approximately $633.5m with negative CFO; customer warrants and convertibles add claims. |

The JSON records the evidence, sources and leadership attribution for each dimension. Outcomes are team and market results; inherited assets and supply conditions are not assigned entirely to the current CEO.

## Unresolved obligation and asset register

Every item below has an exact date, source IDs, conditions, treatment and remaining gap in evidence-AAOI.html#obligation-asset-register, also embedded in the proposal. Values overlap and must not be summed mechanically.

| Item | Date | Treatment / unresolved issue |
|---|---|---|
| June unrestricted cash | 2026-06-30 | Roll forward using actual transactions; do not simply add ATM proceeds and assume current cash. Current cash after capital spending and leasing unknown. |
| Completed ATM net proceeds | 2026-10-05 | Recognize financing cash and new shares together; known-transaction share total 90.601134m is not independently verified current outstanding. Other issuance, vesting and cash uses since August not fully reconciled. |
| Convertible debt principal / historical fair value | 2026-06-30 | Compare mutually exclusive fair-value claim, if-converted and principal-only sensitivities; stock settlement does not erase cost. October option value, current principal and settlement choices unknown. |
| Bank debt and vendor bank acceptances | 2026-06-30 | Avoid double-counting supplier financing in both debt and operating payables. Economic financing classification and cutoff balance bridge pending. |
| Amazon customer warrant | 2025-03-13 | Model vesting/share dilution with contra-revenue consistently. Grant-date fair value is not current fair value. Current vested amount, modification status and economic valuation pending. |
| Capital prepayments and construction | 2026-06-30 | Treat as operating assets, not excess cash; do not charge prepayments again on delivery. Model later depreciation and utilization. Detailed installation calendar and return on new capacity unknown. |
| Houston leases and property purchase | 2026-08-31 | Include rent, deposits, improvements and purchase spending with consistent lease capitalization. Actual commencement, expenditure and October cash reconciliation pending. |
| Ningbo ten-year lease | 2026-09-10 | Include rent and currency risk in capacity-cost model. Full rent escalation/commencement schedule not modeled. |
| Expected-to-vest employee awards | 2026-06-30 | Include continued SBC cost and a consistent existing-award dilution policy. October vesting/forfeiture/issuance bridge pending. |

## Invalidators and next evidence

1. FY2026 approximately $1.1bn outlook is missed; the implied Q4 step-up is especially demanding.
2. 650,000 monthly nameplate capacity is not qualified, productive or saleable on the stated timetable.
3. 1.6T qualification, component supply or customer acceptance pushes the main ramp beyond 2027.
4. Capital prepayments and factory costs keep growing faster than collections, forcing repeated dilution.
5. Gross margin/EPS miss despite revenue delivery; adjusted net income does not become operating profit.

## Coverage and limitations

current financial and issuer deck verified; post-quarter financing metadata reused from existing verified research. Third-party transcripts may contain timing/transcription inconsistencies. No full commercial transcript stored; no paywall/account bypass. 2025 capacity outcome not scored without an exact matched realized measure.

The source ledger distinguishes readable primary filings/decks/letters, readable third-party transcripts and reused previously verified extracts. Dates refer to publication/event dates rather than URL cache timestamps. Public transcripts were used for summarized management statements, not copied wholesale; no accounts, purchases or paywall bypasses were used. Sources were available as of the cutoff, but this is not a claim to have read every filing, interview or event. Inherited historical series preserve original units and provenance and are not an as-known-then backtest.

baseline-reference.classification: provisional unsupported linear-ramp research assumptions; not a validated base-case valuation
baseline-reference.summary: Provisional research assumptions only. A directional AI-cloud operating hypothesis only: growth, funding, depreciation and post-financing equity claims need a specialist model.

rationale.growth: 85% is a deliberately capped smooth-path hypothesis, not near-term guidance. Latest quarterly growth exceeded 400%, so a single initial rate fading for ten years cannot reproduce the actual capacity ramp.
rationale.targetMargin: 25% is mature EBIT after depreciation, not the reported AI-cloud adjusted EBITDA margin. Reaching it requires sustained utilization, pricing and discipline after the infrastructure buildout.
rationale.tax: 25% is a normalized eventual profitable-state tax assumption. The engine taxes positive EBIT only and does not model jurisdictional loss carryforwards.
rationale.salesCapital: 0.6x means $1.67 of incremental net capital per added $1 of revenue. Hardware/data centers are capital-heavy; this normalized ratio is far less demanding than today’s front-loaded spend and cannot finance the actual ramp.
rationale.terminalROIC: 12% assumes competitive mature infrastructure returns below the constant 15.5% model WACC. A credible model would separately fade risk and capital intensity as the company matures.
rationale.wacc: 15.5% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 2.1 plus a 2-point equity allowance, 10% target debt and a 4-point debt spread reflect severe execution/funding uncertainty; this is not a verified capital structure or a substitute for default scenarios.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
rationale.otherClaims: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not evidence that no additional claims exist. Preserve the existing hard gate: August financing and share exchanges supersede the June balance sheet; post-financing cash, debt, exact shares and equity-linked claims must be reconciled.
rationale.otherAssets: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not a statement that all non-operating assets are absent or worthless. Review assets not already included in snapshot cash and avoid double counting.

scenarioInterpretation.company_build_central: $20bn gross capex annually in 2027–2029; requires robust advances and roughly 50–55% adjusted EBITDA at assumed 3% SBC to preserve the inherited EBIT path. Forward spend, commissioning and unit prices must support this.

scenarioInterpretation.owned_build_stress: $28bn/$26bn/$24bn early cash capex and higher D&A; early margin reset so adjusted EBITDA does not exceed 50% merely to preserve a valuation. More capital does not guarantee the inherited sales path.
scenarioInterpretation.prepaymentMethod: Early new advances assumed 20–40% of cash capex. This is an assumption, not 70% deal-count times 50–60% capex; deal-size weighting is undisclosed. Model recognition and eventual advance runoff.
scenarioInterpretation.maturity: Other WC 3% of incremental revenue; D&A 30% of revenue after 2029. Advances normalize to 25% of annual sales by 2034 and remain stable in 2035–2036 and perpetuity. Explicit years bear every normalization cash use. Before-advance investment coefficient converges to 1.403125, leaving 1.153125 after normal advance growth; the (1+g) factor aligns current-year revenue increments with forward-funded NOPAT*g/ROIC. Final 2036 reinvestment is exactly NOPAT2036*g/ROIC; 2037 FCFF grows exactly 2.5%, with no exceptional terminal adjustment or extra transition years.

formulas.fcff: EBIT - cash tax on EBIT + D&A - gross capital cash spending - increase in other operating working capital + increase in customer advances.
formulas.capitalCashSpending: PPE/intangible cash purchases + capital supplier advances not already in those purchases + capitalized site purchases. Reclassification of existing prepayments/CIP is not a new cash use.
formulas.customerAdvances: Ending = opening + new cash advances - recognized prepaid revenue - refunds (+ FX/acquisition adjustments where applicable).
formulas.fundingNeed: Peak cash uses + debt service + cash reserve - opening usable cash - net cash proceeds actually received - available committed credit draws. FCFF alone omits financing costs and principal maturity timing.
formulas.terminal: Terminal net reinvestment = terminal NOPAT * stable growth / terminal ROIC; customer-advance movement must be included consistently.

cautions: All future investment schedules are analytical sensitivities anchored to disclosed spending/capacity, not disclosed future budgets. Cumulative peaks are not precise financing forecasts.

Economic FCFF retains SBC as compensation expense. Strict cash liquidity adds back noncash SBC and separately subtracts award withholding/buybacks; modeled 1% AAOI and 3% NBIS SBC addbacks below are illustrations, and dilution must be recognized once.

NBIS 2026 guide is modeled as cash-equivalent capital spending. If guidance includes accrued equipment additions, adjust payment timing and vendor-capital payables before using the H2 bridge. $973.3m H1 additions not yet paid cannot simply be added to cash capex twice.
Annual average capacity and gross deployment are distinct. Margin, replacement cost and commissioning schedules must change coherently when the physical build or economic useful life changes.
capital-funding-reconciliation.asOfStubPolicy: The 2026 bridge is a June-to-December liquidity roll-forward. It is separate from 2027–2036 FCFF and is not the full future FCFF stub at October 17. For an October 17 valuation, estimate cash at that date using post-June actual/known transactions and cash use, then include only remaining October 17–December 31 FCFF. Never charge July–October cash uses twice or add June cash plus raises as current excess cash. The disclosed June balance and full H2 envelope bracket rather than verify current cash.

selectedCentralProposal.selection: Selected analytical central owned-build alternative for conditional operating valuation; funding and new customer advances are scenario assumptions.
selectedCentralProposal.anchorClassification: Midpoint of management full-year revenue guidance, not TTM reported revenue or ARR.
selectedCentralProposal.legacyAdapterPolicy: Use explicit gross capital cash spending - D&A + core WC - net customer advance increase. Do not also apply legacy delta-sales/S:C or add forecast deficits as debt. Revenue, WACC, tax, target margin and terminal ROIC otherwise preserved.

terminalTreatment.advanceBalancePolicy: At year 2029 use explicitly accumulated balance. For years 2030 through maturity-year minus two, linearly fade advance/revenue ratio to 0.25; hold at 0.25 thereafter. For general allowed horizon N starting in 2027: fade = min(1,(forecastYearIndex-3)/(N-5)), where forecastYearIndex is 1-based and greater than 3. Thus N=10 completion is forecast year 8 = 2034.
terminalTreatment.advanceDeltaFormula: advanceBalance_t - advanceBalance_(t-1); include in FCFF exactly once. Balance does not run off to zero. Do not add a separate terminal cash adjustment.
terminalTreatment.growthInvestmentTiming: Forward-funded: final-year net investment after advances = NOPAT_final * g / terminalROIC. The smooth gross-capital path approaches a before-advance coefficient [(1+g)/impliedTerminalSalesToCapital + 0.25] times current revenue change, not [1/impliedTerminalSalesToCapital + 0.25].
terminalTreatment.terminalValueFormula: terminalFCFF/(WACC-g), measured at end of final explicit year
terminalTreatment.presentValueFormula: Sum explicit FCFF_t / cumulativeDiscountFactor_t, plus terminalValue / cumulativeDiscountFactor_final. At the FY2026 anchor, cumulativeDiscountFactor_final=(1+WACC)^10. For October17 valuation use the same additional FY2026 stub discount interval as explicit FCFF; do not discount terminal from an inconsistent date.
terminalTreatment.freeFundingPrevention: All normalized advance reductions are charged in explicit years; stable advance growth is subtracted from gross capex/WC investment to deliver the stated net NOPAT*g/ROIC, never added a second time.

companies.dossierMarkdown:
# Nebius (NBIS): forecast and valuation dossier

**Decision:** Withhold a renewed stand-alone base valuation until a specialist capacity, customer-advance, lease and financing model exists. The supplied operating scenarios are useful stress tests, not decision-ready equity defaults. Our conditional base uses $3.2bn calendar-2026 revenue and $9.6bn/$17.28bn/$25.056bn in 2027–2029, with 18% mature EBIT margin. That trajectory does not establish financeability or common-equity value.

**Cutoff:** October 17, 2026. Calendar-year reporter. Latest financials cover June 30 and were published August 12. Annual financials were filed April 30. Later financing and corporate announcements were reviewed through October 1. USD millions unless specified; power is identified in GW or MW. ARR, annual revenue, total contract value and RPO are kept separate.

## A new operating perimeter

The Russian-business divestment in July 2024 and Toloka deconsolidation in 2025 make old Yandex growth and margins poor comparables. Recast continuing revenue was $91.5m in 2024 and $529.8m in 2025. The four 2025 quarters were $50.9m, $105.1m, $146.1m and $227.7m. Q1 2026 revenue reached $399.0m; Q2 reached $582.3m, with AI cloud contributing $574.9m, about 98% of group revenue. TripleTen and Avride remain in consolidated economics, while private investments require separate treatment.

Formal 2026 guidance began in the February 12 call at $3.0–3.4bn revenue, approximately 40% group adjusted EBITDA margin, and $7–9bn December AI-cloud ARR. ARR means final-month AI-cloud revenue multiplied by 12; it is not the year's recognized revenue. The range was reaffirmed in May and August. H1 actual revenue of $981.3m leaves $2,218.7m for H2 to reach the revenue midpoint. No 2027 formal revenue guide is imported into our scenario.

Management increased 2026 capex from $16–20bn in February to $20–25bn on May 13, explaining that spending supports capacity contributing in H1 2027. That is a change in the funding and timing burden, not just a higher revenue forecast. A contracted-power target of 5GW at year-end differs from the 0.8–1.0GW connected-power target and from fully active, billable capacity. The March 4 issuer-hosted leadership interview reinforces the integrated hardware/cloud strategy while acknowledging the realities of the development pipeline.

## Contract visibility has conditions

June RPO was $37,490.6m, with 36% expected in the next 24 months and 40% in the following 24. It includes deferred and unbilled noncancelable revenue subject to recognition constraints, and excludes short-duration contracts. This is not the same measure as every announced TCV or every booking.

The Meta agreement signed March 13 and filed March 16 contains $12bn of dedicated five-year orders beginning deployments in early 2027, plus a potential $15bn backstop for eligible unsold capacity. Third-party revenue on those clusters and Meta purchases of the same unsold capacity cannot both be counted. Service commitments, termination provisions and discounts for late delivery apply. RPO and headline contract values must be reconciled rather than summed as independent assets.

Customer advances improve funding, but June deferred revenue of $5,975.2m represents future performance and can include refundable balances. Management's attractive deal-payback statements are estimates under its utilization, pricing and cost assumptions. They are not evidence of consolidated through-cycle ROIC or unconditional cash available to common shareholders.

## Capital, depreciation and cash quality

FY2025 continuing CFO was $401.9m against $4,066m of PPE/intangible cash purchases. Deferred revenue added $1,565.8m of CFO while receivables consumed $714.6m. D&A was $417.9m and SBC $83.2m; $1,057.7m of purchased PPE/intangibles had not yet been paid. The newer H1 2026 CFO of $4,504.1m is largely explained by $4,395m of deferred-revenue inflow. H1 PPE/intangible cash spending was $8,130.3m, acquisition cash $251.6m, and financing cash inflow $9,160.4m. The H1 supplemental statement also reports $973.3m of acquired PPE/intangibles not yet paid, matching June-end PPE trade payables. This is not additional immediate H1 cash spending. Reconcile opening payables, cash payments, closing payables and other adjustments before comparing accrual capex with a cash funding model.

H1 EBIT remained negative $303.9m, with D&A of $471.7m and SBC of $137.8m, including $74.9m acquisition-related SBC. Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $236.2m and AI-cloud adjusted EBITDA margin of 49.7% therefore do not equal operating profit. The prospective server/network life change from four to five years lowers accounting depreciation; it does not prove that replacement economics improved.

Net PPE is $13,045.2m, including $7,836.4m not yet in use. As assets enter service, depreciation and ongoing operating costs rise. Signed leases not yet commenced add $12,054.1m of undiscounted payments, with $612.4m prepaid; recognized operating lease liabilities are another $1,625.3m. Minimum power commitments total $5,324.1m. These are not all debt deductions to add mechanically, but they cannot disappear because facilities are not yet active.

Our first-year sales-to-capital ratio of 0.30 implies approximately $21.3bn net reinvestment in 2027. The separate $20–30bn gross-capex and $3.5–6bn depreciation ranges are our stress inputs, not issuer guidance. Model GPU cohorts, useful lives, maintenance, datacenter construction, customer advances, rent and power before relying on FCFF. The 18% mature margin and 12% terminal ROIC are conditional judgments; a 15.5% WACC recognizes substantial financing and competitive risk.

## The common-equity bridge is unresolved

June cash was $8,042.1m, with $1,056m restricted. Convertibles had $8,499m carrying value, $10,041.8m nominal maturity amounts and $20,823.7m disclosed fair value. Those are different measurement bases. July introduced a $775m secured facility. August closed $5.75bn of new original-principal notes and exchanged $800m old original principal for approximately 15.8m shares. Accretion, proceeds, fees, repayments and conversion optionality must be rolled on consistent bases.

The 21.065936m NVIDIA pre-funded warrants are effectively paid common equity, with a $0.0001 strike. Basic EPS already includes them, while legal common shares do not; count them once. The June legal count also differs from weighted-average EPS and contains acquisition shares with distinct vesting treatment. An authorization to issue shares is not actual issuance.

ClickHouse's $1,517.7m carrying value reflects a valuation adjustment and security/illiquidity terms, not a simple stale ownership percentage times a headline funding-round value. Toloka preferred is carried at $86.5m. Avride SAFE/milestone liabilities of $178.1m, Tavily holdback/earnout of $19m, and minority claims require consistent subsidiary treatment. The October Inferize announcement does not disclose purchase terms; zero consideration cannot be assumed.

## Management interpretation

Assess Arkady Volozh and the post-divestment team on the new Nebius business. Engineering and product integration have evidence, and financing access has been substantial. Commercial forecasting improved after December 2024 ARR of $90m missed the original $170–190m range. Year-end 2025 active power reached approximately 170MW against a 100MW target, although the distinct 220MW connected-power outcome was not independently resolved. Capacity activation, lifecycle returns, dilution and the ability to monetize differentiation remain open. No generic CEO confidence score is warranted.

Primary financial evidence: [FY2025 annual report, continuing operations recast](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1513845/000110465926052948/nbis-20251231x20f.htm); [June 2026 interim financial statements and notes](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1513845/000110465926094844/nbis-20260812xex99d2.htm). Exact fact/source links are in evidence-NBIS.html#facts and evidence-NBIS.html#sources.

## Guidance track record

Eight consecutive reporting events, Q3 2024 through Q2 2026, were reviewed. No formal standalone quarterly revenue-range series was identified; absence is not zero or a miss. Annual ranges, ARR and aspirations are kept separate.

| Forecast | Earliest verified issue | Later change | Matched outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| December 2024 ARR $170–190m | October 18, 2024 SEC investor deck | Issuer acknowledged miss February 20, 2025 | $90m; 50% below original midpoint |
| FY2024 group revenue $120–130m | October 18, 2024 | Same as-reported perimeter including Toloka | $117.5m, 6% below midpoint |
| March 2025 ARR ≥$220m | February 20, 2025 | None required for match | $249m, above minimum by 13.2% |
| December 2025 ARR $500–1,000m | October 18, 2024 SEC investor deck | Lower bound raised to $750m December 2; $900–1,100m August 7 | $1,250m, above original and revised ranges |
| FY2025 revenue $500–700m including Toloka | October 18, 2024; reaffirmed February 20, 2025 | Ex-Toloka $450–630m; tightened to $500–550m November 11 | $529.8m continuing revenue; within comparable ex-Toloka and final ranges |
| Group adjusted EBITDA positive in H2 2025 | May 20, 2025 | No independently scored reaffirmations | Q4 $15m, met |
| FY2026 revenue / ARR / margin | February 12, 2026; ARR first issued November 2025 | Reaffirmed May and August | Pending at cutoff |
| FY2026 capex $16–20bn | February 12, 2026 | Raised to $20–25bn May 13 | Pending; larger funding burden |

An earlier medium-term 20–30% adjusted EBIT-margin aspiration used a four-year depreciation assumption and has no fixed completion horizon. It is not scored as quarterly guidance.

## Proposed scenarios and scale check

All rows are our analytical scenarios. Stable growth is 2.5%; no case was calibrated to the share price. Normalized positive-profit cash tax is 25%. Loss-year tax benefits are not assumed realizable.

| Case | Explicit early annual growth | Early years / total horizon | Revenue at early-phase end | Revenue at maturity | Mature EBIT margin | WACC | Terminal ROIC |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bear | 100%, 45%, 20% | 3 / 10 | $9.40bn | $18.18bn | 10% | 18% | 8% |
| base | 200%, 80%, 45% | 3 / 10 | $25.06bn | $90.30bn | 18% | 15.5% | 12% |
| bull | 300%, 100%, 60%, 40%, 30% | 5 / 15 | $79.21bn | $309.53bn | 28% | 13% | 17% |

The very large maturity values, especially the bull cases, are feasibility tests, not verified market forecasts. The early phase ends in FY/calendar 2029 for three-year cases and 2031 for five-year cases; maturity is 2036 or 2041. Require a market-share and capital-capacity check before assigning probabilities. Early revenue growth fades to stable growth; capital efficiency then reconciles with terminal margin, tax and ROIC. Full annual paths, net-reinvestment diagnostics and FCFF illustrations are stored in evidence-NBIS.html#judgment. A fiscal/calendar anchor is not the October 17 valuation date: use the appropriate stub period.

The common risk-free input is the October 16 USD 10-year Treasury yield of 5.09%; chosen ERP is 4.5%. Beta, debt spread and weights were not newly measured. WACC values are explicit scenario judgments, not falsely precise empirical estimates. Terminal reinvestment is stable growth divided by terminal ROIC, rather than a free-growth assumption.

## Management capabilities: evidence rather than a single score

| Capability | Assessment | Confidence | Counterexample / limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| demand forecasting | Annual ARR delivery improved, but the record is short and contains a 2024 miss. | moderate | December 2024 ARR forecast of $170–190m was followed by $90m actual, a 50% midpoint miss; FY2024 group revenue also missed $120–130m at $117.5m. |
| product delivery | The integrated platform and cloud growth demonstrate traction; acquired capabilities still need proof. | moderate | Tavily, ClarifAI and Eigen AI add acquisition costs and SBC; standalone profitability is not demonstrated. |
| capacity execution | Physical build-out is substantial, but contracted and active power differ materially. | moderate | Assets not yet in use total $7.836bn; $12.054bn of signed leases have not commenced. |
| cost control | Adjusted EBITDA improved; depreciation and SBC still prevent GAAP operating profit. | mixed, moderate | Q2 EBIT was negative $175.9m, with D&A of $259.7m and SBC of $102.5m. Accounting life increased to five years. |
| capital allocation | Large financing and customer advances support the build, while return and dilution outcomes remain unproven. | moderate-low | June convertible fair value of $20.824bn far exceeds its $8.499bn carrying amount; future rent and power commitments are substantial. |

The JSON records the evidence, sources and leadership attribution for each dimension. Outcomes are team and market results; inherited assets and supply conditions are not assigned entirely to the current CEO.

## Invalidators and next evidence

1. Connected and active MW lag contracted power; customer acceptance delays billable utilization.
2. The $7–9bn December 2026 ARR or $3–3.4bn full-year revenue range is missed or metric definitions change.
3. Customer prepayments are delayed, refunded or insufficient for capex and lease commitments.
4. GPU refresh cycles are shorter than accounting lives, or realized rental prices fall as capacity supply grows.
5. Meta backstop conditions, late delivery or contract termination reduce expected cash recovery.
6. New financing, collateral restrictions or conversion dilution absorbs most common-equity residual.

## Coverage and limitations

June 2026 interim notes and post-quarter announcements through October 1 reviewed; eight consecutive reporting events covered. Original October 18, 2024 investor-deck forecasts recovered and matched.. No matched quarterly revenue-range series was identified. Annual revenue and ARR are recorded separately. Latest official webcasts were not watched. Shareholder letters and selected readable public transcripts were reviewed. Asset URL cache-buster timestamps are not publication dates. Third-party transcripts can mislabel speakers or numerals. Primary documents take precedence. No full commercial transcript copied.

The source ledger distinguishes readable primary filings/decks/letters, readable third-party transcripts and reused previously verified extracts. Dates refer to publication/event dates rather than URL cache timestamps. Public transcripts were used for summarized management statements, not copied wholesale; no accounts, purchases or paywall bypasses were used. Sources were available as of the cutoff, but this is not a claim to have read every filing, interview or event. Inherited historical series preserve original units and provenance and are not an as-known-then backtest.

# Micron (MU): forecast and valuation dossier
As of 17 October 2026. USD millions in JSON; narrative uses USD billions where marked. Research and analytical scenarios, not a price target. No price calibration or CEO valuation multiplier.

## Decision summary
Preserve the reported FY2026 revenue of $133.188bn and GAAP EBIT of $99.340bn. They are real reported results, but an exceptional pricing-cycle endpoint. A flat 8% growth forecast from that annual base misses the much higher exit rate, while perpetuating the latest margin makes scarcity permanent. The preferred analytical base explicitly captures another boom year, then a price/capacity normalization in FY2029–2030. The date of normalization is a judgment, not management guidance.

Use five individually modeled early years and ten years to mature economics. The base reaches a 35% EBIT margin and 12% terminal ROIC, with substantial replacement/reinvestment spending. Refundable customer deposits, tax-payment timing, contingent grants and award dilution prevent an unqualified equity/per-share conclusion. Keep existing release gates.

## 1. Business, mix and the unusual starting point
Micron sells DRAM, NAND and related memory/storage products across cloud, other data-center, mobile/client and automotive/embedded applications. FY2026 product revenue was DRAM $100.679bn, NAND $31.785bn and other, mainly NOR, $0.724bn. Business-unit revenue was CMBU $43.085bn, CDBU $37.592bn, MCBU $36.601bn and AEBU $15.886bn, plus $0.024bn other. Segment-profit measures exclude some consolidated expenses; they must not replace GAAP EBIT. [FY2026 10-K, notes16/20](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723125/000072312526000023/mu-20260903.htm)

The annual period ended September 3 and contained 53 weeks. Revenue rose 256% from FY2025, far faster than physical bit growth. The filing attributes approximately 180% DRAM and 200% NAND average selling-price increases, versus mid-20s bit growth. ### Capitalization and maintenance policy
Reported R&D remains expensed; no synthetic research asset, amortization add-back or starting EBIT rewrite is used. A later capitalization choice must adjust both earnings and invested capital consistently. SBC remains expensed. Maintenance/technology-refresh capex is not separately disclosed: D&A is a consistency proxy, not a claim that accounting depreciation equals economic replacement. After year5, D&A is assumed at18% of sales, with no additional grant cash. Base year10 gross capex is $50.09bn versus D&A $38.66bn; positive growth still requires additional capital. Tool inflation, obsolescence and uncommenced leases can require more cash than this proxy; the downside does not assume immediate factory liquidation. ## 6. Management capabilities, with limits
Sanjay Mehrotra has been CEO sinceMay 2017 and chairman sinceJanuary 2025; Mark Murphy CFO sinceApril 2022. August 2026 expanded Bhatia/DeBoer operating/technology roles are organizational changes with limited outcome history. The same leadership era includes the FY2023 downturn. No reputation score is assigned.

- **Demand forecasting (medium confidence):** Strong near-term visibility in the observed boom; through-cycle forecasting remains uncertain. Evidence/outcome: 8 consecutive revenue outcomes at or above original midpoint; six above original range. SCAs make portions of minimum demand/pricing enforceable. FY2026Q2 and Q3 revenue exceeded original midpoints by roughly 27.6% and 23.7%, indicating material underforecasting during scarcity. Counterevidence: FY2023 operating loss and earlier inventory correction show cyclicality persists. FY2025Q2 gross margin was below midpoint; recent sample omits a completed downturn. Customer purchases to fulfill commitments can build inventories and amplify the next bust.
- **Product delivery (medium-high confidence):** Recent execution has tangible shipment/qualification evidence; next-generation wins remain conditional. Evidence/outcome: HBM4 entered volume production in FY2026. 1-gamma and G9 are largest production nodes as of Q4; data-center SSD and server-memory products shipping. Mix and share opportunity are real, but FY2026 revenue growth was dominated by ASP. Counterevidence: Sampling/custom-HBM4E design work is not production revenue. 2027 node volume-production milestones are not yet achieved.
- **Capacity execution (medium confidence):** Multiple construction milestones are visible; future US/Japan/Singapore ramps still require yield and schedule proof. Evidence/outcome: FY2026 gross PP&E cash spending $30.712bn; net PP&E $63.310bn. ID1 mid-2027, ID2 late-2028, New York 2030 plans extend capacity visibility. FY2026 supply expanded in mid-20s bit terms, far below nominal revenue increase. Counterevidence: Initial wafer output precedes meaningful run-rate by quarters. Grants, construction and tools add execution/financing exposure during a price downturn.
- **Cost control (high for attribution; medium for durability confidence):** Manufacturing progress supports economics, but peak margins mostly reflect price rather than permanent cost advantage. Evidence/outcome: FY2026 DRAM ASP approximately +180%, NAND +200%, versus mid-20s bit growth. GAAP margin improves sharply; Q4 incentive compensation and community investment raised expenses. No basis for assigning all 74.6% FY2026 EBIT margin to management skill. Counterevidence: Q4 operating expense exceeded originally guided level after compensation decisions. Cost absorption and lagged inventory expense change as output/utilization normalizes.
- **Capital allocation (medium confidence):** Deleveraging and financial flexibility improved; unprecedented capacity commitment remains untested across a full cycle. Evidence/outcome: FY2026 debt repayment $10.043bn; stock repurchases $650m; $1.333bn SBC remains an economic cost. Customer deposits and grants supplement operating cash. Balance-sheet strength rose, but $12.747bn refundable deposits are not unencumbered economic surplus. Counterevidence: $10.8bn longer-term purchase commitments; cost and subsidy clawback exposure. 100% excess-cash return intention is not a defined guaranteed distribution.

Source mapping, tenure and evidence are in `evidence-MU.html#management`. Capability affects execution timing, cost assumptions and scenario width; it does not earn a mechanical valuation multiplier.

## 7. What changes the conclusion
Monitor realized DRAM/NAND pricing separately from bits; contracted volumes versus customer inventories; SCA floor renegotiation/default; the FY2027 sequential path; fab construction versus economically usable yields; grant collection/clawback; cash taxes; and incremental returns on the enlarged asset base. Earlier price reversal, persistent oversupply or weaker contract enforcement moves toward bear. Evidence of durable differentiated margins after supply expansion could justify bull. A demand forecast is not confirmed merely by customer capital-spending announcements.

companies.dossierMarkdown:
# Broadcom forecast and valuation dossier
As of 2026-10-17. USD amounts unless stated. Provisional scenarios, with unresolved financing and equity-value gates.

## What changes the base case
Latest quarterly revenue was $29.591bn, up 86% year over year; GAAP EBIT $15.955bn, a 53.92% margin. Latest TTM revenue/EBIT were $89.104bn/$42.814bn. AI is accelerating far faster than the old undifferentiated 35% growth assumption, but memory pass-through, customer concentration and financing support make a simple high-margin extrapolation incomplete.

[September 2 issuer results](https://investors.broadcom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/broadcom-inc-announces-third-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-financial) cover FY2026 Q3 ended August 2. The [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1730168/000173016826000080/avgo-20260802.htm) was accepted September 9 at 21:56:42 UTC and filed September 10. Latest actuals and contractual terms are separated from management outlooks below.

## Business, mix and historical development
Quarterly semiconductors were $20.839bn, 70.4% of revenue; infrastructure software $8.752bn, 29.6%. AI semiconductors were $16.7bn, a subset of semiconductors and 56.4% of total revenue, up 221% year over year and 54% sequentially. The balance includes slower non-AI chips and VMware/other software, so applying AI growth to the entire company would overstate the forecast. Semiconductor/software revenue progressed from $12.515bn/$6.796bn in Q1 to $15.009bn/$7.178bn in Q2 and $20.839bn/$8.752bn in Q3. Q2 segments are derived from nine-month less Q1 and Q3 figures.

Annual revenue growth was 7.9% in FY2023, 44.0% in FY2024 and 23.9% in FY2025. FY2024 includes VMware acquisition effects and is not organic growth. GAAP EBIT margins were 45.2%, 26.1% and 39.9%; acquisition amortization and restructuring complicate comparisons. FY2025 revenue/EBIT were $63.887bn/$25.484bn. Annual financial and source history is in evidence-AVGO.html#facts.

## Guidance, revisions and leadership context
Q4 FY2026 issuer guidance is approximately $34.8bn corporate revenue, $21.7bn AI revenue and 66% non-GAAP operating margin. Q4 ends November 1 and has not been reported at cutoff. The [September 2 public call transcript](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/avgo/transcripts/685349-q3-2026/) raises FY2026 AI revenue from $56bn to $58bn and FY2027 from over $100bn to approximately $115bn, adding FY2028 $230bn. Those are AI-segment forecasts reported in a public secondary transcript, not independently issuer-document-verified official guidance. They are future and unscored, not consolidated revenue or binding customer cash obligations. Management said it did not intend to update the multi-year trajectory quarterly.

Management described supply secured against these plans but also depends on customer sites, land/power/shell and financing. Customer GW deployment plans are not booked revenue. Q4 capex outlook was $1.4bn, reflecting growing direct capacity investment. Memory pass-through reduces percentage gross margin; strong revenue growth can coexist with lower gross-margin percentage.

The March 20, 2024 [issuer investor-day slides](https://investors.broadcom.com/static-files/4378d14e-a52f-409f-9ae4-03d810bc7a6c) show multi-generation custom-accelerator strategy and an early $10bn-plus FY2024 AI outlook. A future million-accelerator cluster illustration is a scale vision, not corporate financial guidance. Hock Tan's June 5 Bloomberg Tech interview was read through a public transcription, with primary-host event metadata checked; no video was watched. His account of an early customer bet and competition with customer insourcing informs risk interpretation, not a numerical credibility score.

## Like-for-like guidance record
| Target period | Original date | Revenue guide, $bn | Actual, $bn | Error vs midpoint/point | Result |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| FY2024Q4 | 2024-09-05 | 14.000 approx. | 14.054 | 0.39% | above |
| FY2025Q1 | 2024-12-12 | 14.600 approx. | 14.916 | 2.16% | above |
| FY2025Q2 | 2025-03-06 | 14.900 approx. | 15.004 | 0.70% | above |
| FY2025Q3 | 2025-06-05 | 15.800 approx. | 15.952 | 0.96% | above |
| FY2025Q4 | 2025-09-04 | 17.400 approx. | 18.015 | 3.53% | above |
| FY2026Q1 | 2025-12-11 | 19.100 approx. | 19.311 | 1.10% | above |
| FY2026Q2 | 2026-03-04 | 22.000 approx. | 22.187 | 0.85% | above |
| FY2026Q3 | 2026-06-03 | 29.400 approx. | 29.591 | 0.65% | above |

Eight consecutive corporate revenues exceeded original approximate point forecasts, with mean signed error +1.29%. Unlike NVIDIA's ±2% ranges, Broadcom's approximate points do not specify comparable probability coverage. Seven adjusted-EBITDA-margin forecasts also have matched actual dollar numerators/denominators. The Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA forecast is retained as unmatched: the current release switches to non-GAAP operating income and no comparable EBITDA actual was found. Substitution would be a definition error.

Separate annual evidence: FY2024 original $50bn guidance on December 7, 2023, revised to $51bn on June 12, 2024, versus $51.574bn actual on December 12. Original and revised errors are preserved separately. Unseasoned FY2027/2028 targets are not scored as successes. Full dates, units, sources, error formulas and exceptions are in evidence-AVGO.html#guidance.

## Earnings quality, cash investment and ROIC
Q3 non-GAAP operating income was $20.095bn versus GAAP $15.955bn; exclusions include $2.019bn SBC and $2.006bn acquisition intangible amortization. A 67.91% non-GAAP operating margin cannot be used as GAAP EBIT without a reconciliation. Segment profit also excludes corporate items.

Nine-month CFO was $32.950bn, capex $1.013bn, depreciation $484m and intangible/right-of-use amortization $6.047bn. SBC was $6.287bn. Receivables and inventory absorbed $8.797bn; payables provided $2.313bn. The existing historical D&A mapping is depreciation-only for Broadcom, an important model gap. ROU amortization also needs a consistent lease convention. Physical capex alone understates economic capital deployed through customer finance and purchase commitments. The latest filing also says most new software contracts no longer permit termination for convenience; additional license recognition contributed to Q3 growth. Distinguish recognition timing from recurring demand when forecasting VMware.

Reported book sales/capital ratios reflect $97.801bn goodwill and $26.325bn intangibles at August 2, not an organic factory efficiency measure. The FY2025 effective tax rate was negative because of discrete items, unsuitable as a normalized operating rate. A 20% normalized tax rate, 2x forward incremental sales/capital and 20% terminal ROIC are explicit judgments, not reported operating facts.

## Obligations and asset bridge: unresolved
The evidence-AVGO.html#judgment register contains source, measurement date, conditionality and treatment for:
- $59.419bn carrying debt, $23.975bn cash and the incomplete current lease reconciliation.
- $126.821bn enforceable purchase commitments, including $52.674bn FY2027 and $72.952bn FY2028. The schedule excludes cancelable-without-penalty agreements and remaining terms of one year or less, so it is not total near-term procurement.
- $3.941bn other contracts; $1.755bn uncertain-timing tax benefits/interest/penalties excluded from that schedule.
- The customer-financing backstop: maximum $29bn undiscounted after all rack deployment. It covers a default-related difference between 85% of outstanding lease obligations and asset-disposal proceeds over five-year leases, with alternative remedies. Reported fair value was immaterial and no payment had occurred. Maximum contractual exposure is not expected loss or funded debt.
- Up to $42bn conditional notes that the customer may issue TO Broadcom for customer lease obligations. None existed at August 2. This is potential investment/funding exposure, not Broadcom convertible debt. Reconcile its overlap with the backstop before modeling simultaneous losses.
- 165m unvested RSUs, $18.221bn unrecognized SBC over 2.9 years, versus 4,773.629865m cover shares on August 28. Future compensation expense is not award fair value. Current holdings beyond cash remain unreconciled.

One distributor was 50% of quarterly revenue; the top five end customers approximately 55%. These overlap and cannot be added. The same concentration can damage operating revenue, receivables, financing recoveries and supplier obligations simultaneously. No unconditional $29bn/$42bn deduction or zero-claim assumption is appropriate.

## Provisional scenarios and scale check
| Scenario | Early years / annual growth | Total years | Mature revenue, $bn | Mature EBIT margin | Sales/capital | Tax | WACC | Terminal ROIC |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| base | 3: 75%/65%/30% | 10 | 837.7 | 45% | 2.0x | 20% | 11% | 20% |
| bull | 5: 85%/80%/40%/25%/18% | 15 | 1,502.5 | 52% | 2.5x | 20% | 10% | 25% |
| bear | 3: 40%/10%/-10% | 10 | 100.3 | 30% | 1.3x | 20% | 13% | 12% |

Annual growth fades linearly after early years to 2.5% terminal growth. Base GAAP EBIT margins are 53/55/54%, then fade to 45% by year 10. These are rolling 12-month periods after August 2. Illustratively, management AI forecasts plus an analyst $50bn non-AI/software layer imply fiscal corporate revenue around $165bn/$280bn for FY2027/FY2028; rolling base years 1/2 are $155.932bn/$257.288bn. This is not management consolidated guidance and needs a quarterly bridge.

Base mature sales $837.7bn and bull $1.50trn are strong scale requirements. Three explicit early years fit current customer ramps; a 10-year base is preferable to an unsupported 20-year runway. The 15-year bull tests durable custom-silicon/networking/software economics. WACC 11% versus the old 10% is a rounded risk judgment, using common October 16 Treasury 5.09% and chosen 4.5% ERP as context; no measured issuer beta/spread is claimed. The bull/base/bear ranges are not probabilities or market-price-calibrated outputs.

## Management capabilities and failure conditions
Observed strengths are conservative short-horizon revenue guidance, custom-silicon execution, operating leverage and historical cash conversion/debt repayment. Evidence is less mature for expanded customer financing. Hock Tan led throughout; Kirsten Spears was CFO through June 12, 2026, then Amie Thuener. Do not attribute the whole history to the new CFO. Product insourcing, site delays, customer funding, memory cost/mix, VMware renewal economics and contingent loss/recovery are the main invalidators. The dimension-specific evidence-AVGO.html#management preserves counterexamples.

## Source limits and adoption gate
Primary releases, current/annual SEC filings and investor-day slides were reviewed. A readable issuer-hosted call transcript was not found, so public Quartr direct-speech transcriptions are labeled as secondary; dates and quarterly figures are corroborated with issuer sources. No video/audio was watched, no full commercial transcript stored and no paywall bypass used. No analyst consensus archive was collected. evidence-AVGO.html#sources lists gaps. These scenarios cannot become final valuation defaults until capital, lease, fiscal-period and contingent-credit bridges are completed. No app edits or price calibration were made.
