companies.dossierMarkdown:
# TSMC (TSM): forecast and valuation dossier
As of 17 October 2026. Native TWD millions in JSON; narrative often uses TWD trillions. USD figures are explicitly labeled. Research assumptions, not a price target. Currency and ADS gates remain active.

## Decision summary
TSMC's leading-node/advanced-packaging position and recent execution support strong near-term growth and longer persistence than a commodity-memory supplier. They do not justify compounding management's2024–2029 target for five fresh years from today. The preferred base starts with the TIFRS TTM revenue of TWD4.944817tr, models five explicit early years, and fades growth/returns across15 years. The base reaches46% EBIT margin,18% terminal ROIC and2% terminal growth, with capital intensity rising as growth matures.

TTM accounting, flow FX, valuation-date spot FX and the5ordinary-shares-per-ADS ratio must remain separate. No per-ADS output is released until current claims, share precision and date-consistent spot FX are reconciled.

## 1. Business, mix and operating evidence
TSMC is a dedicated foundry with one reportable foundry segment. Platform and technology mixes describe revenue drivers, not independently valued operating segments. Q3 revenue mix was HPC68%, smartphone21%, IoT4%, automotive4%, digital consumer1% and other2%. HPC is broader than AI accelerators. Wafer-revenue mix was2nm8%,3nm33%,5nm28%,7nm10%, older21%; 7nm-and-below represented79%. North American customers contributed79% of revenue. [Q3 management report](https://investor.tsmc.com/english/encrypt/files/encrypt_file/reports/2026-10/f83780000ddc0c3b48e57a87eab6814c4ab35058/3Q26%20ManagementReport.pdf)

Q3 revenue was TWD1.494243tr, EBIT TWD0.876445tr and parent net income TWD0.763064tr. TWD revenue grew50.9% while USD revenue grew41.2%, and12-inch-equivalent wafer shipments grew9.6% to4.476m. Thus mix, realized value per wafer and currency, not just units, drive growth. The FY2025 top-ten customers accounted for78% of revenue; the largest two represented19% and17%. Customer names are not inferred from those anonymous disclosures. [Q3 financials](https://investor.tsmc.com/english/encrypt/files/encrypt_file/reports/2026-10/3a94d1034b9e6b22446b674f7aaf3d088a12a193/FS.pdf), [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1046179/000162828026025362/tsm-20251231.htm)

| Historical annual IASB IFRS context | Revenue TWD tr | EBIT TWD tr | EBIT margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2023 | 2.162 | 0.921 | 42.6% |
| 2024 | 2.894 | 1.322 | 45.7% |
| 2025 | 3.809 | 1.936 | 50.8% |

The2023 decline from 2022 provides a cycle counterexample. Those annual numbers are separately labeled IASB IFRS. They are not blindly combined with local quarterly statements. Current TTM is FY2025 **TIFRS** +9M2026TIFRS −9M2025TIFRS: revenue TWD4,944,817.272m, EBIT2,866,916.677m and tax505,293.060m. IASB IFRS and local TIFRS tax/net income differ. The research retains the supplied TIFRS TTM basis instead of splicing incompatible annual and interim amounts. [Local FY2025 statements](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1046179/000104617926000024/a2025q4consolidatedreport-.htm)

## 2. Cash generation and capital intensity
The latest9M2026 statements show CFO TWD2.402117tr, gross PP&E capex1.289971tr and D&A0.584192tr. These are **nine-month**, not TTM, cash flows. Q3 alone shows CFO0.919776tr, capex0.443206tr and D&A0.220204tr. The combined working-capital-and-other cash line is −0.251447tr year-to-date and cannot be presented as pure NWC. Receivable days were28 and inventory days82. [Q3 financial statements](https://investor.tsmc.com/english/encrypt/files/encrypt_file/reports/2026-10/3a94d1034b9e6b22446b674f7aaf3d088a12a193/FS.pdf)

For full-year2025 TIFRS, CFO was TWD2.274976tr, gross capex1.272411tr, D&A0.688096tr, cash income taxes0.267557tr and SBC TWD1,246.070m. CFO less PP&E capex was1.002565tr before intangibles/lease-principal adjustments. This fills previously absent cash-flow context without manufacturing a TTM flow from9M data. [FY2025 TIFRS filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1046179/000104617926000024/a2025q4consolidatedreport-.htm)

Reported Q3 ROE45.5% is not ROIC. A current, clean average-invested-capital return remains unresolved because refundable receipts, operating cash, leases, foreign-fab NCI and investments need consistent classification. Our terminalROIC 18% is a forward judgment, materially below current earnings-based indications, not a relabeled management ROE target. Increasing equipment cost and overseas fabs can reduce incremental returns even while revenue and accounting profits rise.

## 3. Original guidance versus matched outcomes
The ledger uses eight consecutive quarters, original next-quarter USD revenue, TIFRS gross margin and operating margin, with actual publication dates and source IDs. It retains original FX assumptions and actual average FX because currency explains some margin variance.

| Actual period | Original guide date | Revenue guide → actual (USD bn) | Result; midpoint error | gross / operating margin: original → actual |

All projected growth, margins, tax, capital efficiency, discount rates and timing below are analyst judgments. There is no price calibration or scenario probability.

Years1–5 are rolling annual periods ending September 2027–2031, from the current TTM. They are not calendarFY2027growth overcalendarFY2026. The base combines leading-node/HPC and packaging growth with moderation in smartphone and mature nodes. Revenue reaches TWD11.605tr in year5 and18.080tr in year15,3.66times the starting scale. The bull reaches29.440tr, requiring sustained high-value mix, capacity and industry demand far beyond today's level. Base early marginal sales/capital ratios are1.30,1.25,1.20,1.15 and1.10x. Positive sales increments divided by those ratios produce net reinvestment; the ratio later fades to0.489x, consistent with18% terminalROIC and36.8% after-tax margin. D&A rises from17% toward20% of sales and NWC is modeled at5% as audit assumptions, not asserted historical ratios. Implied capex = D&A + net reinvestment − changeNWC; do not subtract that capex again. It is an approximate consistency check, not a reconstruction of gross management capex after grant/accrual/FX timing. The bear contraction year retains an8%-of-revenue net-reinvestment floor instead of fictitious liquidation.

SBC remains an expense, with a0.05%-of-revenue reserve slightly above2025 reported intensity. Low historical SBC does not remove award/share-count checks. Ordinary grant economics are embedded in net capital efficiency; there is no additional free grant asset. Overseas ramp costs are embedded in declining margins; do not subtract3–4points again.

Fifteen years permits several technology and overseas-fab generations before mature economics. Ten years would compress an unusually durable but fading ecosystem advantage; twenty would prolong a speculative high-growth tail. After year5 the base growth schedule is8%,7%,6%,5%,4.5%,4%,3.5%,3%,2.5%,2%, then perpetual2%. Mature EBIT46% is below current~58% TTM and reflects mix/utilization/foreign-cost normalization.

## 5. WACC, units and mechanical valuation audit
Native TWD flows use nominal TWD WACC: base10%, bull8.5%, bear13%. Construction begins with the verified October 16 USD10-year5.09% and judgmentERP4.5%, beta/debt spread/weights and risk allowances, then translates using assumed long-run USD inflation2.5% andTWD1.5%. These are scenario assumptions, not measured current TWD risk-free rates or observed beta/spreads. Exact inputs and common-market reference are in `evidence-TSM.html#judgment`. Currency-specific risk adjustment is not a substitute for a separate Taiwan continuity scenario.

Mechanics: base: operating EV 46.75 TWD tr, terminal PV 38.6%; bull: operating EV 105.45 TWD tr, terminal PV 51.7%; bear: operating EV 15.12 TWD tr, terminal PV 22.9%. These are native operating values before claims, precise stub timing and currency/share conversion. Terminal reinvestment = growth/ROIC; growth remains below WACC. A higher terminal return without evidence would reduce required investment and inflate value.

TheQ3 flow rate31.983 and9M31.744 translate income/flows. TheSeptember 30balance-sheet spot31.880 is neither theQ3average nor verified valuation-date spot. Once the bridge is complete, TWD equity per ordinary share is divided by independently verified valuation-date TWD/USD and multiplied by5 to obtainUSDper ADS. Dividing TWDenterprisevalue directly byADSshares, using flow FX for equity, or omitting the5x ratio are release-blocking errors.


### Capitalization and maintenance policy
Reported R&D remains expensed; no synthetic research asset, amortization add-back or starting EBIT rewrite is used. A later capitalization choice must adjust both earnings and invested capital consistently. SBC remains expensed. Maintenance/technology-refresh capex is not separately disclosed: D&A is a consistency proxy, not a claim that accounting depreciation equals economic replacement. The later D&A audit is20% of sales. Base year15 implied capex is TWD4.323tr versus D&A3.616tr, retaining substantial replacement plus growth spending. Tool inflation, obsolescence and uncommenced leases can require more cash than this proxy; the downside does not assume immediate factory liquidation. Cash-flow capitalization/lease reconciliation remains a final implementation gate.

## 7. Management capabilities and counterevidence
C.C. Wei has been CEO sinceJune 2018 and chairman sinceJune 2024, following a co-CEO role fromNovember 2013. Wendell Huang has been CFO sinceSeptember 2019 andSVP sinceFebruary 2024. This tenure permits meaningful execution review, but does not isolate their contribution from customer architectures, ecosystem strength, currency and industry conditions. [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1046179/000162828026025362/tsm-20251231.htm)

- **Demand forecasting (medium-high short term, medium long term confidence):** Strong recent quarterly execution and conservative ranges; multiyear demand remains a judgment. Evidence/outcome: Eight consecutive reported quarters meet or exceed original USD revenue range; five above, three within. Management checks customers and their customers and now reports checking data-center build-outs/power. Supports a strong near-term starting path, not automatic 25% growth from today. Counterevidence: Raising 2026 capex from $52-56bn to $60-64bn demonstrates forecast revision rather than perfect foresight. 2023 revenue declined in the historical record. Demand signals may overlap across customers; signed product plans are not end-user monetization.
- **Product delivery (high recent, medium forward confidence):** Leading-node ramp has revenue and yield evidence; future A14 remains a roadmap. Evidence/outcome: N2 entered high-volume production Q4 2025 and accounts for 8% of Q3 2026 wafer revenue. 7nm-and-below is 79% of wafer revenue. Demonstrated ability to monetize leading nodes, enabling measured persistence in margin/returns. Counterevidence: A14 2027 risk/2028 volume-production objectives are not realized. Node mix and competitor yield improvements can change advantage quickly.
- **Capacity execution (medium-high confidence):** Operational ramp competence is visible, with larger overseas execution burden ahead. Evidence/outcome: Arizona first fab high-volume production confirmed in Q4 2024. N2 now ramps across Hsinchu/Kaohsiung; capacity expected to more than double in 2027. Capacity delivers current shipments, but almost 20 fab projects make forward workload unusually large. Counterevidence: Overseas dilution increases as several fabs open. Tool availability, power/water, skills, labor and subsidies can delay economically usable output.
- **Cost control (medium-high confidence):** Better utilization and productivity repeatedly beat margin guidance; FX and mix must be separated from skill. Evidence/outcome: Q3 2026 58.7% EBIT margin versus 56-58% guide; Q2 60.3% versus 56.5-58.5%. Q3 gross margin fell 1.3 points as N2 ramp diluted margins, as directionally anticipated. Justifies above-industry mature economics, with explicit fade for foreign-fab cost. Counterevidence: 2025Q3 favorable currency versus guide helped margins; not all beat is cost control. N2 and overseas costs can outlast productivity gains.
- **Capital allocation (medium-high historical, medium forecast confidence):** Investment has supported profitable growth, but new capex is a demanding long-duration commitment. Evidence/outcome: FY2025 operating cash flow TWD2.275tr versus capex TWD1.272tr. Current balance sheet has substantial cash/investments; regular dividends. Model requires reinvestment and returns decay; no valuation premium solely for leadership reputation. Counterevidence: Higher construction/tool cost per wafer and foreign fab economics may depress future incremental returns. Cash/ROE is not ROIC; refundable customer receipts and NCI/leases affect claims. Taiwan continuity risk is outside management control.

Each domain has evidence, outcome, confidence, counterexamples and source IDs in `evidence-TSM.html#management`. No management reputation score or automatic valuation multiplier is used.

## 8. Risks, invalidators and research gates
Watch leading-node utilization versus added capacity; N2/A14 qualification and yields; CoWoS/packaging throughput; customer concentration; overseas fab cost and subsidies; supplier/tool/energy inflation; export restrictions; and power/water continuity. More wafer revenue per unit can reflect value creation but also creates exposure to high-end demand concentration. Multi-quarter revenue shortfalls, slower node qualification or foreign-margin dilution beyond the modeled path invalidate the base. Customer capex announcements and overlapping forecasts do not prove ultimate demand or monetization.

Taiwan geopolitical disruption, earthquakes and operational concentration deserve explicit stress scenarios. A few WACC points cannot faithfully encode total interruption or asset loss. The annual filing recorded earthquake-related losses in 2024/2025, demonstrating nonzero physical disruption risk; the proposed bear assumes continued operation. [Annual risks and note37](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1046179/000162828026025362/tsm-20251231.htm)

Research covered current quarter, eight matched guidance quarters, annual/local filings and readable prepared/Q&A transcripts. No video/audio watched claim is made. `evidence-TSM.html#facts` labels units/accounting/periods, `evidence-TSM.html#sources` supplies status/date/URLs, and missing current cash-flow/lease/claim data remain explicitly missing. Required next reconciliation: current customer receipts and leases, minority economic value, investment composition, award/share precision, valuation-date FX and post-quarter bridge. No production-app changes were made; public per-share output stays null.

analystJudgment.growthCurrencyPolicy: Forecast nominal TWD revenue from TIFRS TTM. USD management guidance is a separate plausibility check; no mixing flow FX with spot equity FX. First-year next-12-month growth is not FY2027 over FY2026 calendar growth.
analystJudgment.reinvestmentPolicy: Net reinvestment = positive incremental revenue / marginal sales-capital, with an 8%-of-revenue floor in the bear contraction year. D&A/NWC/capex are a consistency audit, not additional deductions. Marginal capital efficiency fades to ROIC/(margin*(1-tax)) by maturity, making terminal economics coherent.
analystJudgment.capexInterpretation: First-year base implied gross capex is about one-third of revenue, close to the recent capital-spending scale. Capex and D&A depend on equipment timing; fixed replacement needs mean low-growth downside cannot assume cash liquidation of fab assets.
analystJudgment.sbcPolicy: Expense recurring compensation in EBIT; 0.05% of forecast revenue is an analytical reserve, slightly above FY2025 reported SBC intensity. Do not infer no dilution from low reported SBC.

equityBridge.notes: Do not double-add long-term equity-method assets if operating income/value includes their economics. FY2025 lease and customer deposit values are stale references, not current claims. Verify current claims, share precision, and valuation-date FX before release.

invalidators: Leading-node customer demand or effective utilization falls below capacity additions for multiple quarters.
N2/A14 qualification, yields or packaging throughput miss customer production windows.
Overseas ramp dilution materially exceeds 3-4 points, or tool/energy inflation outstrips strategic pricing.
A few major customers reduce orders, insource a meaningful share, or shift to competing foundries.
Export controls, power/water disruptions or Taiwan geopolitical events impair continuity; a normal WACC increment cannot fully represent asset-loss tail risk.

valuationTimingPolicy.operatingModelConvention: end-of-year discounting from latest reported annual/TTM baseline; illustrative operating EV only
valuationTimingPolicy.unresolved: Precise stub-period cash generation, distributions, new financings and post-balance-sheet claims must be rolled to valuation date before per-share release.

analystJudgment.forecastStatus: Independent analytical scenarios; all current and unresolved claims retained; no implementable equity recommendation or per-share output.
analystJudgment.grantTreatment: Marginal sales/capital represents net economic reinvestment after ordinary support; no separate grant asset or cash grant added. Implied gross capex is an audit proxy before a detailed grants/accruals bridge, not a precise management capex reconstruction.

capitalizationPolicy.reportedEBITBasis: Reported GAAP operating income for MU; TIFRS operating income for TSM. No synthetic starting-margin rewrite.
capitalizationPolicy.researchAndDevelopment: Keep reported R&D expensed. No research-asset capitalization or amortization adjustment has been made. If a later model capitalizes R&D, it must restate both operating profit and invested capital consistently across history and forecast.
capitalizationPolicy.softwareAndLeases: Maintain reported treatment in starting facts; detailed software/intangible additions and lease roll-forwards remain in final cash-flow reconciliation. Do not capitalize operating expenses merely to lift margins.
capitalizationPolicy.SBC: Recurring SBC remains an expense; no add-back that ignores dilution.

maintenanceAndCapitalPath.maintenanceDefinition: Economic replacement and technology-refresh spend is not separately reported. D&A is an audit proxy, not evidence that economic maintenance equals accounting depreciation.
maintenanceAndCapitalPath.earlyYears: MU direct gross capex/grants/D&A/NWC in years1–5; TSM net reinvestment with implied capex/D&A audit. Fixed commitments and technology refresh remain during downside.
maintenanceAndCapitalPath.laterGrants: MU cash-grant forecast ends after year5; TSM ordinary support embedded in net capital-efficiency judgment, with no extra asset.
maintenanceAndCapitalPath.stressTest: Replacement/tool inflation or faster node obsolescence requires higher investment and/or lower ROIC. Negative revenue growth never automatically releases factory book capital.

currencyConsistencyChoice.method: Nominal native-TWD cash flows and terminal growth discounted at nominal TWD WACC.
currencyConsistencyChoice.formula: (1 + USD WACC) * (1 + expected TWD inflation) / (1 + expected USD inflation) - 1
currencyConsistencyChoice.limitation: Long-run Fisher/relative-inflation consistency assumption, not an empirically estimated FX path or observed TWD market rate. Risk allowances are analytical judgments. Current USD spot conversion remains a separate gate.
currencyConsistencyChoice.implementationGate: Do not substitute USD WACC for TWD WACC; any implementation must preserve this explicit native-currency method or independently rebuild USD cash flows with an explicit FX path.

methodology.scope: These defaults apply only to a fresh or explicitly reset current-company draft matching the named snapshot. Existing user edits and historical/frozen experiments must not change.
methodology.growth: Except for the documented AAOI staged profile, year 1 uses growth, then annual growth fades linearly to terminalGrowth in year 10. It is not a constant ten-year CAGR. Economic checks show the resulting size and CAGR.
methodology.margin: Except for the documented AAOI staged profile, reported baseline EBIT margin fades linearly to targetMargin by year 10, except an explicitly disclosed starting-EBIT normalization. Target margin is operating EBIT after ongoing R&D, SBC and depreciation, not gross margin, EBITDA or an adjusted EPS margin.
methodology.reinvestment: Net reinvestment = max(0, change in revenue / salesCapital). Ratios are independent forward judgments, not mechanically copied from total sales/book-capital or capex/sales. Gross maintenance capex, R&D capitalization and replacement cycles are not separately modeled.
methodology.tax: Normalized blended operating cash-tax estimates apply to positive EBIT only. Reported accounting effective rates are evidence, not marginal cash-tax forecasts; tax-loss carryforwards are not modeled.
methodology.wacc: WACC is an assumed nominal required return, never issuer-reported. Use observed USD Treasury 5.09% on 2026-10-16, an explicitly chosen 4.5% equity premium informed by January 2026’s 4.23% estimate, and assumed beta, target market-value debt weight and debt spread. The January premium is not an October observation. Round model WACC to 0.5 percentage points; betas and weights are not measured live. TSM uses a separately disclosed assumed currency conversion.
methodology.terminal: Stable growth is modest nominal growth in the model currency, below WACC and terminal ROIC. Terminal reinvestment/NOPAT = g/ROIC. Mature returns normally fall from explicit-period productivity; a discrete year-11 transition remains a simplification.
methodology.bridge: otherClaims=0 and otherAssets=0 are unreviewed numerical placeholders, not verified absence or fair values. No reviewed flags, financing reconciliation or share conversion is implied. Explicit specialist and claim-related gates take precedence over these defaults.
methodology.validation: Deterministic operating-path checks and lower/higher operating cases are model sanity tests, not calibrated probabilities. No stock price or future return is used to choose assumptions.
methodology.evidence: Primary issuer releases and exact current filing sources available by 2026-10-17 anchor judgments. Historical annual data are latest-reported context and may include recasts; structural breaks are disclosed.
methodology.companySpecificPath: AAOI fresh research uses the documented staged capacity profile. Growth/margin progression and capital-intensity terminal fade are applied to every deterministic and simulated case. Other companies retain the original linear transition.

AAPL.name: Apple Inc.

rationale.growth: 8% starts above FY2025 growth of 6.4% but below the latest 16% quarter. Services and replacement demand support growth; the installed base and hardware maturity argue for an immediate fade rather than extrapolating one strong quarter.

rationale.tax: 20% is a normalized blended cash-tax judgment above FY2025 accounting tax of 15.6%; one-off tax charges, geographic mix and minimum-tax changes make any single reported rate a weak long-run anchor.

rationale.terminalROIC: 20% retains a brand/ecosystem advantage but materially reduces returns on new capital from the explicit-period margin/capital combination.
rationale.wacc: 9.0% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.0, modest 10% target debt and a 0.7-point debt spread reflect broad cash generation, balanced against product concentration and supply-chain exposure.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.

# Company forecast evidence review

As-of cutoff: 2026-10-17 UTC. Universe: AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOG, META, NVDA, TSLA, COHR, LITE, AAOI, NBIS, MU, AVGO, TSM.

## Purpose and scope
Research and propose new educational operating valuation cases; not investment advice, price targets, consensus estimates, or proof of attainable outcomes. Current app defaults are preserved until a separate reviewed integration. Coverage is bounded: latest available quarter, preceding quarters/annual materials, selected investor days and management interviews, and a target of 8–12 consecutive comparable guidance observations when available. Never represent this as an exhaustive record of every management statement.

## Evidence rules
- Use issuer filings, releases, official prepared remarks/transcripts, and original interview publisher first.
- Record source URL, actual publication/event date, fiscal period, currency/unit, retrieved date/status, source provenance where available.
- Label reported actual, formal management guidance, qualitative outlook, analyst estimate, and our inference separately. Revenue, bookings, backlog, contracted capacity and annualized run rate are not interchangeable.
- Keep original guidance and revisions separately; score the original observation against the exact matched metric/period. Report range placement and midpoint error, not an unqualified CEO credibility score.
- Guidance policy differences and intentional conservatism mean beat rates cannot be used as a cross-company competence ranking. Recent-quarter accuracy does not validate ten-year forecasts.
- Keep management product aspirations and long-term quantitative goals separate from near-term financial guidance. Unknown future outcomes are pending, never misses.
- No unreviewed video claims or full unlicensed commercial transcripts. Save analytical summaries, short lawful excerpts, metadata and permitted issuer filing copies. Source discovery alone is not content verification.

## Modeling rules
- Proposed cases are dated analyst judgments; no target-price calibration, including GOOG $250.
- Explain early maintained/explicit growth phase of 3 or5 years, total maturity horizon of10/15/20 years, and why duration is warranted. Show scale consequences and bear/base/bull.
- Margin is EBIT after ongoing SBC, R&D and depreciation. Adjusted EBITDA or gross margin cannot be substituted.
- Sales/capital is incremental revenue / net reinvestment, not historical sales/book capital or revenue/gross capex. Large replacement needs, lease investment, R&D, useful-life changes and working capital can invalidate a single-ratio model.
- Stable growth below WACC and ROIC; terminal reinvestment/NOPAT = stable growth/terminal ROIC. Growth without adequate reinvestment is not free.
- Review currency, shares, convertibles, warrants, minority/preferred claims, leases and non-operating assets. Unreviewed zero placeholders do not prove absence. Preserve unresolved valuation gates.

## Files
Each company: dossiers.html#source-policy, dossiers.html#source-policy, dossiers.html#source-policy, dossiers.html#source-policy, dossiers.html#source-policy. Root coverage/index/source-ledger compiled after research; shared-evidence.html#prior-assumption-comparison retains existing assumptions for change comparison.

# Independent capital-reconciliation audit

Reviewed 17 October 2026, 18:10 UTC. USD billions below unless stated. Read-only review of the three funding supplements, the standalone GOOG notes, selected company proposals and aggregate proposal index. Only this audit file was written. No share price was used or calibrated.

## Verdict

**The direct-capital supplements materially improve the accounting and all reviewed annual funding arithmetic reconciles. The material Tesla normalization and NBIS terminal-transition artifacts were corrected during this review.** The first-three-year models are analytical spending scenarios, not disclosed obligations. They do not by themselves validate revenue, utilization, margins or capital-market access.

META/TSLA's direct capital inputs are already in their selected company bases. AMZN/GOOG and AAOI/NBIS now have explicit selected overlay recommendations in their supplements, but the original company proposals remain unchanged pending integration. Do not confuse selection of an overlay with completion of a model update.

## Severity-ranked findings

### High — corrected during review: Tesla's unexplained year-4 capital normalization

- The earlier selected base fell from **29.000 to 12.927** net reinvestment, a **55.4%** reduction without a gross-capital bridge. A one-year delay in that reduction would have erased **10.214** of the earlier **11.000** operating EV.
- **Verified corrected:** `selectedFullBaseCapitalBridge` and the selected company base now specify years 4–7 gross cash capex **38/35/34/34**, D&A **20/24/27/28** and core WC **1.5 each**, producing net investment **19.5/12.5/8.5/7.5**. Years 8–10 preserve the terminal-consistent net path with explicitly derived gross components.
- Independently recomputed all ten capital/FCFF identities and the discounted operating EV of **3.063772**. The full economic deficit now peaks at **74.379824** in year 4; the unchanged 65.210 first-three-year figure remains correctly window-labeled. Final-to-terminal FCFF growth is exactly 2.5%.
- The remaining uncertainty is now explicit: keeping year-4 investment at 29.000 instead of 19.500 reduces EV by **6.037422**, producing a negative conditional operating case. These are analytical commissioning/utilization assumptions, not verified later company budgets. No share-price calibration is needed to accept a negative scenario.
- The earlier obsolete “roughly $11bn” paragraph was also replaced. The narrative now agrees with **3.064** selected operating EV.

### Medium — corrected during review: aggregate capital fields were stale

- `shared-evidence.html#scenario-index` initially retained META early S:C `[0.45, 0.45, 0.45]` and TSLA `[0.65, 0.65, 0.65]` after direct-capital inputs had replaced them.
- Selected annual inputs derive META `[0.341928, 0.361182, 0.391755]` and TSLA `[0.460529, 0.488645, 0.448206]`. **Verified corrected:** regenerated aggregate values now match the selected annual inputs.
- The regenerated AMZN/GOOG/AAOI/NBIS aggregate fields now also derive their selected overlays rather than legacy ratio paths. Preserve the explicit-method labels: these ratios describe the capital results and must not become a second reinvestment driver.

### Medium — corrected during review: NBIS terminal advance runoff distorted the transition

- The first version left central 2036 FCFF at **2.914** because of **6.249** exceptional advance runoff, versus about **9.892** under the next-year terminal formula. The runoff was charged, not omitted, but the resulting 239.5% terminal jump was not a normalized transition.
- **Verified corrected in `terminal-coherence-v2`:** advance balances reach 25% of sales by 2034, remain on that policy in 2035–36, and all normalization cash uses remain in explicit years. End-2036 advances remain **22.576**, not zero. Central 2036 FCFF is **9.651165**, followed by 2037 **9.892444**, exactly +2.5%. No extra transition years or one-time terminal cash adjustment were introduced.
- This correction materially changes the funding result: NBIS central economic/cash peaks are now **49.703 / 39.397**, replacing **37.866 / 26.337**. The revised Markdown and JSON agree. AAOI's small forward-funding convention mismatch was corrected too; every AAOI/NBIS scenario now has +2.5% final-to-terminal FCFF growth.

### Low — residual: cloud terminal convention

- AMZN's final S:C 0.98684 and GOOG's 0.64103 preserve the old current-revenue-increment convention. Applying the stated forward terminal NOPAT × growth / ROIC formula yields final-to-terminal FCFF growth of **1.8464%** and **2.0391%**, respectively, rather than exactly 2.5%.
- These are small mismatches and do **not** change the funding peaks. If implementing the same forward-funded convention used by META/TSLA and the revised optics overlays, the matching terminal S:C values are approximately **0.962773** and **0.625391**; recalculate the fade coherently rather than changing only a terminal field.
- The main cloud Markdown's GOOG year-3 D&A range was corrected from **70–100** to **70–105**, matching the embedded JSON and standalone notes. This did not change the selected 90 D&A case.

## Independently recomputed results

All values below reconcile to the annual rows and the current narratives; figures are rounded to three decimals. Economic deficits and cash deficits are deliberately different measures.

| Company / selected capital case | Economic deficit | Separate cash result | Observation boundary |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| META central | 122.498 | 77.786 before other omitted cash uses | First three rolling years only |
| TSLA central | 65.210 | 49.650 before award settlements and other uses | First three rolling years only |
| AMZN central | 275.773 | 155.018 operating cash depletion | Economic path 15 years; detailed cash years 1–7 |
| GOOG delivery-led overlay | 148.162 | 129.869 after dividends and July fine | Economic continuation 15 years; cash budget first three years |
| AAOI central | 1.113 | 0.982 before financing/award withholding | Calendar 2027–36; excludes 2026 bridge |
| NBIS central, corrected | 49.703 | 39.397 before financing/award withholding | Calendar 2027–36; excludes 2026 bridge |

AMZN's final cash result includes a **1/year provisional award-settlement allowance**, explicitly not a verified reported withholding amount. At a 40 liquidity reserve, 118.301 opening cash/debt securities and the known 21.300 OpenAI payment, new funding is **98.017**, or **113.017** with the conditional 15.000 Anthropic draw. The previous 95/110 figures were superseded during finalization.

GOOG's selected cash budget includes SBC **32/38/45** less award cash **26/30/34**, lease additions and principal/prepayments, temporary tax benefits, financing cost, dividends and the **5.200 July fine once**. The funding calculation is **14.458**, or **36.358** if all 21.900 VIE commitments are drawn before the trough. These are first-three-year cash-budget results, not a verified lifetime debt issuance requirement.

## Accounting and source controls that passed

- **Historical normalization:** AMZN's displayed arithmetic sums to **−48.18788**; its PPE depreciation **49.741** is correctly distinguished from total cash-flow D&A **75.200**. GOOG's independent identity, EBIT × 78% + PPE depreciation − cash capex + non-tax WC, equals **−4.13916**. Its exact H1 cash waterfall reconciles to **25.203** cash growth and **55.911** closing cash. Tax movements embedded in WC are removed before normalized operating taxes are substituted.
- **SBC and settlements:** META explicitly deducts a 60%-of-SBC settlement sensitivity. TSLA and optics label their cash measures as before unmodeled award settlement. AMZN now reserves 1/year and tests 0–2. GOOG distinguishes the **12.056** H1 award cash payment from **10.835** equity-statement withholding/other; TTM SBC cash uplift net of award payments is **7.655**, not 28.147. No cash SBC addback is added to economic valuation FCFF.
- **Period and units:** META/TSLA/AMZN/GOOG use rolling July 2026–June 2027 year 1. CY2026 guidance is bridged through reported H1; it is not equated to that rolling forecast. JSON amounts are millions, Markdown billions except optics' explicitly labeled mixed presentation. AAOI/NBIS 2026 revenue anchors **1.100/3.200** are full-year outlook/midpoint assumptions, not TTM actuals or exit ARR.
- **Stub spending retained:** AAOI's June cash plus confirmed October ATM equals **1.087737 before post-June uses**; its H2 scenarios produce **0.162737–0.612737** year-end cash before other uses. NBIS remaining 2026 capex is **11.8697–16.8697**, under the explicitly qualified cash-equivalent guide convention. Its central year-end cash calculation equals **3.3222**. The >9 annual gross advance target is not incorrectly reduced by the H1 **4.395 net** liability/cash movement.
- **Capex/prepayments/leases:** AAOI's 335.132m PPE, 289.744m advances and 8.581m land are separate reported lines; their sum is a physical-capital subtotal, not total investing cash flow. The 0.259m intangible purchase and 0.003m proceeds explain the small difference to investing cash use. Existing construction and prepayments are not repurchased on commissioning. AMZN capital-creditor growth and finance-lease additions are separately identified; noncash leased additions included in economic investment receive matching cash-financing addbacks, with principal then deducted once. Operating rent is retained in EBIT without a second blanket operating-lease debt deduction.
- **Customer advances:** all NBIS yearly advance balances, movements, recognition and FCFF equations reconcile. The no-new-advances case separately services the assumed opening 8.8 balance. Backlog/TCV and expected advances are not treated as cash on hand; no duplicate Meta backstop revenue is assumed for capacity already sold to third parties.
- **No duplicate financing deduction:** none of the tested valuation formulas adds cumulative FCFF deficits as current debt. Future funding is a separate liquidity calculation. June balances already include pre-June fundraising; the closed AAOI ATM and NBIS subsequent financings enter the separate roll-forward once. Undrawn facilities, restricted cash and private-investment marks are not credited as unrestricted cash.

## Residual implementation gates, already disclosed rather than hidden arithmetic errors

AMZN's approximately **9.315** recognized financing obligations are identified as a missing opening claim to review; that review is not completed merely by the supplement. META's lease-principal-in-guidance convention still needs an additions/principal bridge; the present proxy assumes approximate balance. NBIS site deposits/prepaid rent and rent/power commencement require actual timing rather than treating its 12.054 undiscounted lease commitments as debt or using a 12-year average as an annual forecast. GOOG cash budgets do not yet cover later refinancing/strategic uses. These gaps can change equity/cash feasibility but do not justify subtracting the same future investment twice.

**Recommended disposition:** the revised Tesla and optics capital/terminal arithmetic passes; aggregate fields and identified narrative inconsistencies are corrected. The selected overlays are suitable for a clearly conditional research handoff. The only remaining numerical convention cleanup identified is the small AMZN/GOOG terminal mismatch, which does not affect the cash-funding conclusions. Asset-cohort, claim and cash-timing gates should stay visible, not be resolved by changing forecast growth to fit a desired result.

# Independent research-coherence audit

Research cutoff: 17 October 2026. Closing audit snapshot: approximately 17:54 UTC on that date. This is a read-only review of the company files and application; only this audit document was written by the reviewer. Corrections below were made by the research coordinator and then rechecked. Separate direct-capital reconciliation work begun after this review is not certified by this audit.

## Verdict

The package is suitable for review as **conditional operating research**, subject to the retained company-specific gates. It is **not cleared for automatic replacement of application defaults or release of definitive common-equity/per-share values**. The most important issues found were a materially mislabeled Micron reinvestment input in the compiled summary, abrupt Meta/Tesla terminal-capital transitions, and corrupted source-audit metadata. Those have been corrected and independently rechecked.

No material new reported-financial-number error, improper price calibration, currency conversion error, or quantified future outcome presented as an accomplished fact was identified in the completed checks. This is not a fresh external verification of every source statement. Source contents already acquired in the package, company narratives and structured data were used; no current market price was obtained or used.

All **14 company narratives and their structured facts, sources, guidance records, management assessments and proposed scenarios** were reviewed. The final COHR, LITE, AAOI and NBIS narratives and their added obligation/asset registers were included in the closing review at approximately 17:53 UTC; no additional material narrative/JSON contradiction was found. Their new source-ID references resolve.

## Findings, ranked by implementation consequence

### 1. High: funding and investment paths are not yet implementable base plans

**Status: retained, acknowledged implementation gate; not a newly discovered arithmetic error. Blocks funded equity/per-share implementation, not publication as a clearly conditional operating scenario.**

Exact references: `evidence-AMZN.html#judgment.scenarios.base.annual_path`; the corresponding `annualForecast` arrays for AAOI, NBIS and COHR; and `evidence-GOOG.html#judgment.scenarios.base.annual_path`. For list-based schemas, select `scenario == "base"`.

The original ratio-based base schedules reviewed here imply the following peak cumulative **undiscounted operating FCFF deficits**. These are **diagnostic outputs of those provisional ratios**, not independently established financing needs or validated capex forecasts. They are calculated before applying starting liquidity, distributions, financing, or a valuation-date stub:

| Company | Peak cumulative deficit, USD bn |
|---|---:|
| AMZN | 356.702 |
| NBIS | 76.755 |
| GOOG | 87.210 |
| AAOI | 6.472 |
| COHR | 3.829 |

These magnitudes make funding feasibility economically consequential, especially for AAOI and NBIS. AAOI's first modeled year alone has USD2.750bn net reinvestment and negative USD2.626bn FCFF; NBIS has USD21.333bn and negative USD20.973bn respectively. AMZN's first-year net reinvestment is USD214.804bn, versus USD220bn current calendar-year **gross cash capex** outlook; these are different periods and definitions, so they cannot be equated without a D&A, working-capital and lease bridge.

The proposal files appropriately withhold implementation and identify these limitations. Preserve those gates when producing a normalized summary or downstream model. The coordinator has begun subsequent direct-capital reconciliation for AMZN/GOOG, AAOI/NBIS and META/TSLA; revised paths must supersede these diagnostic figures when available and receive their own arithmetic/cash-bridge check. Funding deficits are already cash outflows in the DCF: **do not subtract their total a second time as an additional debt claim**. Future funding, claims, customer advances and existing cash must be reconciled without duplicate cash benefits or duplicate financing deductions.

### 2. High: Micron's post-normalization ratio was mislabeled as early capital efficiency

**Status: corrected and rechecked. Formerly blocking mechanical import of the compiled case.**

Exact references: `shared-evidence.html#scenario-index.companies[ticker=MU].earlySalesCapital`; authoritative `evidence-MU.html#judgment.scenarios.base.postNormalizationSalesCapital` and `.annualForecast[0:5]`.

The compiled value was 0.8, but 0.8 belongs to the period after the first five explicit years. Years 1–5 instead use direct gross capex, cash grants, D&A and operating working capital. The first year has USD126.529bn incremental revenue and USD57.800bn net reinvestment, an effective ratio of approximately 2.189. Applying 0.8 in that year would charge USD158.161bn reinvestment, approximately USD100.36bn more than the actual proposal.

The canonical field is now null, accompanied by an explicit direct-capital method and a link to the full schedule. The coordinator also added revenue anchors, actual-versus-forecast status and first modeled periods to all canonical rows. In particular, AAOI's USD1.1bn and NBIS's USD3.2bn anchors are explicitly FY2026 forecasts, with FY2027 as the first full forward year; their high growth rates must not be applied to the older TTM anchors.

### 3. Medium: Meta/Tesla had unexplained terminal reinvestment discontinuities

**Status: corrected and rechecked. Formerly an adoption-blocking economic-path inconsistency; no remaining blocker from this issue.**

Exact references: `evidence-META.html#judgment.scenarios[*].annualForecast`, the corresponding TSLA arrays, `impliedTerminalSalesToCapital`, and the new `terminalTransitionPolicy`.

Previously, TSLA base remained at 2.0x incremental sales/capital through year 10 while the stated terminal economics implied 1.6x under the simple marginal-return convention. Moving to forward-year NOPAT × growth / terminal ROIC raised annual reinvestment from USD2.569bn to USD3.374bn, with FCFF falling 3.1% despite unchanged margin and 2.5% revenue growth. TSLA bull had a 122% reinvestment step; META bull a 47% step. The bears received a sudden capital-efficiency improvement.

The revised final-year capital paths now use a separately stated, forward-NOPAT-consistent incremental-sales ratio. Recalculation verifies final explicit FCFF grows into terminal FCFF at exactly the stated 2.0% or 2.5% rate for all six scenarios. Updated narrative EV figures agree with revised selected cases. The simple ROIC/after-tax-margin identity and the timing-adjusted incremental-sales convention should remain distinctly labeled.

### 4. Medium: source hashes and retrieval timestamps had been changed by text polishing

**Status: corrected and independently rechecked against cached bytes. Formerly blocking a claim of machine-reproducible source integrity.**

Exact references: `evidence-META.html#sources[0:16].sha256`, `evidence-TSLA.html#sources[0:13].sha256`, and affected `retrievedAt` fields.

Whitespace had been inserted inside SHA-256 strings and ISO timestamps. The coordinator restored them from untouched retrieval records or recomputed the original cached-file hash. All **16 META and 13 TSLA** hashes now match the referenced local file bytes, and the repaired retrieval timestamps parse as ISO timestamps. This was an audit-metadata error, not evidence that the underlying financial figures were changed.

### 5. Medium-low: Micron canonical fiscal anchor had an incorrect date

**Status: corrected and rechecked.**

Exact reference: `shared-evidence.html#scenario-index.companies[ticker=MU].anchorPeriod`, against `evidence-MU.html#facts.latestAnnual.periodEnd` and the FY2026 annual filing.

The summary briefly labeled the fiscal year end August 27, 2026. The reported 53-week FY2026 ends **September 3, 2026**. The canonical row now uses September 3 and describes FY2027 as following that reported base. The cached annual filing's calendar rule is the Thursday closest to August 31; under that rule September 2, 2027 is the inferred FY2027 year end, rather than an asserted reported result.

### 6. Low: Meta duration sensitivity needs a consistent definition after the capital repair

**Status: corrected and rechecked. Not a material numerical valuation error.**

Exact reference: `evidence-META.html#judgment.durationSensitivity[0]` versus its selected 3-year/10-year base scenario.

At the first post-repair check, the sensitivity still showed the old USD865.332bn operating EV while the revised selected base showed USD864.029bn. The coordinator has now explicitly labeled this grid as constant-sales/capital diagnostics in `durationSensitivityDefinition` and the narrative, identifying the omitted final capital transition and explaining why the 3/10 diagnostic differs from the selected base. The two results are no longer represented as identical economic settings.

## Checks with no new substantive finding

- **AAPL and MSFT:** June annual/TTM anchors match their forecast revenue bases. AAPL's rolling year is distinguished from its September fiscal year. Reported versus normalized tariff effects, MSFT depreciation versus broader cash-flow addbacks, cash capex versus lease additions, stale/current leases, and outstanding versus weighted-average shares are distinguished. WACC builds recompute at their stated assumed tax/weights.
- **AMZN and GOOG:** Percentage-form scenario fields are correctly converted to decimals in the canonical summary. Revenue categories are not added across overlapping segment/product definitions. Investment assets, customer funding, acquisitions, preferred conversion and capped-call matters remain gated. No GOOG price-target calibration is apparent. Some historical actual evidence uses later comparative filings; the package should not be represented as an exhaustive point-in-time first-release backtest.
- **META and TSLA:** Revenue/margin/TTM narratives and corrected financial anchors remain consistent with their structured facts. Identified legal claims, debt and dilution issues are retained. Conditional autonomy/product ambitions are not mechanically scored as quarterly revenue guidance.
- **NVDA and AVGO:** Rolling forecast periods are distinguished from fiscal management targets. AI/customer-capex visibility is not presented as incremental recognized revenue or an additional balance-sheet asset. GAAP/non-GAAP metrics and approximate point forecasts versus ranges are distinguished. Unreconciled investment/guarantee/lease claims and capital schedules prevent final implementation.
- **COHR, LITE, AAOI and NBIS:** Current financing and conversion effects, contingent warrants, forecast calendar anchors, ARR/revenue differences and customer-prepayment limitations are explicitly identified in both narratives and structured files. Net-reinvestment proxies are not mislabeled gross capex. No immediate tax benefit is booked for modeled operating losses. Final obligation/asset registers preserve conditions, treatments and gaps rather than silently clearing the claims.
- **MU and TSM:** Direct versus inferred capex is explicitly separated. MU gross capex minus grants/asset proceeds reconciles with the separately reported net-capex definition. TSM TIFRS/IASB IFRS, TWD/USD, flow/spot FX and ordinary-share/ADS distinctions are preserved. The stated USD-to-TWD WACC inflation translation recomputes; it is labeled an assumption rather than an observed local risk-free rate.
- Scenario annual arithmetic was recomputed for revenue, NOPAT and FCFF; no material discrepancy was found. Minor differences caused by rounded published margin fields are immaterial. Guidance range-placement checks and the principal summary beat/miss counts recomputed without a substantive discrepancy. Local source-ID references resolve in the current company ledgers.

## Limits and release rule

This audit does not certify all third-party transcripts, reconstruct every historical revision, establish private-asset fair values, quantify guarantee losses, or clear actual financing, tax, lease, minority-interest and compensation schedules. Explicitly missing values remain missing. No reviewed case becomes a verified equity value merely because its arithmetic and references are internally consistent. Preserve the company-specific implementation and per-share gates.

normalization_basis.reasoning: Existing assets plus recent buildout moving in service drive depreciation catch-up. Do not depreciate all new construction from day1 or keep D&A flat as capex surges. normalization_basis.management_cycle_statement: Management described data-center spending about2years before monetization, servers purchased months before use, server breakeven under3years and longer-lived facilities. normalization_basis.non_PPE_reinvestment_basis: Historical combined non-PPE amortization plus tax-adjusted operating-asset/liability cash movements was a 3.9bn source; forecast0–15bn year1 uses to allow Cloud receivables, inventory/content and lease-payment timing, excluding capital creditors and financing investments.

GOOG.purpose: Standalone funding reconciliation; do not replace existing company assumptions automatically. No price calibration.
bottom_line: The existing 87,209.56 cumulative economic FCFF deficit peaks after year 2; it is not an annual cash-financing requirement.

The latest CY2026 gross cash capex guide is 195,000–205,000. The rolling year ending June2027 includes the higher 2027 spend profile, so 196,181 of net reinvestment is plausible; neither an error nor proof of financing distress can be inferred from comparison with the calendar guide.
Reported TTM cash FCF 53,273 becomes a normalized, SBC-expensed, PPE-only FCFF proxy of -4,139.16 at a 22% operating tax rate. Working-capital tax movements are explicitly removed in the bridge.

Rapid D&A catch-up can eventually reduce net reinvestment, but the latest guide, 122,814 of assets not yet in service and 707,000 of multiyear purchase commitments do not support assuming immediate investment normalization.
Cash and current debt securities total 155,411 before liquidity buffers and constraints, versus headline cash/current marketables of 242,474. Current equity investments must not be treated as cash.

bridge_method.CFO_identity: NI + PP&E depreciation + SBC + deferred tax adjustment - securities gains + other noncash + non-tax WC cash effect + income-tax WC cash effect
bridge_method.normalized_PPE_proxy: CFO - cash capex - SBC - (OI&E - securities gains reversed in CFO) + tax provision - deferred tax adjustment - tax WC cash effect - EBIT*normalized_tax - other noncash
bridge_method.equivalent_identity: EBIT*(1-normalized_tax) + PP&E depreciation - cash capex + non-tax WC cash effect
bridge_method.tax_rate: 22% is the existing proposal sensitivity, not an observed effective cash tax rate. Use 20–24% normalization sensitivity.

tax_disclosure_check.caution: H1 and TTM cash-flow-implied amounts are algebraic all-items approximations, not separately disclosed cash taxes. They include taxes on nonoperating results, settlements, temporary differences and rounding/classification effects.

bridge_method.limits: PPE-only proxy strips the entire other noncash line for exact reproducibility. Restore independently verified operating amortization and appropriate operating noncash charges; do not treat this stripped residual as precise final FCFF. H1 intangible amortization 545 yields -25,109.52 before financing-lease asset adjustments. FY2025 full intangible amortization was not separately identified in this review, so no unsupported TTM estimate is added.
bridge_method.interest: H1 interest expense 1,811 and interest income 2,811 are in OI&E, which this bridge removes together with other nonoperating amounts. Adding after-tax interest again would double count. The 628 of H1 capitalized interest requires a consistent capex/financing convention; do not assume accrued interest equals cash interest paid.
bridge_method.sbc: Retain SBC in EBIT/NOPAT and do not add it back to economic FCFF. Add the actual noncash SBC cash-flow adjustment only in the separate cash-funding bridge. Forecast employee equity dilution or its replacement cost consistently; do not charge the same SBC cost again through both an expense-retained valuation and a full replacement-cost/share-dilution penalty.
bridge_method.WC: H1 non-tax WC cash consumption is 21,406, including inventory 7,739 and receivables 6,904; tax WC is a separate +8,304. Never combine a normal WC forecast with a second customer-prepayment benefit already inside that forecast.

gross_vs_net_and_supplier_credit.treatment: Do not add the entire 29,113 unpaid PPE balance to cash capex. If reconstructing accrual investment, reconcile the change in capital payables and acquisition/FX/disposal effects, and record matching supplier-credit financing. When using cash capex directly, its eventual settlement is a timing consideration, not another current investment deduction.
gross_vs_net_and_supplier_credit.policy: Depreciation starts when assets enter service. Servers/network equipment generally depreciate over six years; buildings over seven to forty years. Model asset cohorts and in-service dates; a six-year life does not justify instantaneous depreciation of all current cash capex.

guidance_to_rolling_forecast.rolling_2027_formula: H2 2026 cash capex + H1 2027 cash capex. There is no quantified CY2027 issuer guide in the reviewed sources.
guidance_to_rolling_forecast.classification: Analytical scenario ranges anchored to guide, investment backlog, depreciation policy and observed WC. They are not management forecasts or confidence intervals; extreme component bounds need not occur together.
guidance_to_rolling_forecast.range_rationale: June2027 gross capex range assumes roughly 111–141bn H1 2027 at the matching guide endpoints. June2028 permits continuing 2027 ramp and June2029 allows stabilization or another expansion. D&A rises as the 122.8bn construction/installation pipeline and new cohorts enter service. Inventory/receivables keep WC a possible cash use; customer backlog itself supplies no cash.
normalization_conditions: Use 2027/2028 physical deliveries and cohort depreciation to decide whether 2029 capex stabilizes; do not automatically fade cash capex when revenue growth fades.
Test supplier-credit unwind, TPU inventory-to-revenue conversion, leased capacity cost and acquired-intangible amortization separately.

D&A ranges are intended as total operating D&A, including verified intangible amortization and finance-lease asset depreciation. Reconcile the finance-lease amortization disclosure to modeled PP&E depreciation before any separate addback; include it once.

After June2029, transition asset cohorts and reinvestment over several years. Do not jump from explicit capital spending to a terminal sales/capital ratio; satisfy terminal net reinvestment = growth/ROIC*NOPAT.

22% tax and original revenue/NOPAT are sensitivities. Higher depreciation, temporary third-party capacity and TPU hardware mix must also be tested through margins; preserving margins while changing D&A is not an integrated forecast.

earlier_stabilization.classification: analytical conditional sensitivity, not an endorsed integrated base forecast
earlier_stabilization.interpretation: Maximum cumulative deficit observed through June2029. This is a lower bound on any full-forecast peak, not a lifetime funding maximum. FCFF turns positive within this window; later outcomes remain unmodeled here.

delivery_led_illustration.classification: analytical conditional sensitivity, not an endorsed integrated base forecast
delivery_led_illustration.interpretation: Maximum cumulative deficit observed through June2029. This is a lower bound on any full-forecast peak, not a lifetime funding maximum. FCFF remains negative in the final observed year, so the deficit is still increasing at the boundary.

continued_acceleration_stress.classification: analytical conditional sensitivity, not an endorsed integrated base forecast
continued_acceleration_stress.interpretation: Maximum cumulative deficit observed through June2029. This is a lower bound on any full-forecast peak, not a lifetime funding maximum. FCFF remains negative in the final observed year, so the deficit is still increasing at the boundary.

original_model_diagnostic.interpretation: Original first-year net reinvestment lies inside the explicit range. There is no source-supported reason to force it downward purely to eliminate a deficit. The mechanically linked sales/capital path omits D&A, supplier financing, leases and cash taxes needed to explain cash funding.

forward_cash_funding_identity: Start with economic FCFF with SBC expensed and operating taxes normalized.
Add back the noncash SBC cash-flow adjustment only to measure cash available; separately recognize the employee equity claim consistently in valuation.
Add actual temporary operating tax savings (or subtract reversals), and bridge cash nonoperating receipts and cash interest; do not use unrealized securities/derivative gains as funding.

If economic reinvestment included financed lease assets or accrued capital-payable increases, add matching financing sources, then deduct actual principal/prepayments or supplier settlements only once. If using cash capex, do not add supplier financing again.
Deduct strategic equity/customer financing, acquisitions, dividends, employee award withholding, debt maturities and any other cash commitments excluded from operating FCFF.
Then apply existing liquid assets above an explicit buffer and new net debt/equity financing. This required-financing balance is distinct from cumulative economic FCFF.

liquidity_and_obligations.liquidity_caution: Do not treat equity values or unrealized gains as cash. Debt securities include longer maturities and market risk. A parent-level availability/operating-buffer adjustment is still needed; the annual filing identified 5.6bn of consolidated VIE assets restricted to those VIE obligations at December2025, with no updated June amount established in this review.
liquidity_and_obligations.financing_caution: Credit and CP capacity are contingent financing tools, not cash assets and not necessarily additive independent borrowing capacity. June balance sheet already includes H1 proceeds; do not add them again. Bridge August debt proceeds and uses together if updating anchor.
liquidity_and_obligations.treatment: Schedule commitments in the appropriate capex, inventory/COGS, rent, financing or contingent-loss line. Do not subtract notional commitments as extra debt on top of forecast spending. The 20bn contingent funding is inside 21.9bn VIE commitments, not additive. Existing lease VIE exposures are already in lease totals. Treat guarantees through default/mitigation scenarios and avoid double counting recorded derivative liabilities. Preferred conversion/capped-call terms require the existing claim model; never subtract full liquidation preference and also apply full conversion dilution.
liquidity_and_obligations.energy_guarantee_update_gap: The June filing describes terms through September2026. Do not assume all 7.6bn remains live or has expired at October17 without a later update.
liquidity_and_obligations.lease_caution: H1 repayments of debt in the cash-flow statement already include finance-lease cash amounts under the filing convention. Do not deduct lease cash again in the exact funding bridge. Finance-lease assets are in PP&E: reconcile the 485 amortization disclosure to the modeled depreciation definition rather than automatically adding it again. If EBIT includes operating rent, do not also subtract the operating lease liability unless rent/EBIT and invested capital are recast consistently.
liquidity_and_obligations.known_July2026_fine_treatment: Note10 reports the previously accrued Android fine and interest paid in July2026. Schedule 5,200 as a post-June cash use. Because previously accrued, do not also book a new recurring EBIT expense or deduct the same accrued liability twice in the valuation/funding bridge.

rules: RPO includes unbilled future invoices and is not a funding balance.
Deferred revenue is received or due before performance, and can be refundable; the balance is not necessarily all cash already collected.
Use only actual deferred-revenue cash movement once, via WC; do not also net backlog/customer advances against gross capex.
Customer financing investments and credit backstops consume or risk funding; they are not independent evidence that recognized revenue is cash-funded.
