sharedResearch.optics-funding-reconciliation-narrative:
# AAOI and NBIS: capital, cash funding and normalization

As of 17 October 2026. All financial figures are USD millions unless explicitly labeled billions. This supplements the dossiers without replacing their proposals. Forward schedules are analytical sensitivities; actual observations and management guidance are identified separately. No assumption has been calibrated to a stock price.

## Decision-useful conclusions

1. AAOI's mechanical $6.47bn 2027+ cumulative FCFF shortfall is not a defensible stand-alone estimate of financing required. It charges the first $1.65bn revenue increase $2.75bn of *net* reinvestment, even though substantial factories/equipment were funded in 2026. Explicit factory cash spending, commissioning and working capital yield materially smaller, still nontrivial shortfalls.
2. NBIS's $76.75bn mechanical shortfall is also not a financing forecast, but its capital burden is real. Its $20–25bn 2026 capex guide and later owned deployments cannot disappear when replacing the sales-to-capital ratio. Customer advances improve liquidity, while eventual advance recognition/refunds, depreciation and equipment replacement must remain in the model.
3. Publish conditional operating values and financing/dilution sensitivities rather than suppressing all operating results. A single equity per-share figure still needs a dated cash/debt/share bridge. Do not deduct projected operating shortfalls as additional present debt; the negative FCFF is already inside the operating DCF.

### What the alternatives actually establish

| Company / path | Peak economic FCFF shortfall, 2027 onward ($bn) | Illustrative cash shortfall before financing / award withholding ($bn) |
|---|---:|---:|
| AAOI capital-efficient | 0.43 | 0.40 |
| AAOI central explicit | 1.11 | 0.98 |
| AAOI capital stress | 3.03 | 2.56 |
| NBIS paced / partner-funded | 24.48 | 14.34 |
| NBIS owned-build central | 49.70 | 39.40 |
| NBIS owned-build stress | 98.48 | 88.17 |

These are model outputs, not statements that these amounts will be borrowed or raised. They exclude the 2026 bridge, opening cash, new financing, interest, principal maturities, liquidity reserves and award withholding. The cash illustration adds back noncash SBC at an assumed 1% of revenue for AAOI / 3% for NBIS; that improves cash liquidity while remaining a real shareholder cost through dilution. It is not free cash. All individual years and the no-new-advance stress are in dossiers.html#source-policy.

## 1. AAOI

### Reported starting point and accounting repair

H1 2026 cash use comprised $335.132m PPE, $289.744m equipment/capital advances and $8.581m land, totaling $633.457m; CFO was -$73.781m. June capital advances were $324.045m; PPE already contained $168.805m construction in progress. Moving either balance into operational machinery creates depreciation, not another purchase. June unrestricted cash was $499.737m and unused bank capacity $106.5m. June receivables/inventory/payables were $314.009m/$278.791m/$286.088m. Supplier terms and customer concentration are material funding variables. [AAOI June 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1158114/000143774926026278/aaoi20260630_10q.htm)

June cash already reflects H1 financing; do not add it again. October's completed ATM produced approximately $588m net and 5.694845m additional shares. This is confirmed funding, with dilution, rather than merely an available program. Its proceeds must be rolled forward with Q3/Q4 cash use; they do not make June cash an October balance. [October ATM completion](https://appliedoptoelectronics.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/applied-optoelectronics-announces-completion-previously)

AAOI's machinery accounting lives range from 2–20 years. New productive assets require a commissioning schedule; carrying forward H1's low D&A forever overstates margin. The explicit $100–200m 2027 D&A envelope below is analytical, reflecting a much larger asset base, not a disclosed depreciation forecast. [AAOI FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1158114/000143774926005875/aaoi20251231_10k.htm)

### Capacity to revenue, rather than nameplate to sales

The issuer targets 800G / 1.6T monthly capacity of 420k / 230k at Q4 2026, 550k / 230k at Q2 2027 and 550k / 380k at Q4 2027. Linear interpolation implies about 9.42m high-speed nameplate units in 2027. This excludes AOC, lower-speed modules and ELSFP, whose economics differ. Annual guidance around $1.1bn and Q3 midpoint $272.5m imply Q4 revenue $484.434m. Consequently, $2.75bn 2027 means average quarterly sales only 41.9% above that demanding implied Q4, despite 150% annual growth. [Issuer presentation, guidance and capacity roadmap](https://investors.ao-inc.com/static-files/93d502fe-1481-4462-9017-8ea05c43e7ce)

**Our unit test, not a price forecast:** allow $300–450m for other products. The remaining $2.30–2.45bn needs the following recognized blended ASP on high-speed modules:

| Accepted/sold units as fraction of interpolated nameplate | Required blended ASP |
|---|---:|
| 60% | $407–433 |
| 75% | $326–347 |
| 90% | $271–289 |

The accepted fraction combines production utilization, yield, qualification, customer acceptance and sell-through. These are not interchangeable. Product mix and actual ASP must satisfy the hurdle; manufacturing floor area or a design win alone does not. As a further analytical scale check, $5.94bn 2029 sales, $350m other revenue, $300 blended high-speed ASP and 80% accepted yield/utilization would need approximately 1.94m monthly nameplate units, more than twice the Q4 2027 combined 930k target. The 2028–29 capex envelope therefore finances another expansion; it cannot merely run the 2027 factory unchanged. Disclosed nameplate targets make a ramp plausible, while the required output/price combination remains unproven.

### Explicit investment envelopes

These are source-anchored analytical budgets. The issuer disclosed continued expansion through 2027, but this review did not find an approved 2027 dollar budget.

| Year | Gross capital cash range | D&A range | Other operating WC increase range |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2026 H2 | 450–800 | included in full-year analytic 50–80 | reflected in H2 CFO envelope |
| 2027 | 550–1,000 | 100–200 | 200–400 |
| 2028 | 450–900 | 175–275 | 180–350 |
| 2029 | 500–1,000 | 225–375 | 170–350 |

The central path is:

| Year | Revenue | Gross capital cash | D&A | Δ operating WC | NOPAT | Economic FCFF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,027.0 | 2,750.0 | 750.0 | 150.0 | 247.5 | 123.8 | -723.8 |
| 2,028.0 | 4,400.0 | 700.0 | 225.0 | 247.5 | 396.0 | -326.5 |
| 2,029.0 | 5,940.0 | 800.0 | 300.0 | 231.0 | 668.2 | -62.8 |
| 2,030.0 | 7,743.2 | 760.5 | 309.7 | 270.5 | 871.1 | 149.8 |

Central 2027 net investment is $847.5m, not the mechanical $2.75bn: $750m cash capital spending minus $150m D&A plus $247.5m working capital. The 2027–29 peak is $1.113bn, versus $6.47bn under the persistent ratio. The low branch assumes high utilization and strong capital turns; the high branch raises capital/WC and lowers D&A. These envelopes can be wrong in either direction and should be replaced with actual purchase/commissioning schedules as disclosed.

After 2029, gross capex is replacement spending plus growth-asset spending, not a permanently repeated emergency ramp ratio. D&A reaches 5% of sales. Total net-investment intensity fades to 1.048295 per dollar of current-year incremental revenue by 2036, including the (1 + growth) forward-funding factor, preserving the existing terminal 11% ROIC, 15% operating margin and 25% tax. Final 2036 net reinvestment is exactly NOPAT2036 × 2.5% / 11%, so 2037 FCFF grows exactly 2.5%. This makes normalization explicit rather than giving the terminal period a hidden investment holiday. It does not validate the inherited $16.85bn 2036 revenue scale.

### Funding bridge and leases

June cash plus confirmed ATM net proceeds equals $1,087.737m **before** post-June spending. With analytical H2 capital cash of $450–800m and CFO of -$125m to -$25m, December cash is roughly $163–613m before unidentified financing/uses. A $100–150m reserve leaves roughly $13–513m headroom. That would cover part, not necessarily all, of the central 2027+ cash shortfall. June unused bank capacity is conditional capacity, not assured future cash.

Known site purchases, deposits and fit-outs are included within these cash envelopes; do not add them again. The September property purchase was about $26.8m. Houston leases create rent and deposits; keep rental costs in EBIT under the operating-lease convention. If instead capitalizing leases, adjust EBIT, cash flows and claims together. [Property purchase](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1158114/000168316826007057/aaoi_8k.htm) · [Houston lease filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1158114/000168316826006862/aaoi_8k.htm) · [Ningbo lease filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1158114/000168316826007160/aaoi_8k.htm)

Bank acceptances require a consistent convention: if they are debt, do not also net them into operating payables. The $4bn customer-warrant vesting threshold is neither funded backlog nor a customer cash advance. Convertible debt and customer/employee dilution remain separate claims; existing proceeds cannot be added twice.

## 2. NBIS

### Reported build and forward customer funding

H1 cash capital spending was $8.1303bn; CFO $4.5041bn included $4.395bn net deferred-revenue inflow. June cash was $8.0421bn unrestricted, with $1.056bn restricted. PPE included $7.8364bn not yet in use. Deferred revenue was $5.9752bn; it includes refundable amounts. H1 acquired equipment/intangibles not yet paid were $973.3m. Commissioning pre-funded assets, adding unpaid purchases to cash capex, or adding lease right-of-use assets as cash spend would each overstate near-term investment. [NBIS June interim financial statements](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1513845/000110465926094844/nbis-20260812xex99d2.htm)

Management's 2026 capex guide increased to $20–25bn, including buildout benefiting 2027. Dossier call-text review verified that range; this reconciliation independently read the primary statements and letters, but did not listen to the webcast. The remaining-H2 bridge treats that range as cash-equivalent spending; reconcile any accrued-addition/vendor-payment differences before using it as a cash forecast. [May earnings-call record](https://www.roic.ai/quote/NBIS/transcripts/2026-year/1-quarter) · [August earnings-call record](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/nbis/transcripts/655490-q2-2026/)

The August letter expects >$9bn annual customer advances, describes 70% of Q2 deals carrying prepayments covering 50–60% of associated capex, and cites an estimated 22-month payback. That payback is based on recognized revenue and forecast costs, excluding advances; it is not consolidated realized ROIC. Deal-count percentages cannot be multiplied into a company-wide capex-funded percentage without deal-size weights. [August shareholder letter](https://assets.nebius.com/assets/a6ecfd85-a6cb-4967-8ef7-9a25bd261f9c/SHLQ226.pdf?cache-buster=2026-08-12T11%3A54%3A46.695Z)

### Capacity and revenue recognition

Connected power is distinct from contracted power and active revenue-generating hardware. The 2026 connected target is 800–1,000MW. At $12m/$16m/$20m/$25m annual revenue per billable MW, $9.6bn 2027 revenue requires average billable capacity of 800/600/480/384MW. These are algebraic hurdles, not utilization estimates. At $16m/MW, the inherited $17.28bn and $25.056bn sales require 1,080MW and 1,566MW average billable capacity. [Capacity definitions and 2026 connected target](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1513845/000110465926059872/tm2614392d1_ex99-2.htm)

The August letter's >1GW/year deployment ambition and new $20–25m/MW contracts are relevant evidence, but do not imply that all contracted power is active all year or that premium pricing applies to the whole installed base. December ARR is monthly revenue times 12; it must not be counted as full-year revenue. An asset-light partnership can reduce Nebius cash capex, but partner ownership, profit sharing and gross-versus-net revenue recognition must change consistently. [Deployment and partnership discussion](https://assets.nebius.com/assets/a6ecfd85-a6cb-4967-8ef7-9a25bd261f9c/SHLQ226.pdf?cache-buster=2026-08-12T11%3A54%3A46.695Z)

Meta's dedicated orders are $12bn over five years, with deployments starting early 2027; a separate order backstops eligible unsold capacity up to $15bn. Third-party sales and Meta backstop sales cannot be assigned to the same capacity. Neither headline amount is an additional asset on top of RPO. Late-delivery discounts, service obligations and termination rights remain relevant. [Meta agreement 6-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1513845/000110465926027886/tm268879d1_6k.htm)

### Why the 2026 bridge cannot be skipped

June cash already includes H1 convert/ATM/NVIDIA receipts and H1 customer advances. Subsequent additions are the August $5.75bn gross new-note issue, with fees, and the July $775m secured facility only to the extent funded/available. The $800m old-note exchange brought shares and debt extinguishment, not another $800m cash receipt. [Closed August financing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1513845/000110465926100347/tm2623863d1_ex99-1.htm) · [July secured financing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1513845/000110465926084452/tm2620683d1_ex99-1.htm)

On a cash-equivalent guide interpretation, remaining H2 capital spending is $11.87–16.87bn. An analytical central bridge uses $22.5bn full-year spending, $5.65bn August net cash, a full $775m July draw, $400m other H2 operating cash and $2.8248bn net advance increase. It produces approximately $3.322bn December cash and $8.8bn deferred revenue; a $2bn cash reserve leaves $1.322bn. The net-note cash assumption allows $50–125m fees/other deductions from gross proceeds; it is not a disclosed net-proceeds figure. These are not reported October or December balances. The wider stated inputs produce an envelope from a $1.0bn shortfall to $7.45bn cash before reserve/unknown uses, showing that timing can matter as much as total contract value.

Do not compute remaining annual advances as $9bn minus $4.395bn. The latter is a **net** cash-flow increase; $154.3m of opening deferred revenue was recognized in H1, and within-period receipt/recognition is not fully isolated. A gross receipt target and a net liability movement are different quantities.

### Annual investment alternatives and depreciation test

| Path | 2027 / 2028 / 2029 gross cash capex ($bn) | D&A ($bn) | Assumed new advances / capex |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Paced / partner | 14 / 14 / 14 | 3.5 / 5.0 / 6.5 | 40% |
| Owned-build central | 20 / 20 / 20 | 4.0 / 6.5 / 8.5 | 35% |
| Owned-build stress | 28 / 26 / 24 | 5.5 / 8.5 / 11.5 | 20% |

All future budgets, D&A and advance proportions in this table are analytical. The $14bn path requires greater use of already funded assets, construction pacing, higher revenue yield or genuinely partner-funded capacity. It is not compatible with assuming Nebius funds every new >1GW deployment while retaining all gross customer revenue. The $20bn path is a plausible scale test around the current build intensity; it is not a disclosed annual budget. The original $90.3bn 2036 sales path requires about 5.64GW of average billable capacity at $16m/MW (7.53GW at $12m/MW), so some large cumulative investment need persists even after repairing the early ratio. Contracted power is not billable output.

Central early-year details:

| Year | Revenue | Gross capex cash | D&A | Other ΔWC | Net advances | Economic FCFF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,027.0 | 9,600.0 | 20,000.0 | 4,000.0 | 300.0 | 5,200.0 | -10,740.0 |
| 2,028.0 | 17,280.0 | 20,000.0 | 6,500.0 | 400.0 | 3,800.0 | -8,544.8 |
| 2,029.0 | 25,056.0 | 20,000.0 | 8,500.0 | 400.0 | 2,000.0 | -6,517.4 |
| 2,030.0 | 34,809.9 | 19,904.3 | 10,443.0 | 292.6 | 3,946.8 | -1,107.8 |

The central margins require adjusted EBITDA of approximately 49.7%, 52.6% and 54.9% at assumed 3% SBC. That is a clear profitability hurdle. The stress case lowers early EBIT margins to approximately -10.3%, -2.2% and 1.1%, consistent with a 50% adjusted EBITDA ceiling and its higher D&A, rather than holding 18% EBIT alongside implausibly high depreciation.

Servers/network accounting life moved from four to five years in 2026. The model must also test economic replacement at three/four/five years. Moving hardware from five to three years adds annual depreciation/replacement need equal to 13.33% of in-service hardware cost before salvage and falling unit prices; changing only D&A while keeping margin unchanged would manufacture cash flow. [Interim management discussion](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1513845/000110465926094844/nbis-20260812xex99d1.htm) · [Annual asset-life and cash-flow disclosures](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1513845/000110465926052948/nbis-20251231x20f.htm)

In 2027–29 the central scenario receives $7bn new annual advances but recognizes $1.8bn/$3.2bn/$5bn of prepaid revenue. Thereafter deferred revenue normalizes to three months of annual sales by 2034; its runoff is a cash use in explicit 2030–34 rows. The policy is already stable in 2035 and 2036, so no exceptional runoff remains in the last forecast year. No permanent advance windfall is assumed. The central peak is $61.19bn before customer-advance movements, $49.70bn with the specified advances and $69.99bn if no new advances arrive while the $8.8bn opening balance is serviced. These differences are genuine financing sensitivities, not alternative present debt balances.

Beyond 2029, D&A is explicitly 30% of sales, other operating WC 3% of sales increments, and physical growth investment is separated from replacement. Before-advance investment intensity converges to 1.403125 per current-year incremental sales dollar; normal advance growth reduces it to 1.153125. The (1 + 2.5% growth) timing factor makes this consistent with forward-funded NOPAT × growth / ROIC, rather than mixing current-year sales increments with a next-year funding convention. Final-year net investment is exactly NOPAT2036 × 2.5% / 12%.

### Executable terminal bridge: no hidden advance-runoff jump

Advances do not fully run off. The $22.5758bn year-end 2036 balance remains a performance obligation, equal to 25% of $90.3033bn revenue. Both 2035 and 2036 have normal positive advance growth, and every reduction in excess advances was already charged in explicit 2030–34 FCFF. Accelerating normalization into those years raises the central economic funding trough from the preliminary $37.87bn to $49.70bn; the correction is not free funding.

| Year | Ending advances | Net advance cash movement | Net investment after advances | Economic FCFF |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2033 | 25,342.9 | -1,986.5 | 16,580.5 | -7,025.1 |
| 2034 | 20,286.4 | -5,056.5 | 18,206.3 | -7,251.7 |
| 2035 | 22,025.2 | 1,738.8 | 7,553.0 | 4,340.6 |
| 2036 | 22,575.8 | 550.6 | 2,539.8 | 9,651.2 |
| 2037 terminal | 23,140.2 | 564.4 | 2,603.3 | 9,892.4 |

2037 economic FCFF is exactly 2.5% above 2036, replacing the preliminary approximately 239.5% discontinuity. Gross terminal capex is $30,868.2m, including $27,768.3m replacement/D&A, while core working capital rises $67.7m and advances rise $564.4m. These produce the required $2,603.3m **net** terminal investment; advances are not added to FCFF a second time.

Terminal value is $9,892.4444m / (15.5% - 2.5%) = $76,095.7264m at end-2036. Discount it using the same cumulative factor as the final explicit cash flow; at an end-2026 anchor its PV is $18,011.1078m. An October 17 valuation also applies the same remaining-2026 stub interval used for the explicit rows. No additional transition years or terminal one-time cash adjustment is required. All 10-year explicit FCFF remains discounted as cash flows in its actual forecast year.

For allowed maturity horizons of 10, 15 or 20 years, complete advance normalization by explicit year N−2, leaving the last two years on the stable balance policy. The selected case remains 10 years. The JSON selectedCentralProposals.NBIS.terminalTreatment supplies the executable formulas; terminalBridges contains the recomputed 2037 row and PV checks.

### Leases, energy and customer support

Keep rent/power in EBIT, or capitalize them and restate operating economics consistently. June commenced leases entail $235.2m 2027 payments. Uncommenced agreements total $12.054bn future undiscounted payments; dividing by the maximum 12-year term is roughly $1.00bn/year as a *scale illustration*, not a calendar forecast. Add the $541.8m 2027 fixed power minimum and existing rent and the visible annual scale is about $1.78bn, before other variable power/costs and any overlap. New sites may have very different commencement timing. Prepaid lease balances and new deposits also need a cash-timing bridge. Do not subtract the $12bn undiscounted sum as debt while still charging all rental expense in EBIT.

Secured customer contracts, prepayments and pledged GPUs can support financing; they do not remove repayment, refinancing or performance risk. Current private-investment carrying values are not immediate funding. A new issue that funds a negative FCFF year contributes cash and a debt/equity claim together; adding the proceeds as an asset without the claim overvalues equity, while deducting the FCFF deficit again as debt undervalues it.

## Selected central alternatives and implementation

For canonicalization, select AAOI central_explicit and NBIS company_build_central. These replace the legacy sales-to-capital reinvestment calculation with the explicit annual rows; they must not be layered on top of it. Both are analytical conditional bases, not disclosed budgets or confirmed financing. The JSON selectedCentralProposals block specifies field names and adapter requirements.

The June-to-December 2026 bridge remains separate from 2027–2036 FCFF. For an October 17 valuation it is not valid to treat all H2 spending as still future: estimate October cash from the June balance and intervening uses/financing, then discount only October 17–December 31 remaining FCFF. Do not add June cash plus known raises as current excess cash or charge July–October spending twice. The present envelope brackets current liquidity; it does not establish an exact October balance.

## Implementation implications

- Preserve the original proposals as diagnostic scenarios. Use explicit capital/prepayment/cash bridges for AAOI and NBIS operating values.
- Show the selected capital pathway beside its implied billable output, EBITDA/D&A hurdle and cumulative cash trough. These are conditional values, not probabilities or financing commitments.
- Start at the actual valuation date: include remaining 2026 cash flows, distinguish the FY2026 outlook anchor from trailing actual revenue, and reconcile financing once.
- Maintain both economic FCFF (SBC expensed) and cash liquidity (SBC added back, award withholding separately deducted); reflect dilution once.
- Model lease prepayments, rent and power in consistent locations. Do not turn operating commitments or backlog into additive debt/assets mechanically.
- For a practical default, AAOI's central explicit investment case is more coherent than its persistent 0.6–1.3 ramp S:C proxy. For NBIS, use an explicitly named owned-build case and a separately conditional paced/partner case, rather than presenting capital-light growth as already established.
- Missing current cash, exact supplier budgets and financing terms should widen valuation/funding intervals. They do not prevent computation of the conditional operating cash flows already specified.

The JSON includes reproducible annual schedules through 2036, original-source links, exact formulas and limitations. Its peak figures are sensitivity diagnostics, not a recommendation to trade or a capital-raising plan.

company-base-cases.name: Broadcom Inc.
company-base-cases.summary: Custom AI silicon and infrastructure software support growth and high profitability, with customer concentration and product-mix normalization.

rationale.growth: 35% is above FY2025 growth of 23.9% but far below the latest 86% quarter. Custom accelerators and networking justify the uplift; a large base and concentrated programs require a steep fade.
rationale.targetMargin: 45% is below 48.0% TTM GAAP EBIT margin. High software and semiconductor profitability persists, while lower-margin system mix and competition prevent extrapolating non-GAAP peak margins.
rationale.tax: 20% is a normalized operating-tax assumption. FY2025’s tax benefit and discrete restructuring/acquisition effects do not establish a sustainable long-term rate.
rationale.salesCapital: 2.0x means $0.50 of net investment per incremental $1 of revenue. Fabless design and software are efficient, but working capital, supply commitments and future investment are not zero because reported capex is low.
rationale.terminalROIC: 20% retains defensible IP and installed software advantages while reducing growth-period incremental returns substantially.
rationale.wacc: 10.0% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.3, 15% target debt and a 1.5-point debt spread reflect strong cash generation alongside concentrated semiconductor customers and acquisition leverage.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
rationale.otherClaims: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not evidence that no additional claims exist. Review acquisition debt, employee awards, contingent obligations and non-operating assets; no future acquisition is assumed to arrive without a capital cost.
rationale.otherAssets: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not a statement that all non-operating assets are absent or worthless. Review assets not already included in snapshot cash and avoid double counting.

company-base-cases.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
company-base-cases.summary: Normalize a memory scarcity boom before forecasting modest through-cycle growth; do not capitalize the peak EBIT margin for a decade.

rationale.growth: 8% is a through-cycle growth judgment on the already elevated FY2026 revenue base. HBM/content demand supports long-run expansion, but pricing and supply cycles prevent extrapolating 256% annual growth or near-term guidance.
rationale.targetMargin: 35% is a normalized mature EBIT margin. The base case also resets starting EBIT to 35% of reported revenue, so the model does not take ten years to fade from FY2026’s extraordinary 74.6% margin.
rationale.tax: 20% is a normalized operating tax above FY2026 accounting tax of 14.8%; tax incentives and geographical manufacturing mix remain uncertain.
rationale.salesCapital: 0.8x requires $1.25 of net reinvestment per extra $1 of sales. Fabs, advanced packaging and process transitions require capital across the cycle; the ratio is not gross capex divided by current revenue.
rationale.terminalROIC: 12% allows a modest technology/industry-structure advantage while avoiding a perpetual scarcity return on memory capacity.
rationale.wacc: 11.0% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.4, 10% target debt and a 1.5-point debt spread reflect cyclical memory pricing and capital intensity even after unusually strong current cash generation.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.0% nominal USD avoids granting a mature cyclical memory producer permanent above-economy growth.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
rationale.otherClaims: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not evidence that no additional claims exist. Review restricted cash, long-dated investments, customer prepayments, commitments and incentives before treating all cash as surplus or the equity bridge as complete.
rationale.otherAssets: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not a statement that all non-operating assets are absent or worthless. Review assets not already included in snapshot cash and avoid double counting.
rationale.normalization: Analyst through-cycle assumption: reset starting EBIT to 35% of reported FY2026 revenue instead of carrying the 74.6% scarcity-cycle margin through a slow ten-year fade. FY2025 EBIT margin was 26.1%; 35% assumes structural HBM benefits above that year. This is not a reported restatement and revenue is not normalized.

reportedAnchors.classification: reported or directly derived from reported current financials
reported results and explicitly labeled management outlook; not the base-case forecast
reportedAnchors.text: FY2026 revenue was $133.188bn and GAAP operating income $99.340bn, a 74.6% margin, versus a 26.1% FY2025 operating margin.

waccBuild.classification: analyst model estimate; only riskFreeUSD is an observed input
waccBuild.equityRiskPremiumClassification: chosen long-run assumption; January reference is 4.23%, not a current estimate
waccBuild.formula: Ke = Rf + assumed beta × chosen ERP + extra equity risk; WACC = Ke × (1 − debt weight) + assumed Kd × (1 − tax) × debt weight
waccBuild.limits: Not a live beta regression, bond yield, market-value capital structure or country-default estimate. Extra equity allowances can overlap with operating downside; stress both rather than treating precision as evidence.

bridgePolicy.note: Review restricted cash, long-dated investments, customer prepayments, commitments and incentives before treating all cash as surplus or the equity bridge as complete.

modelLimits: The 35% EBIT normalization is an analyst assumption, not a reported restatement; peak revenue itself is not normalized. The simple model cannot simulate a boom/bust sequence or replacement-capex spikes.
uncertainties: HBM demand versus DRAM/NAND supply additions and pricing reversals
Fab execution, node transitions, customer prepayments and incentive timing

modelSuitability.note: An internally checked conditional model, not proof that business assumptions will be realized.

normalization.adjustmentReason: Analyst through-cycle assumption: reset starting EBIT to 35% of reported FY2026 revenue instead of carrying the 74.6% scarcity-cycle margin through a slow ten-year fade. FY2025 EBIT margin was 26.1%; 35% assumes structural HBM benefits above that year. This is not a reported restatement and revenue is not normalized.
normalization.classification: analyst judgment; modifies model EBIT only, never reported facts

economicChecks.note: Operating math only. No cash/debt/claims/share bridge is asserted; hard gates remain. Terminal share above 100% means negative explicit-period present value, not a probability.

company-base-cases.name: NVIDIA CORP
company-base-cases.summary: AI infrastructure sustains exceptional expansion, followed by substantial growth and margin normalization as customers, competitors and the supply chain mature.

rationale.growth: 40% starts below Q2 year-over-year growth of 106% and produces about $424bn in first-year revenue from the $303bn TTM base. The lower rate limits a ten-year straight-line fade; it is not a transcription of near-term guidance.
rationale.targetMargin: 45% falls materially from 65.2% TTM. Software/ecosystem and system-level integration support a premium, but customer-designed chips, competition and scarcity normalization erode peak economics.
rationale.tax: 20% is above the company’s 16–18% FY2027 outlook, allowing tax benefits to normalize over a much longer horizon.
rationale.salesCapital: 2.0x assumes $0.50 of net reinvestment per added $1 of revenue. Fabless production helps, while inventory, receivables, supply commitments and broader infrastructure investments prevent growth from being capital-free.
rationale.terminalROIC: 25% deliberately retains a strong platform advantage but is far below the explicit margin/capital combination. This remains an optimistic moat assumption requiring stress tests.
rationale.wacc: 11.0% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.4, 3% target debt and a 1-point debt spread reflect high operating volatility and customer-capex concentration despite limited conventional leverage.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
rationale.otherClaims: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not evidence that no additional claims exist. Review strategic investments, commitments, convertible instruments and awards; gross capex alone does not measure economic reinvestment.
rationale.otherAssets: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not a statement that all non-operating assets are absent or worthless. Review assets not already included in snapshot cash and avoid double counting.

reportedAnchors.classification: reported or directly derived from reported current financials
reported results and explicitly labeled management outlook; not the base-case forecast
reportedAnchors.text: Fiscal Q2 2027 revenue was $96.2bn, up 106%; Q3 revenue guidance was $108bn ±2%, with no China Data Center compute revenue assumed.

waccBuild.classification: analyst model estimate; only riskFreeUSD is an observed input
waccBuild.equityRiskPremiumClassification: chosen long-run assumption; January reference is 4.23%, not a current estimate
waccBuild.formula: Ke = Rf + assumed beta × chosen ERP + extra equity risk; WACC = Ke × (1 − debt weight) + assumed Kd × (1 − tax) × debt weight
waccBuild.limits: Not a live beta regression, bond yield, market-value capital structure or country-default estimate. Extra equity allowances can overlap with operating downside; stress both rather than treating precision as evidence.

bridgePolicy.note: Review strategic investments, commitments, convertible instruments and awards; gross capex alone does not measure economic reinvestment.

modelLimits: 40% fading over ten years still implies roughly 6.5x revenue. A multistage ramp followed by faster early deceleration may be more realistic than this deliberately simplified curve.
uncertainties: AI customers’ sustainable returns, custom accelerators and export restrictions
Supply availability, product transitions and investment/financing commitments

modelSuitability.note: An internally checked conditional model, not proof that business assumptions will be realized.

economicChecks.note: Operating math only. No cash/debt/claims/share bridge is asserted; hard gates remain. Terminal share above 100% means negative explicit-period present value, not a probability.

company-base-cases.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited
company-base-cases.summary: Leading-edge foundry and packaging scale support growth, with eventual margin normalization and explicit TWD-currency assumptions.

rationale.growth: 22% is below recent annual growth and Q3’s 50.9% TWD growth. Advanced nodes and AI demand support expansion; scale, cyclicality and currency effects require a decline toward mature growth.
rationale.targetMargin: 45% is below the 58.0% TTM operating margin and near earlier-cycle levels. Technology leadership persists, while overseas-fab costs, node transitions and pricing normalize peak profitability.
rationale.tax: 20% is a normalized rate above FY2025’s 17.0% accounting tax, allowing tax incentives and geographic production mix to normalize.
rationale.salesCapital: 0.9x means $1.11 of net reinvestment per additional TWD1 of sales. Fabs and advanced packaging are capital-intensive; depreciation is already inside EBIT and this ratio represents investment net of that economic consumption.
rationale.terminalROIC: 18% assumes lasting process/yield advantages with much lower returns than the explicit margin/capital combination. It does not eliminate geopolitical tail risk.
rationale.wacc: 10.0% nominal TWD is a rounded model estimate. A USD risk build uses beta 1.2, 10% target debt, a 1.5-point debt spread and 1.5-point extra equity risk. Assumed USD 2.5% versus TWD 1.5% inflation converts this to about 10.2% nominal TWD, rounded to 10%.
rationale.terminalGrowth: 2.0% nominal TWD combines an assumed 1.5% long-run inflation rate with modest real expansion; it is not USD ADR growth.
rationale.years: 10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
rationale.otherClaims: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not evidence that no additional claims exist. Preserve the existing hard gate for reporting currency, FX and five-ordinary-shares-per-ADR mapping; review minority interests and lease liabilities separately.
rationale.otherAssets: 0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not a statement that all non-operating assets are absent or worthless. Review assets not already included in snapshot cash and avoid double counting.

reportedAnchors.classification: reported or directly derived from reported current financials
reported results and explicitly labeled management outlook; not the base-case forecast
reportedAnchors.text: Q3 2026 TWD revenue grew 50.9% and operating margin was 58.7%; the issuer’s Q4 operating-margin outlook was 56.5–58.5%.

waccBuild.classification: analyst model estimate; only riskFreeUSD is an observed input
waccBuild.equityRiskPremiumClassification: chosen long-run assumption; January reference is 4.23%, not a current estimate
waccBuild.formula: Ke = Rf + assumed beta × chosen ERP + extra equity risk; WACC = Ke × (1 − debt weight) + assumed Kd × (1 − tax) × debt weight
waccBuild.limits: Not a live beta regression, bond yield, market-value capital structure or country-default estimate. Extra equity allowances can overlap with operating downside; stress both rather than treating precision as evidence.

currencyConversion.formula: (1 + USD WACC) × (1 + assumed TWD inflation) / (1 + assumed USD inflation) − 1
currencyConversion.classification: analyst inflation/currency judgment, not observed inflation or current FX

bridgePolicy.note: Preserve the existing hard gate for reporting currency, FX and five-ordinary-shares-per-ADR mapping; review minority interests and lease liabilities separately.

modelLimits: Valuation remains withheld: native TWD financials and ordinary shares cannot be compared directly with a USD ADR. The inflation conversion is an analyst assumption, not a quoted TWD yield or a verified ADR mapping.
uncertainties: Advanced-node demand, overseas-fab economics and capacity utilization
Geopolitical interruption, energy/water supply and exchange rates
